hadiths.text: Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al -A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  who said: A man said: O Apostle of Allah, will a man be held accountable for what he did in the Jahiliyyah? He said: “Whoever does good in Islam will not be held accountable for what he did in the Jahiliyyah, and whoever does evil in Islam will be held accountable for the first and the last.”

Al-Walid ibn al-Nadr al-Ramli informed us, on the authority of Masarrah ibn Ma’bad from Banu al-Harith ibn Abi al -Haram from Lakhm, on the authority of al -Wadhin, that a man came to the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) and said: O Apostle of Allah, we were people of ignorance and idol worship, so we used to kill children, and I had a daughter of mine. When she responded, and she was… She was pleased with my supplication when I called her. So, I called her one day, and she followed me. I passed by until I came to a well of my family, not far away. I took her by the hand 6 and threw her back into the well. The last thing I saw of her was that she said: O my father! O my father! The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  wept until his eyes stopped shedding tears. A man from among the companions of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said to him: You have made the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  sad. He said to him: Stop, for he is asking about what is worrying him. Then he said to him: Repeat your story to me. So, he repeated it, and he wept until  his tears stopped from his eyes and dripped onto his beard. Then he said to him: “Indeed, Allah has removed from the ignorance what they did, so resume your work.”

Harun ibn Mu’awiyah informed us, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Sulayman al-Mu’addib, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: My master told me: “His family sent with him a cup containing butter and milk to their Gods (idols). He said: So, he prevented me from eating butter for fear of them. He said: Then a dog came and ate the butter and drank the milk, then he urinated on the idol, which was Usaf.” And Na’ila, Harun said: When a man traveled in the pre-Islamic era, he would carry four stones with him: three for his pot, th e fourth he would worship, raise his dog, and kill his son.

Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, Rayhan, he is the son of Saeed al -Sami narrated to us, Abbad, he is the son of Mansour narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, he said: “In the pre-Islamic era, if we found a beautiful stone, we would worship it, and  if we did not find a stone, we would gather a pile of sand, then we would bring the pure camel and milk it on the pile of sand until…” We narrate it, then we worship that hill as long as we stay in that place.” Abu Muhammad al-Safi said: “The one with many milks.”

Al-Hasan ibn al-Rabi’ informed us, Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, on the authority of al -A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, who said: Ka’b (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه ) said: We find it written: “Muhammad is the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) He is neither rude nor harsh, nor a loudmouth in the markets, and he does not repay evil for evil, but he pardons and forgives. His nation is the praisers, who glorify Allah upon Every Najd, and they praise Him in every position, and they tighten their belts on their middles, and they perform ablution on their ends, their caller calls in the sky, their ranks in battle, and their ranks in prayer are equal, they have a buzzing at night like the buzzing of bees, his birthplace is in Makka, his migration is i n Madina, and his kingdom is in Ash-Sham.

Abdullah bin Salih narrated to us, Al-Layth narrated to me, Khalid - he is Ibn Yazid - narrated to me, on the authority of Saeed - he is Ibn Abi Hilal - on the authority of Hilal bin Usamah - on the authority of Ata bin Yasar - on the authority of Ibn Sala m (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  that he used to say: “We find the description of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  as: We have sent you as a witness, a bringer of good tidings, a warner, and a protection. To the unlettered, you are My servant and My Apostle. I have named him Al -Mutawakkil. He is not rude, nor harsh, nor loud in the markets. He does not repay evil with the like of it, but he pardons and overlooks. And I will not take him until he establishes the crooked religion by bearing witness that there is no Allah but Allah. We open through him blind eyes, deaf ears, and sealed hearts.” He said: Ata’ bin Yasar: Abu Waqid Al-Laythi informed me that he heard Ka’b say the same as what Ibn Salam said.

Zayd ibn Awf told us: Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Abd al -Malik ibn Umair, on the authority of Dhakwan Abu Salih, on the authority of Ka’b  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) In the first line: 8 Muhammad (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  is the Apostle of Allah, My chosen servant, neither rude nor harsh, nor loud in the markets, nor does He repay evil with evil, but He pardons and forgives. His birthplace is in Makka. And his migration to Madina, and his kingdom in Ash -Sham, and in the second line: Muhammad (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  is the Apostle of Allah, his nation is the praisers, they praise Allah in prosperity and adversity, they praise Allah in every position, and they glorify Him on every honor, the shepherds of the sun, they pray the prayer whe n its time comes even if they are on top of a dustbin, and they wrap their waists around their waists, and they perform ablution. Their limbs and their voices at night in the sky are like the voices of bees.

Mujahid ibn Musa informed us, Ma’n ibn ‘Isa told us, Mu’awiyah ibn Salih told us, on the authority of Abu Farwah, on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  that he asked Ka’b al -Ahbar (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)How do you find the description of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) in the Torah? Ka’b said: “We find him Muhammad ibn Abdullah, born in Makka, and migrating to Tabah, His kingdom will be in Ash-Sham. He will not be obscene, nor will he make noise in the markets. He will not repay evil for evil but will pardon and forgive. His nation will be the praisers. They will praise Allah in every good and bad time, and they will glorify Allah in every Najd. They will wash their extremities and wear their waistbands. They will line up in their prayers as they line up in their battles . Their buzzing in their mosques is like the buzzing of bees. Their caller is heard in the sky.

Haywah ibn Shurayh informed us, Baqiyah ibn al -Walid al-Tamimi informed us, Bahir ibn Sa`d informed us, on the authority of Khalid ibn Ma`dan, on the authority of Jubayr ibn Nufayr al - Hadrami (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)that the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: “An Apostle has come to you who is neither weak nor lazy, to revive the hearts that are covered, open the eyes of the blind, and make the hearing of the tongues heard by the deaf ears, and establishes the crooked, Sunnah, until it is said: There is no Allah but Allah alone. 9

Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Hizami told us, Ishaq ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Qays, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Aamir, who said: There was a man from the companions of the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) who had a need from him, so he walked with him until he entered. He said: One of his feet was in the house and the other was outside as if he was talking in private, so he turned and said: “Do you know who I was speaking to? This is an angel whom I have n ever seen before this day. He asked permission of his Lord to greet me. He said: Indeed, We have given you, or sent down, t he Qur’an as a detailed explanation, and tranquility as patience, and the Criterion as a connection.

Mujahid ibn Musa informed us, Rayhan, he is Ibn Saeed, told us, Abbad, he is Ibn Mansour, told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Atiyyah, that he heard Rabi’ah al-Jurashi (رضئ  اللہ تعالی عنه)  say: The Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) was visited and it was said to him: Let your eyes sleep, let your ears hear, and let your heart understand. He said: “So my eyes slept, and my ears heard.” And my heart understood,” he said: “It was said to me: A master built a house, made a banquet, and sent an inviter. Whoever answered the inviter entered the house, ate from the banquet, and the master was pleased with him. Whoever did not answer the inviter did not enter the house, did not eat from the banquet, and the master was angry with him.” He said: “So Allah is the Master, Muhammad (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  is the inviter, the house is Islam, and the banquet is heaven.

Al-Hasan bin Ali (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) informed us, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Ja`far bin Maymun al-Tamimi, on the authority of Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, that the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) went out to al-Batha’, and with him was Ibn Mas`ud  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)He made him sit down and drew a line over him, then he said: “Do not move, for men will come to you, so do not speak to them, for they will not speak to you.” The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) went wherever he wanted, then they would reach the line and not go beyond it, then they would return to the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  until at the end of the night he came to me and rested his head on my thigh, and when he slept, he would blow in his sleep, blowing. While the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  was resting his head on my thigh, sleeping, someone came to me. Men like camels, wearing white garments. Allah knows best what beauty they have. A group of them sat at his head and a group at his feet. They said among themselves: We have never seen a servant who has been given what this Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  has been given. His eyes are sleeping, and his heart is awake. Give him an example: a master. He built a palace, then held a banquet and invited the people to his food and drink. Then they went up, and the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) woke up at that time and said: “Do you know who these are?” I said: “Allah and His Apostle (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  know best.” He said: “They are the angels.” He said: “Do you know what the example they gave is?” “I said: Allah and His Apostle (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) know best.” He said: “The Most Gracious built Paradise and called His servants to it. Whoever answered Him, He entered His Paradise, and whoever did not answer Him, He punished and tormented him.”

Nu`aym ibn Hammad informed us, Baqiyah told us, on the authority of Baheer, on the authority of Khalid ibn Ma`dan, on the authority of `Abd al -Rahman ibn `Amr al-Sulami, on the authority 11 of `Utbah ibn `Abd al-Sulami, that he told them, and he was one of the companions of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)A man said to the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)How did your affair begin, O Apostle of Allah? He said: “My foster mother was from Banu Sa`d ibn Bakr. I and her son set out with our cattle, and we did not take any provisions with us. I said: ‘O my brother, go and bring us provisions from our mother.’ So, my brother set out and I stayed with the cattle. Then two white birds came, looking like eagles. One of them said to his companion: ‘Is it him?’ The other said: ‘He is the one.’ Yes, so they came running towards me, and they seized me, and they laid me on my back, and they split open my belly, and they took out my heart, and they split it open, and they took out from it two black clots. One of them said to his companion: Bring me some icy water, and he washed my insides with it. Then he said: Bring me some cold water, and he washed my heart with it. Then he said:  Bring me a knife and put it in my heart. Then one of them said to his companion: “Put him on a scale and put a thousand of his nation on the other scale.” The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: “When I look at the thousand above me, I fear that some of them will fall on me.” He said: “If his nation were weighed against him, it would lean toward him.” “With them, then they went away and left me.” The Apostle of Allah (صلى علیه و آله وسلم) said: “I was very afraid, then I went to my mother and told her what I had encountered. She was afraid that something bad might have happened to me, so she said: I seek refuge in Allah from you. So, she saddled a camel of hers, put me on the saddle, and rode behind me until we reached my mother. She said: I have fulfilled my trust.” And my conscience, and I told her what I had encountered, but that did not frighten her, and she said: When something c ame out of me, I saw, meaning: a light from which the palaces of Ash-Sham were illuminated.

Abdullah bin Imran informed us, Abu Dawud told us, Ja`far bin Uthman Al -Qurashi told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Urwah bin Az-Zubayr, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Dharr Al-Ghifari (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)who said: I said: O Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)how did you know that you were a prophet until you were certain? He said: “O Abu Dharr, two angels came to me while I was in some of the plains of Makka, and one of them fell on the earth, and the other was between the sky and the earth, so one of them said to his companion: Is it him? He said: Yes. He said: Weigh him with a man, so I was weighed with him and weighed him. Then he said: Weigh him with ten, so I was weighed with them a nd outweighed them. Then he said: Weigh him with a hundred, so I weighed with them and outweighed them. Then he said: Weigh him with a thousand, so I weighed with them and outweighed them. It is as if I see them falling on me because of the lightness of the scale. He said: Then one of them said to his companion: If you weighed him with his nation, he would outweigh them. 12

Ismail bin Khalil told us, Ali bin Mushir told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, who said: The Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) used to call out to them: “O people, I am only a mercy sent as a gift.”

Muhammad ibn Tarif informed us, Muhammad ibn Fadil told us, Abu Hayyan told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Umar  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  who said: We were with the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  on a journey, and a Bedouin approached. When he came close to him, the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said to him: “Where are you going?” He said: “To my family.” He said: “Would you like “Good?” He said: “What is it?” He said: “You testify that there is no Allah but Allah alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) is His servant and Apostle.” He said: “And who will testify to what you say?” He said: “This is As-Salama.” The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  called her while she was on the bank of the valley, and she came forward, scratching the ground, until she stood b efore him. He called her to witness three times. She testified three times that it was as he said, then she returned to her place of origin, and the Bedouin returned to his people and said: If they follow me, I will bring them to you, and if not, I will return and be with you.

Ubaydullah bin Musa informed us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abdul Malik, on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: I went out with the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) on a journey, and he would not relieve himself until he was hidden and not seen. We stopped in a deserted area of land in which there were no trees or landmarks. He said: “O Jabir, put water in your vessel, then…” “Let us go,” he said. “So , we went until we could not be seen. Then he came to two trees, between which there were four cubits. He said: ‘O Jabir, go to this tree and say: “The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  says to y ou: ‘Catch up with your companion so that I may sit behind you.’ So, she returned to it, and the Apostle of Allah (صلى علیه و آله وسلم) sat behind them. Then they returned to their place. So, we rode with the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)and the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) was between us, as if birds were shading us. Then a woman with her child came to him and said: O Apostle of Allah, this son of mine is seized by the devil three times every day. He said: So, he took the child and put him between him and the front of the saddle, then he said: “Get lost, enemy of Allah. I am…” The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: “Get lost, enemy of Allah! I am the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) He then handed him over to her. When we had finished our journey, we passed by that place and the woman came to us with her child and two rams that she was herding. She said: “O Apostle of Allah, accept my gift from me, for by the One Who sent you with the truth, it has not returned to him.” Then he said: “Take one of them and return the other to her.” He said: Then we walked and the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه وآله وسلم)  was among us as if birds were shading us. Then a camel called out until it was between two rows and fell down in prostration. The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  sat down and said to the people: “Who is the owner of the camel?” “Then some young men from the Ansar came and said: ‘It is ours, O Apostle of Allah.’ He said: ‘What is the matter with it?’ They said: ‘We have been waiting for it for twenty years and it had some fat on it, so we wanted to slaughter it and divide it among our young men, but it escaped from us.’ He said: ‘Sell it to me.’ They said: ‘No, it is yours, O Apostle of Allah.’ He said: ‘But if not, then treat it well until His time comes.” The Muslims then said: “O Apostle of Allah, we are more deserving of prostration to you than the animals.” He said: “It is not appropriate for anything to prostrate to anything, even if that were the case, women would be to their husbands.”

Ya`la narrated to us, Al-Ajlah narrated to us, on the authority of Ad-Dhayyal ibn Harmalah, on the authority of Jabir ibn `Abdullah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  who said: We came with the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) until we were brought to a wall in Banu An-Najjar, and there was a camel in it, and no one entered the wall without it attacking him. They mentioned that to the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) so he came to it. So, he called him, and he came, placing his cloak on the ground until he knelt down in front of him. Then he said, “Bring me a halter.” So, he put the halter on him and gave him to his companion. Then he turned and said, “There is no one between the heaven and the earth who does not know that I a m the Apostle of Allah, except the disobedient jinn and mankind.”

Muhammad ibn Sa`id narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr al-`Abdi informed us, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Tahman, on the authority of Simaak, on the authority of Jabir ibn Samurah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: “I know a stone in Makka that used to greet me before I was sent as aPprophet. I know it now.”

Farwah narrated to us, Al -Walid bin Abi Thawr Al-Hamdani narrated to us, on the authority of Ismail Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abbad Abi Yazid, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “We were with the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) in Makka, and we went out with him to some of its regions. We passed between the mountains and trees, and we did not pass by a tree or a mountain except that he said: Peace be upon you, O Apostle of Allah (السَّلََمُ   عَلَیْكَ   يَا 15

Muhammad ibn Yusuf told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Shimr ibn Atiyah, on the authority of a man from Muzaynah or Juhaynah, who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) prayed the dawn prayer, and there he saw nearly a hundred wolves, the wolves’ delegations, sitting down. So, the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said to them: “Do you give them something from Your food and you feel safe about everything else?” So, they complained to the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  about the need. He said: “Then inform them.” He said: So, they informed them and they went out and they were howling.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us, Abu Mu’awiyah informed us, Al -A’mash informed us, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  who said: Jibreel (علیه  السلَم)  came to the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  while he was sitting sad, and his face was covered in blood because of the actions of the people of Makka from Quraysh. Jibreel (علیه  السلَم)  said: O Apostle of Allah, is it you like me to show you a sign? He said: Yes. Then he looked at a tree behind him and said: Call upon it. So, he called upon it and it came and stood in front of him. Then he said: Order it to go back. So, he ordered it, and it went back. Then the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: “Enough for me, enough for me.”

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim told us, Jarir and Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas (رضئتعالی عنه)  who said: A man from Banu Amir came to the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  and the Apostle of Allah (صلى علیه و آله وسلم) said: “Shall I not show you a sign?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “Then go and call that 16 palm tree.” So, he called her, and she came jumping in front of him. He said: Tell her to go back. The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  said to her: “Go back.” So, she went back until she returned to her place. Then he said: O Banu Amir, I have never seen a man more ecstatic than he is today.

Ismail bin Ibrahim told us, Shuaib bin Safwan told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Abu Al-Duha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: The Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) called Bilal (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)and asked Bilal for water, then he came and said: No, by Allah, I did not find any water. The Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  said: “Is there a water skin?” So, he brought him a water skin. He spread his hands in it, and a spring gushed forth from under his hands. He said: Ibn Mas`ud  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه ) was drinking, and others were performing ablution.

Abu al-Numan informed us, Abu Awanah told us, on the authority of al-Aswad ibn Qays, on the authority of Nubayh al-Anazi, who said: Jabir ibn Abdullah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) said: We went on a military expedition or traveled with the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) and we were on that day about two hundred and ten of us. Then the time for prayer came, so the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: "Is there any purification water among the people?” Then a man came running, carrying a vessel containing some water, and there was no other water among the people. “The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  poured it into a cup, then performed ablution an d performed it well, then he left and left the cup.” The people got on that cup and said: “Wipe yourselves, wipe yourselves.” Then the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  said: “On Your wudu parts, when he heard them say that, then the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  put his hand in the water and the cup, and said: “In the name of Allah,” then he said: “Perform ablution completely,” and by the One Who has tested me with my sight, I saw the springs, the springs of 17 water coming out from between his fingers, and he did not raise them until they had all performed ablution.

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi and Sa`id ibn al-Rabi` told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of `Amr ibn Murrah and Husayn, who heard Salim ibn Abi al -Ja`d say: I heard Jabir ibn `Abdullah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) say: We were afflicted with thirst and we cried out in agony, so we came to the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  and he put his hand in a bowl. It began to bubble up like springs through his fingers, and he said: “Mention the name of Allah.” So, we drank until it was enough for us and it was sufficient for us. In the hadith of Amr ibn Murrah: So, we said to Jabir (رضئ تعالی عنه)How many were you? He said: We were one thousand and five hundred, and if we had been one hundred thousand, it would have been sufficient for us.

Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Raqashi informed us, Ja`far ibn Sulayman informed us, al -Ja`d Abu Uthman informed us, Anas ibn Malik (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) informed us, Jabir ibn Abdullah ((رضئ  اللہ تعالی  عنه)  informed us, he said: The companions of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم ) complained to the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  of thirst, so he called for a bowl and poured water into it. And the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) put his hand in it. He said: So, I began to look at the water springing forth from between the fingers of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) and the people were drawing water until all the people had drawn water.

Ubaydullah bin Musa informed us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: Abdullah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) heard of an earthquake, so he said: We, the companions of Muhammad (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) used to consider the signs as a blessing, and you consider them as a warning. While we were with the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) and there was no one with us, the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: “Ask someone who has extra water.” So, some water was brought to him, he poured it into the vessel, then he put his hand in it, and the water started to flow out from between his fingers. Then he said: “Come to the blessed purification, and the blessing is from Allah the Most High. ” So, we drank, and Abdullah  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  said: We used to hear the food glorifying Allah while it was being eaten.

Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Numayr told us, Abu al-Jawab told us, on the authority of Ammar ibn Ruzaiq, on the authority of al -A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: The earth was shaken during the time of Abdullah, and he was informed of that, so he said: We, the companions of Muhammad (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)saw the signs as blessings, and you see them as a warning . While we were with the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) on a journey, the time for prayer came and we had only a little water with us. So, the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) called for water in a dish, and put his hand in it, and the water began to gush out from between his fingers.” Then he called out, “Come to ablution, and the blessing is from Allah.” He said: So , the people came. So, they performed ablution, and I had no concern except for what I would put in my stomach, because of his saying: “And the blessing is from Allah.” So, I told Salim bin Abi al-Ja`d about it, and he said: They were fifteen hundred people.

Uthman ibn Umar informed us, Muadh ibn Al -Ala informed us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه ) that the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم ) was delivering a sermon in front of a tree trunk. When he took the pulpit, the tree trunk yearned until he reached it, so he touched it. 19

Muhammad ibn Humayd informed us, Tamim ibn Abd al-Mumin informed us, Salih ibn Hayyan informed us, Ibn Buraydah informed me, on the authority of his father, who said: When the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) delivered a sermon, he would stand up and prolong his standing, and it was difficult for him to stand. So, a palm trunk was brought, dug for it, and it was made to stand beside it for the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) Whenever the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  delivered a sermon and stood for a long time on it, he would lean on it. A man who had come to Madinah saw him standing next to that trunk, so he said to the people next to him: If I knew that Muhammad (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  would praise me for something that would be kind to him, I would make a place for him to sit on. If he wishes, He sat as long as he wanted, and if he wanted, he could stand. News of that reached the Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  so he said: “Bring him to me.” So, they brought him to him, and he ordered him to make for him these three steps, or the four that are now on the pulpit of Madinah. The Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  found comfort in that. So, when the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  left the trunk and went to this one, which was made for him. The trunk swayed and moaned like a she -camel when the Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  left it. Ibn Buraydah said, on the authority of his father, that when the Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آلهوسلم)  heard the moaning of the trunk, he returned to it, placed his hand on it, and said: “Choose that I plant you in the place where you were, so that you will be as you were, and if you wish, I will plant you in Paradise.” So, you drink from its rivers and springs, and your plant grows well, and it bears fruit, and the friends of Allah eat from your fruit and your palm trees. He said that he heard the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) say to him: “Yes, I did it twice.” The Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) was asked, and he said: “He chose that I plant it in Paradise.”

Muhammad ibn Katheer informed us on the authority of Sulayman ibn Katheer, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed ibn al -Musayyib, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah al- Ansari (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) used to stand by a tree trunk before the pulpit was made. When the pulpit was made, the tree trunk moaned so much that we heard its moaning. The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  put his hand on it and he calmed down.

Muhammad ibn Katheer narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Katheer narrated to us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Saeed, on the authority of Hafs ibn Ubaydullah, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “The Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) was delivering the sermon facing a piece of wood. When the pulpit was made and the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) sat on it.  It moaned like a young camel until he put down.” The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) put his hand on it and it calmed down.

Farwah told us, Yahya bin Zakariya told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Kurayb, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah  (رضئ تعالی عنه) who said: “The wood moaned like a young camel.”

Zakariya ibn Adi informed us, on the authority of Ubayd Allah ibn Amr, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, on the authority of Tufail ibn Ubayy ibn Ka’b, on the authority of his father, who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) used to pray facing a tree trunk and deliver the sermon towards it when the mosque was like a hut. A man from among his companions said to him: Shall we not make a pulpit for you so that you can stand? On it the people see you on Friday and hear your sermon? He said: “Yes.” So , the three steps were made for him, which are the ones on the pulpit. When the pulpit was made and placed in the place where the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلمhad placed it, he said: When the Apostle of Allah (صلى علیه و آله وسلمcame wanting the pulpit, he passed by it, and when he passed it, he fell down. The trunk was broken and split, so the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) returned to it and wiped it with his hand until it calmed down, then he returned to the pulpit. He said: Whenever he prayed, he prayed towards it. When the mosque was reconstructed, Ubayy ibn Ka`b (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) took that trunk and it remained with it until it decayed and was eaten by termites and became dust.

Abdullah bin Saeed narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of Abu al-Wadak, on the authority of Abu Saeed (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  was delivering a sermon while leaning on a tree trunk. A Roman man came to him and said: Shall I make you a pulpit from which you can deliver the sermon? So, he made for him this pulpit which you see. He said: When he stood on it, the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) was delivering a sermon. The trunk yearned like a she-camel yearns for her young. The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) came down to it, hugged it close to him and it calmed down. Then he ordered that a grave be dug for it and that it be buried.

Muslim ibn Ibrahim told us, Al -Sa`q told us, he said: I heard Al -Hasan say: When the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) arrived in Madinah, he would lean his back against a piece of wood and talk to the people. They gathered around him in large numbers, so the Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) wanted to make them hear him, so he said: “Build something for me to stand on.” They said: “How, O Prophet of Allah? He said: “A trellis like the trellis of Musa (علیه السلَم) When they built it for 22 him, Al-Hasan said: “By Allah, the wood moaned.” Al -Hasan said: “Glory be to Allah! Are the hearts of people who listen, sought?” Abu Muhammad said: “He means this.”

Al-Hajjaj ibn Minhal informed us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Ammar ibn Abi Ammar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) that the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) used to deliver the sermon facing a tree trunk before he had the pulpit built. When he built the pulpit and moved towards it, the tree trunk moaned, so he embraced it, and it calmed down. He said, “If I had not embraced it, it would have moaned until the Day of Resurrection,” Al-Hajjaj bin Minhal informed us, Hammad informed us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) something similar.

Abdullah bin Yazid told us, Al-Mas’udi told us, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Sahl bin Sa’d  (رضئتعالی عنه)  who said: The wood that he used to stand by , yearned so the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) went to it and placed his hand on it, and it calmed down.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Khalaf informed us, Umar ibn Yunus informed us, Ikrimah ibn Ammar informed us, Ishaq ibn Abi Talhah informed us, Anas ibn Malik (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) informed us that the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) used to stand on Friday, lean his back against a tree trunk erected in the mosque and deliver a sermon to the people. Then a man came to him. Roman, he 23 said: Shall I not make you something for you to sit on as if you were standing? So, he made a pulpit for him with two steps, and he would sit on the third. When the Prophet of Allah  (صلى علیه و آله وسلم)  sat on that pulpit, the trunk of the tree moaned like the mooing of a bull until the mosque shook with grief. So the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) came down from the pulpit to him, and he embraced him while he was moaning. When the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) embraced him, Allahs Apostle (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  calmed down, then said: "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, if I had not stuck to him, he would have remained like this until the Day of Resurrection, grieving for the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  ".So, the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) ordered him to be buried.

Abdullah bin Omar bin Abaan informed us, Abdul Rahman bin Muhammad Al-Muharibi told us, on the authority of Abdul Wahid bin Ayman Al-Makki, on the authority of his father, who said: I said to Jabir bin Abdullah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) tell me about a hadith from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) that you heard from him and that I may narrate from you. Jabir (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) said: We were with the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  on the day of the Battle of the Trench, we were digging it. We remained for three days without eating food, nor were we able to do so. Then a mound appeared in the trench, so I came to the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم), and said: O Apostle of Allah, this is a mound that has appeared in the trench, so we sprinkled water on it. Then the Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  stood up. He took the pickaxe, or the spade, then he mentioned the name of Allah three times, then he struck it and it became a pile of sand. When I saw that from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  I said: O Apostle of Allah, give 24 me permission. He said: So, he gave me permission, so I came to my wife and said: May your mother be bereaved of you, I have seen from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) something that I cannot bear. On it, do you have anything? She said: I have a Saa of barley and a young goat. He said: We ground the barley, slaughtered the young goats, skinned them, put them in the pot and kneaded the barley. He said: Then he said: I we nt back to the Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  and stayed for an hour, then I asked his permission a second time and he gave me permission, so I came, and the dough had become ready. So, I ordered her to bake bread and put the pot on the stove. Abu Abd al-Rahman said: It is the stove, but like this. He said: Then I came to the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) and said: We have food for us, so if you see fit to stand with me, you and a man or two men with you, he said: “And how much is it?” “I said: A Sa’ of barley and a young goat. He said: ‘Go back to your family and tell h er not to remove the pot from the fireplace and not to take the bread out of the oven until I come.’ Then he said to the people: ‘Go to Jabir’s (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  house.’ I felt shy with a shyness that only Allah knows, so I said to my wife: ‘May your mother be bereaved of you, the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) has come to you. He (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  said to all his companions: Did the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  ask you: How much is the food? I said: Yes. She said: Allah and His Apostle know best. I have informed him of what we had. He said: So, some of what I had felt went away, and I said: You have spoken the truth. Then the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) came and entered, then he said to his companions: “No. They pressed themselves together, then he knelt on the oven and on the pot. He said: So, we took bread from the oven and took meat from the pot, and we mixed it and scooped it for them. The Prophet (صلى  اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  said: “Let seven or eight sit on the plate.” When they had eaten, we would uncover the oven and uncover the pot, and there they were. We continued to do that every time we opened the oven and uncovered the pot, we found them fuller than they had been until all the Muslims were full, and there was some food left. Then the Apostle of Allah (صلى علیه و آله وسلم) said to us: “The people have been afflicted with famine, so eat and feed others.” So, we continued to eat that day. And we feed. He said: And he informed me that they were eight hundred, or he said: three hundred. Ayman said: I do not know which of them he said.

Zakariya ibn Adi informed us, Ubaydullah ibn Amr informed us, on the authority of Abd al-Malik ibn Umair, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  who said: Abu Talhah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  ordered Umm Sulaym (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنہا) to make food for the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  to eat from. He said: Then Abu Talhah sent me to the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) so I came to him and said: Abu Talha 25 sent me to you. He said to the people: “Get up.” So, he set out and the people set out with him. Abu Talha said: O Apostle of Allah, did you only make food for yourself specifically? He said: “No problem, go.” He said: So, he set out and the people set out. He said: So, the food was brought, “So he placed the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) put his hand on it and said Bismillah over it, then he said: “Give permission to ten.” He said: So, he gave them permission and said: “Eat in the name of Allah.” So, they ate until they were full, then they stood up. “Then he put his hand on it as he had done the first time and said Bismillah over it.” Then he said: “Give permission to ten.” So, he gave them permission and said: “Eat, in the name of Allah.” So, they ate until They were full, then they stood up until he did that with eighty men. He said: “The Apostle of Allah (صلى علیه و آله وسلم) and the people of the house ate and left some leftovers.”

Muslim ibn Ibrahim informed us, Aban - he is Al-Attar - told us, Qatada told us, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Ubayd  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) that he cooked a pot for the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  and he said to him: “Give me the forearm,” and he liked the forearm, so he gave him the forearm, then he said: “Give me the forearm,” so he gave him a forearm, then he said: “Give me the forearm.” The arm,” so I said: “O Prophet of Allah, how many arms does a sheep have?” He said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if you had kept quiet, you would have been given as many arms as I have asked for.”

Abu al-Numan informed us, Abu Awanah told us, on the authority of al-Aswad, on the authority of Nubayh al -Anazi, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) went out to the polytheists to fight them, and Abu Abdullah said: O Jabir, it does not matter to you that you are in the presence of the people of Madina until you know what will happen to our situation, for I... By Allah, if I had not left daughters after me, I would have loved for her to be killed before me. He said: While I was in the audience, my aunt brought my father and my uncle to bury them in our graveyard. A man came calling out, “The Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) commands you to return the dead and bury them in their beds where they were killed.” So we returned them and buried them in their resting place where they were killed: While I was in the caliphate of Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) a man came to me and said: O Jabir ibn Abdullah, your father’s body was stirred up by the workers of Muawiyah, so he appeared, and a group of them went out, so I went to him and found him in the same position in which I had buried him, nothing had changed except what had not left the dead man. He said: So I hid him, and my father left him a debt of dates, and some of his creditors became very angry with me in the litigation, so I came to the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  and said: O Apostle of Allah, my father was afflicted on such and such a day, and he left him a debt of da tes, and some of his creditors became very angry with me in the pursuit, so I would like you to help me with him, perhaps he will give me a reprieve from some of the He said: “Yes, I will come to you, Allah willing, near the middle of the day.” He said: So, he came with his companions. He said: They sat in the shade and the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  greeted us and asked permission, then he entered upon us. He said: I said to my wife: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) came to me today in the middle of the day, so do not he saw you and did not harm the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  in my house with anything and did not speak to him. So , she spread out a bed and a pillow and he put his head down and slept. Then I said to my slave: Slaughter this young goat, which is tame and fat, and the ox and the calf, and finish them before the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  wakes up and I am with you. So, we did not go down in it until we finished it, and he was asleep, so I said: When the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) wakes up, he calls for purification, and I fear that when he finishes, he will get up and not finish his purification until the neck is placed in front of him. So, when he woke up, he said: “O 27 Jabir, bring me purification.” He said: “Yes.” So, he did not finish his ablution until the neck of the goat was placed in front of him. He said: He looked at me and said: “It seems that you know our love for meat. Call Abu Bakr  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) Then he called his companions. The food was brought and placed. He put his hand on it and said: “In the name of Allah, eat.” So, they ate until they were full and there was a lot of meat left over. He said: “By Allah, the assembly of Banu Salamah, when they look at them, is more beloved to them than their eyes, they did not come near him for fear that they would harm him, then he stood up, and his companions stood up, and they went out in front of him, and he was saying: “Leave my back to the angels.” He said: So, I followed them until I reached the roof of the door, and my wife stuck out her chest and she was covered, and she said: O Apostle of Allah, send blessings upon me and upon my husband. He said: “May Allah send blessings upon you and upon your husband.” Then he said: “Call so-and-so for me for the debtor who has been very strict with me in demanding it.” Anas said: “Make Jabir pay a portion of your father’s debt until this coming debt.” He said: “I will not do that.” He said: “And he became ill and said: ‘It is only the property of orphans.’” The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: “Where is Jabir?” He said: I said: I am the one, O Apostle of Allah. He said: “Eat it for him, for Allah the Most High will repay him.” So, he raised his head to the sky, and behold, the sun had set. He said: “The prayer, O Abu Bakr  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  ”.So, they rushed to the mosque, and I said to my creditor: “Bring your vessels near.” So , I measured out for him some ajwa dates, and Allah repaid him and left us with such, and such dates left over. He said: So I came running to the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) in his mosque as if I were a spark, and I found the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  praying, so I said: O Apostle of Allah, I have measured out my creditors dates, and Allah has paid him back and left us with such and such dates left over. So, the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  said: "Where is Umar ibn al -Khattab (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) "? He said: So, he came running. He said: Ask Jabir bin Abdullah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) about his debtor.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us, Yazid ibn Abi Hakim informed us, Al-Hakam ibn Abaan informed me, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “Allah preferred Muhammad (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  over the prophets (علیهم  السلَم)  and over the people of heaven. They said: O Ibn Abbas  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه ) how did He prefer him over the people of heaven? He said: Allah said: To the people of heaven. And whoever among them says, “I am a Allah besides Him,” We will recompense him with Hell. Thus, do We recompense the wrongdoers. Surah Al -Anbiya, verse 29. And Allah Almighty said to Muhammad  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم ) : Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, so that Allah may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what will come after.” Surah Al -Fath, verses 1-2. They said: What is his superiority 28 over the prophets, peace be upon them? He said: Allah said: “And We did not send any Apostle except with the language of his people to make things clear to them.” Surah Ibrahim, verse 4. And Allah said to Muhammad (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) And We have not sent you except as mercy to mankind.” Surah Saba, verse 28. So, Allah sent him to the jinn and mankind.

Ubaydullah bin Abdul Majeed informed us, Zam’ah told us, on the authority of Salamah, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه ) who said: Some of the companions of the Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  were sitting waiting for him. He went out and when he came close to them, he heard them talking, so he listened to their conversation. Then some of them said: It is strange that Allah has taken from among His creation a friend, so Ibrahim (علیه  السلَم ) is His friend. Another said: What is more amazing th en: “And Allah spoke to M usa (علیه  السلَم)  directly” Surah An -Nisa, verse 164. Another said: “So Isa (علیه  السلَم)  is the Word of Allah and His Spirit.” Another said: “And Allah chose Adam (علیه  السلَم) so Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم ) went out to them and greeted them and said: ‘I have heard your speech and your astonishment. Indeed, Ibrahim (علیه السلَم)  is the friend of Allah, and so he is, and Musa (علیه السلَم ) is the Savior, and so he is, and Isa (علیه  السلَم)  His spirit and His word, and so is he, and Adam (علیه السلَم )was chosen by Allah the Most High, and so is he. Beware, I am the beloved of Allah, and that is no boasting, and I am the bearer of the banner of praise on the Day of Resurrection, and that is no boasting, and I am the first intercessor, and the first whos e intercession is accepted on the Day of Resurrection, and that is no boasting, and I am the first to stir the rings of Paradise, and that is no boasting, and Allah opens them and admits me into it, and with me are the poor. The believers, and I am  not boasting. I am the most honorable of the first and the last in the sight of Allah, and I am not boasting.

Saeed bin Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur bin Abi Al-Aswad, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Al -Rabi’ bin Anas, on the authority of Anas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: “I will be the first of them to go out, and I will be their leader when they come, and I will be their orator when they listen, and I will be their intercessor when they are detained, and I will be their bringer of good tidings when they despair. And the keys on that Day will be in My hand, and I will be the most honorable of the sons of Adam (علیه  السلَم)  in the sight of my Lord. A thousand servants will circulate around Me as if they were hidden eggs or scattered pearls.

Abdullah bin Abdul-Hakam Al-Misri informed us, Bakr bin Mudar informed us, on the authority of Jaafar bin Rabi’ah, on the authority of Salih, who is the son of Ata’ bin Khabab, the freedman of Banu Ad-Du’il, on the authority of Ata’ bin Abi Rabah, on the a uthority of Jabir bin Abdullah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) that the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه وآله وسلم)  said: “I am the leader of the Apostles, and I am not boasting, and I a m t he Seal of the Prophets, and that is not boasting. I am the first intercessor and the first whose intercession is accepted, and that is not boasting.

Muhammad ibn ‘Abbad narrated to us, Sufyan - he is Ibn ‘Uyaynah - narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jud’an, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) that the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  said: “I will be the first to take hold of the ring of the door of Paradise and then knock it down.” Anas said: It is as if I see the hand of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) moving it. Sufyan described it to us. Likewise, Abu Abdullah gathered his fingers and moved them. He said: Thabit said to him: Did you touch the hand of Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) with your hand? He said: Yes. He said: Then give it to me so that I may kiss it.

Ahmad ibn Abdullah informed us, Husayn ibn Ali told us, on the authority of Zaydah, on the authority of al -Mukhtar ibn Fulful, on the authority of Anas  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه ) who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: “I am the first intercessor in Paradise.”

Abdullah ibn Salih informed us, Al-Layth told me, Yazid told me - he is Ibn Abdullah ibn Al-Haad - on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Amr, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: I heard the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) say: “I will be the first of the people on the Day of Resurrection when the earth will split open, revealing myself, and that is no boasting. I will be given the banner of praise, and that is not boasting.” I am proud, and I am the master of mankind on the Day of Resurrection, and I am not boasting. I am the first to enter Paradise on the Day of Resurrection, and I am not boasting. I will come to the gate of Paradise and take hold of its ri ng, and they will say: Who is this? I will say: I am Muhammad, and they will open it for me, and I will enter and find the Almighty facing me, so I will prostrate to Him, and He will say: Raise your head, O Muhammad, and speak, and I will be heard. From You, and say, it will be accepted from You and intercede, and your intercession will be accepted. So, I will raise my head and say, “My nation, my nation, O Lord.” He will say, “Go to Your nation, and whoever You find in whose heart faith equal to the weight of a grain of barley, admit him into Paradise.” So, I will go, and whoever I find in whose heart faith equal to that weight, I will admit them into Paradise. Then I will find the Almighty facing me, so I will prostrate. To him, and he says: Raise your head, O Muhammad, and speak, and it will be heard from you, and say: It will be accepted from you, and intercede, and your intercession will be accepted. So, I raise my head and say: My nation, my nation, O Lord. So, he says: Go to your nation, and whoever you find in his heart the weight of a mustard seed of faith, admit him into Paradise. So I go, and whoever I find in his heart the weight of that I will admit them into Paradise, and the reckoning of the people will be completed, and whoever remains of my nation will be admitted into the Fire with the people of the Fire. Then the people of the Fire will say, “What benefit did it avail you that you used to worship Allah and did not associate 31 anything with Him?” Then the Almighty will say, “By My might, I will surely free them from the Fire.” Then He will send for them, and they will emerge from the Fire having been humiliated. Then they will be brought into the River of Life and will grow in it as a seed grows in the scum of a torrent. And it will be written before their eyes, “These are the freed ones of Allah.” Then they will be taken away and will enter Paradise. Then the people of Paradise will say to them, “These are the people of Hell.” T hen the Almighty will say, “Rather, these are the freed ones of the Almighty.”

Abdullah bin Salih informed us, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Yunus bin Maysarah, on the authority of Abu Idris Al-Khawlani, on the authority of Ibn Ghanam, who said: “ Jibreel (علیه السلَم) descended upon the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) and split open his stomach. Then Jibreel said: A submissive heart in which there  are two hearing ears and two seeing eyes. Muhammad is the Apostle of Allah, the follower, the gatherer.” Your character is good, your tongue is truthful, and your soul is at peace.” Abu Muhammad said: Waki (وَكِیع ) means severe.

Abdullah ibn Salih informed us, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Urwah ibn Ruwaym, on the authority of Amr ibn Qays, that the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  said: “Allah has granted me the appointed time and has shortened it for me, so we are the last, and we are the first on the Day of Resurrection. I will say something without boasting: Ibrahim (عَلَیْهِ  السَّلَمُ ) is the friend of Allah.” Musa (عَلَیْهِ  السَّلَمُ ) is the Chosen One of Allah, and I am the Beloved of Allah, and with me is the Banner of Praise on the Day of Resurrection. Allah, the Exalted, has promised me concerning my nation and has protected them from three things: that no famine will afflict them, that no enemy will eradicate them, and that He will not unite them in misguidance. 32

Muhammad ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, Muawiyah ibn Yahya narrated to us, Arta’ah ibn al - Mundhir narrated to us, on the authority of Damrah ibn Habib, who said: I heard Maslamah al - Sakuni - and someone other than Muhammad said: Salamah al -Sakuni (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  - say: While we were with the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) someone said: O Apostle of Allah, have you been given food from the sky? He said: “Yes, I was brought food.” He said: “O Prophet of Allah, was there any surplus in it?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “Then what was done with it?” He said: “It was taken up to the sky, and it was revealed to me that I would not remain among you except for a little while, then you would remain until you would say: W hen, when? Then you would come to me in groups, some of you annihilating others. The Hour is of great affliction, and after it are years of earthquakes.

Uthman ibn Muhammad informed us, Yazid ibn Harun informed us, Sulayman al-Taymi informed us, on the authority of Abu al-Ala’, on the authority of Samurah ibn Jundub (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)that the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) was brought a bowl of tharid and placed in front of the people, and they took turns eating it until noon the next morning, some people standing and others sitting. Then he said: A man said to Samura ibn Jundub: Was it not extended? Samura said: Why are you surprised? It was only extended from here, and he pointed with his hand to the sky.

Muhammad ibn Said narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad informed us, on the authority of Ashath ibn Sawwar, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Jabir ibn Samurah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: "I saw the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) on a bright night, wearing 33 a red garment. I looked at him and at the moon. He said: It was more beautiful in my eyes than the moon."

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir informed us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi al-Thābit al-Zuhri informed us, Ismā’il ibn Ibrahim ibn akhī Musa informed me, on the authority of his paternal uncle Musa ibn ‘Uqbah, on the authority of Kuraib, on the authority of Ibn Abbas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه وآله وسلم)  used to separate his two incisors. When he spoke, it was seen as if light was coming out of his mouth. Between his teeth

Mahmoud bin Ghailan informed us, Yazid bin Harun informed us, Mis’ar informed us, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Umair, who said: Ibn Umar  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  said: “I have never seen anyone more courageous, more generous, braver, more radiant, or more pure than the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم.)

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir al-Hizami informed us, Ubaydullah ibn Musa informed us, Usamah ibn Zayd informed us, on the authority of Abu Ubaydah ibn Muhammad ibn Ammar ibn Yasir, who said: I said to al-Rubayy’ bint Mu’awwidh ibn ‘Afra’: Describe the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) to us. She said: O my son, if you saw him, you would see the sun rising.

Hajjaj ibn Minhal informed us, Hammad ibn Salamah informed us, Thabit informed us, on the authority of Anas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آلهوسلم)  had a radiant complexion, as if his sweat were pearls. When he walked, he would walk with a swaying limp. I never touched silk or brocade softer than his hand, and I never smelled a fragrance more pleasant than his fragrance: musk or anything else. "

Abu al-Numan informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd informed us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  who said: "I served the Apostle of Allah (صلى علیه و آله وسلم) and he never said to me, Uff, nor did he say to me about anything I did, Why did you do such and such? or Why didnt you do such and such? And he said, No, by Allah, I have never touched brocade or silk softer than the hand of..." The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) and I have never found a scent or fragrance more pleasant than the scent or fragrance of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم).

Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Rifai informed us, Abu Bakr informed us, on the authority of Habib ibn Khudrah, who said: A man from Banu Huraysh told me: I was with my father when the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) stoned Ma’iz ibn Malik (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)When the stones hit him, I was terrified. The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  embraced me, and some of his sweat dripped onto me. His armpit smells like musk.

Abu Nu`aym narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Bara`, who said: A man asked him: Do you think the face of the Apostle of Allah (صلى علیه و آله وسلم) was like a sword? He said: “No, like the moon.”

Yazid ibn Harun informed us, Sharik informed us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  was “known at night by his pleasant scent.”

Malik ibn Ismail informed us, Ishaq ibn al -Fadl ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Hashimi informed us, al- Mughirah ibn Atiyyah informed us, on the authority of Abu al -Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) that the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) did not take a path, or did not take a path, and anyone followed him, except that they would know that he had taken it, because of his pleasant scent,” or he said: because of the smell of his sweat

Jafar ibn Awn informed us, Muhammad ibn Amr al-Laythi informed us, on the authority of Abu Salamah, who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  used to eat gifts and not accept charity. Then a Jewish woman from Khaybar presented him with a roasted sheep. He took some of it, and Bishr ibn al-Bara took some of it. Then the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) raised his hand 36 and said: “This woman tells me that she has poisoned the sheep.” Then Bishr ibn al-Bara (رضئ تعالی عنه) died, and the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  sent word to her: “What made you do what you did?” She said: “If you were a prophet, nothing would harm you, and if you were a king, I would have relieved the people of you.” He said during his illness: “I have not ceased from the food I ate in Khaybar, and now it is time for my aorta to sever.”

Al-Hakam ibn Nafi’ informed us, Shu’ayb ibn Abi Hamza informed us, on the authority of Al - Zuhri, who said: Jabir ibn Abdullah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)used to narrate that a Jewish woman from the people of Khaybar poisoned a roasted sheep, then presented it to the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)The Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) took a forearm of it and ate from it, and the group ate from the His companions were with him. Then the Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  said to them: “Raise your hands (do not eat).” The Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) sent for the Jewish woman and called her. He said to her: “Did you poison this sheep?” She said: “Yes. And who told you?” The Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: “This one told me that it was in my hand: for the arm.” She said: “Yes.” He said: “Then what?” Did you mean that?” She said: “I said: If he was a prophet, it would not harm him, and if he was not a prophet, we would be relieved of him.” So, the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) forgave her and did not punish her. Some of his companions who had eaten from the sheep died, and the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) had his shoulder cupped because of the one who had eaten from the sheep. Abu Hind, a freed slave, cupped him. Banu Bayada, with the horn and the blade, and he is from Banu Thamamah, and they are a tribe of the Ansar

Abdullah ibn Salih informed us, Al-Layth told me, Saeed ibn Abi Saeed Al -Maqburi told me, on the authority of Abu Hurairah  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه )who said: When Khaybar was conquered, a poisoned sheep was presented to the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: “Gather for me whoever is here from the Jews.” So, they were gathered for him, and he said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said to them: “I am going to ask you about something. Will you tell me the truth?” They said: “Yes, O Abu al-Qasim.” The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  said to them: “Who is your father?” They said: “Our father is so - and-so.” The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  said: “You have lied. Rather, your father is so-and-so.” They said: “You have spoken the truth and have acted righteously.” The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said to them: “Will you tell me the truth if I ask you about something?” They said, “Yes, and if we lie to you, you will know our lying just as you knew it in our fathers.” Then the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said to them, “Who are the people of Hell?” “They said: We will be in it for a short while, then you will replace us in it.” The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said to them: “Be gone in it, for by Allah, we will never replace you in it.” Then he said to them: “Will you tell me the truth if I ask you about something?” They s aid: “Yes.” He said: “Did you put poison in this sheep?” They said: Yes. He said: What made you do that? They said: If you are a liar, we want to get rid of you, and if you are a prophet, it will not harm you.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn al - Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  who said: “The Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) was never asked for anything and said: ‘No.’” Abu Muhammad said: Ibn Uyaynah said: “If he did not have it, he would promise.”

Abdullah ibn Imran informed us, Abu Dawud al -Tayalisi told us, on the authority of Zam’ah, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa’d, who said: “The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) was modest. He was never asked for anything without giving it to him.” 38

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Khalaf informed us, Abd al -Rahman ibn Muhammad informed us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr informed me, on the authority of an Arab man, who said: I jostled the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) on the day of Hunayn, and I had a thick sandal on my foot, so I stepped on the foot of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) Then he gave me a blow with a whip in his hand and said: “In the name of Allah, you have caused me pain.” He said: “So I spent the night blaming myself, saying: ‘I have caused pain to the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) He said: “So I spent the night as Allah knows, and when morning came, a man said: ‘Where is so -and-so?’ I said: ‘This, by Allah, is what happened to me yesterday.’ So, I left, and I was I was afraid, so the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said to me: “Yesterday you stepped on my foot with your sandal, and it hurt me, so I lashed you once with the whip. Here are eighty ewes, so take them.”

Yaqub ibn Humayd informed us, Abd al -Aziz ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Az - Zuhri’s nephew, on the authority of Az -Zuhri, who said: Jibreel (عَلَیْهِ  السَّلَمُ  )said: “There are no people on earth with ten houses but I turned them over, and I did not find anyone who spent this money more generously than the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)”.

Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to us, Al-Fadl ibn Musa narrated to us, Al -Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Uqayl, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “The Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  used to recite dhikr frequently, and he used to speak little, and he used to prolong the prayer and shorten the sermon, and he did not disdain or disdain to walk with a widow.” And the poor, and He fulfills their need for them. 39

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd informed us, on the authority of Ayyub, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Al-Abbas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) said: I will surely know how long the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  will remain among us. He said: O Apostle of Allah, I see that they have harmed you and their dust has harmed you, so why don’t you build a canopy from which you can speak to them? He said: I will remain between I will see them trampling on my heels and fighting over my cloak until Allah is the one who re lieves me of them.” He said: “Then I knew that his stay among us would be short.”

Al-Hakam ibn Musa informed us, Yahya ibn Hamza told us, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Dawud ibn Ali, who said: It was said: O Apostle of Allah (صلى  اللہ  علیه  و  آله  وسلم) should we not block you? He said: “No, let them tread on my heels and I tread on their heels until Allah relieves me of them.”

Zakariya ibn Adi informed us, Hatim ibn Ismail told us, on the authority of Unays ibn Abi Yahya, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) came out to us during his illness in which he died, and we were in the mosque, wrapping his head with a rag until he fell towards the pulpit, and he sat up on it. And we followed him. He said, “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I can see the Cistern from where I am standing.” Then he said, “A servant was offered the world and its adornments, and he chose the Hereafter.” No one realized this except Abu Bakr  (رضئتعالی عنه) His eyes 40 welled up with tears, and he wept. Then he said, “Rather, we would sacrifice our fathers, our mothers, and ourselves for you.” And our money, O Apostle of Allah. He said: Then he descended and did not rise again until this hour.

Khalifa bin Khayyat informed us, Bakr bin Sulayman informed us, Ibn Ishaq informed us, Abdullah bin Umar bin Ali bin Adi informed me, on the authority of Ubayd, the freed slave of Al- Hakam bin Abi Al-As, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, on the authority of Abu Muwayhiba (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) the freed slave of the Apostle of Allah (صلىاللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said to me: “I have been commanded to ask forgiveness for the people of al-Baqi’, so come with me.” So, I went with him in the middle of the night. When he stopped over them, he said: “Peace be upon you, O people of the graves. May what you have become happy with what the people have become. Trials have come like pieces of a dark night, one after the other. The last is worse than the first.” The first,” then he turned to me and said: “O Abu Muwayhiba, I have been given the keys to the treasures of this world and eternity in it, then Paradise, and I have been given the choice between that and meeting my Lord.” I said: “May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, take the keys to the treasures of this world and eternity in it, then Paradise.” He said: “No, by Allah, O Abu Muwayhiba, I have chosen to meet my Lord.” Then he asked forgiveness for the people of Al -Baqi’, then he left. The pain from which he died was first brought to the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم).

Sa`id ibn Sulayman informed us, on the authority of `Abbad ibn al -`Awwam, on the authority of Hilal ibn Khabab, on the authority of `Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) , who said: When the verse, “When there comes the help of Allah and the conquest,” was revealed, the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) called Fatimah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنہا) and said, “The news 41 of my death has come to me.” She wept, but he said, “Do not weep, for you will be the first of my family to join me.” She laughed, and some of the wives of the Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) saw her and said: O Fatima (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنہا)we saw you cry and then laugh? She said: He told me that he had been informed of his death, so I cried. Then he said to me: “Do not cry, for you will be the first of my family to join me.” So, I laughed, and the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: “The victory and conquest of Allah have come, and the victory has come.” The people of Yemen: They have the most tender hearts, faith is Yemeni, and wisdom is Yemeni.

Al-Hakam ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Muhammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Yaqub ibn Utbah, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah, on the authority of Ummul Momineen Aishah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنہا)who said: The Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم ) came back to me one day from a funeral procession in al-Baqi’, and found me suffering from a headache, and I was saying: Oh, my head! He said: "Rather, I am, O Aisha, and his head!" He said: "What harm would it do you if you died before me, so I washed you, shrouded you, prayed over you, and buried you?" I said: "By Allah, it is as if I see you. If I did that, you would return to my house and go one of your other wives." She said: "The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  smiled, and then the pain in which he died began."

Farwah ibn Abi al -Maghra’ informed us, Ibrahim ibn Mukhtar told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Ummul Momineen Aishah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنہا)who said: The Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said during his illness: “Pour seven water skins from seven different wells over me until I go out to the people and give them advice.” He said: So, we seated him in a tub belonging to 42 Ummul Momineen Hafsa (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنہا)and we poured water over him, or we poured water over him. The doubt is on the part of Muhammad ibn Ishaq. He found relief, so he went out and ascended the pulpit, and praised Allah and extolled Him, and asked forgiveness for the martyrs from among the companions of Uhud and supplicated for them. Then he said: “As for what follows, the Ansar are my refuge to which I have taken refuge. So, honor the honor among them, and overlook the wrongdoer among them, except in  a specific case. Indeed, one of Allah’s servants was given the choice between this world and what is with Allah, and he chose what is with Allah.” Abu Bakr (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) wept, and he thought that he meant himself. The Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said, “Take it easy, O Abu Bakr. Block these doors of the streets leading to the mosque, except for door of Abu Bakr, for I do not know of a man who has a better hand in companionship than Abu Bakr (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)”.

Said ibn Mansur informed us, Fulaih ibn Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of Abd al - Rahman, on the authority of al -Qasim ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Ummul Momineen Aisha (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنہا)who said: the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) was called to prayer during his illness, and he said: "Tell Abu Bakr (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  to lead the people in prayer." Then he fainted, and when he recovered, he said: "Have you ordered Abu Bakr  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) to lead the people in prayer?" I said: Abu Bakr (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) is a gentle man, so why don’t you order Umar (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) He said: “You are like the companions of Yusuf (عَلَیْهِ  السَّلَمُ )Tell Abu Bakr (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) to lead the people in prayer.  Many people say something wishful, but Allah and the believers refuse (to accept their talk).

Sulayman ibn Harb informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Ayyub, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: “The Apostle of Allah  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم ) passed away on Monday. He was kept for the rest of the day and night and the next day until he was buried on Wednesday night. They said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) did not die, but his soul ascended just as the soul of M usa (عَلَیْهِ  السَّلَمُ ) ascended.” Then Umar (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  stood up and said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) did not die, but his soul ascended just as the soul of Musa (عَلَیْهِ  السَّلَمُ ) ascended. By Allah, the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  will not die until he cuts off the hands and tongues of people. Umar (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) continued speaking until his cheeks foamed from what he was threatening and saying. Then al -Abbas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) stood up and said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) and he (the Prophet) said, "He has died, and he is a human being. O my people, bury your companion, for he is more honorable to Allah than for Him to cause him to die twice. Can one of you die once and He causes him to die twice, and he is more honorable to Allah than that?" O my people, bury your companion, for if he is as you say, then it is not difficult for Allah to search for him in the dust. By Allah, the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  did not die unti l he had left behind a clear path. He made lawful what was lawful and made unlawful what was unlawful. He married and divorced, fought and made peace. No shepherd of sheep, whose owner used to follow them to the tops of mountains, beating the branches with his whip and watering their water tank with his hand, was more tireless or more diligent than the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)He was among you, O people, so bury your companion. He said: Umm Ayman  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنہا)  began to cry, and i t was said to her: O Umm Ayman (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنہا)are you crying for the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)She said: By Allah, I am not crying for the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) because I don’t know that he has gone to something better for him than this world, but I am crying because the news from heaven has ceased. Hammad said: “Ayyub was choked with tears when he reached here.”

Abdul Wahhab ibn Said al -Dimashqi informed us, Shuayb ibn Ishaq informed us, al -Awzai informed us, Yaish ibn al-Walid informed us, Makhul informed us that the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: "If a calamity befalls one of you, let him remember my calamity, for it is among the greatest of calamities."

Abu Nu`aym informed us, Fitr told us, on the authority of Ata’, who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلىاللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  said: “If a calamity befalls one of you, let him remember my affliction, for it is among the greatest of calamities.”

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Khalaf narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Umar ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, who said: “I never heard Ibn Umar (رضئ تعالی عنه) mention the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) without him crying.”

Abu al-Numan informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, that Fatimah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنہا) said: "O Anas, how could your souls be content to throw dust on the Apostle of Allah (صلىعلیه و آله وسلم) And she said: "O my father, how close he is to his Lord! O my father, the Garden of Paradise is his abode! O my father, to Jibreel we announce his death! O my father!" He answered his Lord who called him. Hammad said: When Thabit (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) narrated it, he cried. Thabit said: When Anas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) narrated it, he cried.

Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Thabit (رضئاللہ تعالی عنه)on the authority of Anas  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) and he mentioned the Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) who said: “I witnessed him on the day he entered M adina, and I have never seen a day that was better or brighter than the day on which the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  entered 45 upon us.
