And I witnessed him on the day of his death, and I have never seen a day that was uglier or darker than the day on which the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  entered upon us. The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) died in it.

Abdullah ibn Mutee’ narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Abd al -Jalil, on the authority of Abu Hariz al-Azdi, who said: Abdullah ibn Salam said to the Prophet (صلى علیه و آله وسلم)O Apostle of Allah, we will find you on the Day of Resurrection standing before your Lord, and your cheeks will be red, and you will be ashamed before your Lord of what your nation has innovated after you.”

Al-Qasim ibn Kathir told us: I heard Abd al -Rahman ibn Shurayh narrating, on the authority of Abu al-Aswad al-Qurashi, on the authority of Abu Qurrah, the freed slave of Abu Jahl, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)on the authority of the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) : When this surah was revealed to the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)When there comes the help of Allah and the conquest And you see the people They will enter the religion of Allah in multitudes Surah An-Nasr, Verse 1-2, the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: “They will surely leave it in multitudes just as they entered it in multitudes.”

Abu Bakr al -Misri informed me, on the authority of Sulayman Abu Ayyub al -Khuza’i, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa’id al-Umawi, on the authority of Ma’ruf ibn Kharbudh al-Makki, on the authority of Khalid ibn Ma’dan, who said: “Abdullah ibn al-Ahtham entered upon Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz with the common people, and Umar was not surprised until he was in front of him, speaking. He praised Allah and extolled…” Upon him, then he said: As for what follows, Allah created the creation without need of their obedience, safe from their disobedience. On that day, people will be in different ranks and opinions. The Arabs will be in the worst of those ranks: the people of the stone, the people of the hair, and the people  of the back. The good things of this world and the comfort of its life will pass them by. They will not ask Allah as a group, nor will they recite to Him. A book, their dead are in the Fire, and their living are blind and unclean, along with countless things that are desired and disdained. But when Allah wanted to spread His mercy upon them, He sent to them a Apostle from among themselves. Grievous to him is your suffering, concerned over you and to the believers kind and merciful. May Allah’s prayers and peace be upon him, and upon him be the mercy of Allah and His blessings. So, he did not. What prevented them from doing so was that they wounded him in his body and called him by his name, while he had with him a speaking book from Allah, which could only be carried out by His command and could not depart except with His permission. So, when he was ordered to decide and was urged to fight, his excretion was relieved by Allah’s command. So, Allah made his argument successful, made his word permissible, made his call clear, and he departed from this world pious and pure. Then he rose up. After him came Abu Bakr  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who followed his Sunnah and took his path. The Arabs apostatized, or whoever among them did that, but he refused to accept anythi ng from them after the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) except what was acceptable. He pulled the swords from their scabbards and lit fires in their flames. Then he afflicted the people of truth with the people of falsehood, and he did not cease to tear them apart and give water to their families. The earth was covered with their blood, until He brought them into the place from which they had left, and He made them reconcile with that from which they had fled. He had acquired from the wealth of Allah a young camel, from which he could drink, and an Abyssinian woman who had breastfed his son. He saw this at his death as a lump in his throat, and this led to the Caliph after him, and he departed this world pious and pure, following the path of his compa nion. Then Umar (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه ) rose after him . He conquered all the cities, and mixed severity with leniency, and rolled up his sleeves, and rolled up his legs, and counted the matters and the tools of war. When the young man of al -Mughirah ibn Shu’bah struck him, he ordered Ibn Abbas  (رضئ 47 اللہ تعالی عنه) to ask the people: Do they prove his killer? When it was said: The young man of al - Mughirah ibn Shu’bah, he began to praise his Lord that he had not been struck by him has a right to the spoils of war, and he argues against him by saying that he only made his blood permissible because he made his right permissible. He had acquired eighty -odd thousands of Allah’s wealth, so he broke his quarters and was reluctant to support his children because of it. So, he gave it to the Caliph after him, and he departed from this world pious and pure, following the path of his two companions. Then, O Umar, you are a son of this world, and its kings gave birth to you. And she fed you her breasts, and it grew in her, seeking its places. But when you took charge of it, you threw it where Allah threw it. You abandoned it, neglected it, and defiled it, except for what you took from it. So, praise be to Allah, who removed our sin through you and relieved our distress through you. So go on and do not look back, for nothing is too strong for the truth, and nothing is humiliated by falsehood. I say my word. This, and I ask forgiveness of Allah for myself and for the believing men and women.” Abu Ayyub said: “So Umar ibn Abd al -Aziz used to say about something: Ibn al-Ahtham said to me: Go and do not look back.”

Abu al-Numan narrated to us, Said ibn Zayd narrated to us, Amr ibn Malik al -Nukri narrated to us, Abu al -Jawza Aws ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: "The people of Medina were experiencing a severe drought, so they complained to Ummul Momineen Aishah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنہا)and she said: Look at the tomb of the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) and make a window in it that faces the sky so that there is no space between it and the sky." And between the sky is a ceiling. He said: So, they did, and we were showered with rain until the grass grew, and the camels grew fat until they burst from the fat, so it was called the Year of the Burst.

Marwan ibn Muhammad informed us, on the authority of Sa`id ibn `Abd al -`Aziz, who said: “When the days of al-Harrah came, the call to prayer was not made in the Prophet’s (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) Mosque for three days, nor was the Iqama performed, and Sa`id ibn al-Musayyib did not leave the mosque. He did not know the time of prayer except by a murmur he heard from the Prophet’s (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) grave.” He then mentioned its meaning. 48 The above Hadith is not to be preserved as Sa’id was working for the Kings and all his statements about himself, Ahle Baith and Khulafa-e-Rashideen are doubtful.

Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, Al-Layth narrated to me, Khalid - he is Ibn Yazid - narrated to me, from Saeed - he is Ibn Abi Hilal - from Nubayh ibn Wahb, that Ka’b (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) entered upon Ummul Momineen Aishah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)and they mentioned the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) Ka’b said: “There is not a day that dawns except that seventy thousand angels descend until they surround the grave of the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) ”.They would beat their wings and invoke blessings upon him until evening came, and a similar number would ascend and descend. They would do the same until the earth split open and he would emerge with seventy thousand angels escorting him.

Abu Asim informed us, Thawr ibn Yazid informed us, Khalid ibn Ma’dan informed me, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr, on the authority of Irbad ibn Sariyah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  led us in the dawn prayer, then he gave us a powerful sermon that made our eyes shed tears and our hearts fearful. Then someone said: O Apostle of Allah! Allah, is it a farewell sermon? So, he advised us, saying: “I advise you to fear Allah, and to listen and obey, even if he is an Abyssinian slave, for whoever among you lives after me will see much disagreement. So, adhere to my Sunnah and the Sunnah of the Rightly Guided Caliphs, and cling to it firmly. And beware of newly invented matters, for every new ly invented matter is an innovation. Abu ‘Asim said once: And beware of newly invented matters, for every innovation is misguidance.

Abu Al-Mughira informed us, Al -Awzai told us, on the authority of Yunus bin Yazid, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, who said: Those of our scholars who passed away used to say: "Adherence to the Sunnah is salvation, and knowledge is taken away quickly. The revival of knowledge is the stability of religion and the world, and in the loss of knowledge is the loss of all of that."

Abu Al -Mughira informed us, Al -Awza’i told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Amr Al - Saybani, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Daylami, who said: “It has reached me that the first sign of the disappearance of religion is the abandonment of the Sunnah . The religion disappears one Sunnah after another, just as a rope disappears, strength after strength.”

Abu Al-Mughira informed us, Al-Awza’i told us, on the authority of Hassan, who said: “No people innovate an innovation in their religion except that Allah removes something similar from their Sunnah, and then He does not return it to them until the Day of Resurrection.”
Muslim ibn Ibrahim informed us, Wahib told us, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, who said: “No man innovates an innovation except that he considers the sword permissible.”

Sulayman ibn Harb informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Ayyub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, who said: “The people of whims are the people of misguidance, and I do not see their fate except in the Fire. So, test them, for none of them invents a saying or he said: a hadith, and the matter is far from being decided by the sword. Indeed, hypocrisy is of various types.” Then he recited: “And among them is he who made a covenant with Allah, if He gives us from His bounty, we will surely give charity and be among the righteous. Surah At-Tawbah, verse 75. And among them are those who criticize you concerning charities. If they are given from them, they are pleased; but if they are not given from them, at once they become angry. Surah At - Tawbah, verse 58. And among them are those who annoy the Prophet and say, “He is an ear.” Say, “An ear of good for you.” Surah At -Tawbah, verse 61 .  So, their statement differed, and they agreed. In doubt and denial, and these people differed in their statement and gathered in the sword, and I do not see their fate except to the Fire.” Hammad said: Then Ayyub said regarding this hadith or regarding the first: And by Allah, he was among the wise jurists: meaning Abu Qilabah.

Amr ibn Awn informed us, on the authority of Khalid ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Amir, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud and Hudhayfah (رضئ  اللہ  تعالی عنہما)  that they were sitting when a man came and asked them about something. Ibn Mas’ud (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) said to Hudhayfah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)Why do you think they are asking me about this?” He said, “They know it, but then they leave it.” So, Ibn Mas’ud (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  came to him and said, “No, I am not sure.” Mas`ud said: “Whatever you asked us about from the Book of Allah the Most High that we know, we informed you about it, or a Sunnah from the Prophet of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) we informed you about it, and we have no power over what you have innovated.”

Abu Nu`aym informed us, Al -Mas`udi narrated to us, on the authority of `Abd al -Malik ibn Maysarah, on the authority of al-Nazzal ibn Sabrah, who said: “`Abdullah never gave a sermon in Kufa without attending it. I heard him one day, and he was asked about a man who divorces his wife eight times and the like. He said: It is as it is. Then he said: Allah revealed His Book and clarified its explanation. Whoever approaches the matter from its perspective, it has been made clear to him, and whoever opposes it, then by Allah we cannot oppose you.”

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi informed us, Shubah told us, Abd al -Malik ibn Maysarah told me, he said: I heard al-Nazzal ibn Sabrah say: "I witnessed Abdullah when a man and a woman came to him in a state of ihram, and he said: Allah has made things clear, so whoever approaches the matter according to its direction, then it has been made clear, and whoever opposes it, then by Allah we cannot oppose you."
Abdullah bin Saeed told us, Hafs told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ibn Sirin: “He would not say anything based on his opinion except what he heard.”
Abdullah bin Saeed informed us, Uthman, the father of Ali bin Uthman, told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, who said: “I never heard Ibrahim speak his own opinion about anything.”
Abu al-Nu’man informed us, Abu ‘Awana informed us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: “I have not said my opinion for thirty years.” Abu Hilal said: “For forty years.” 52

Makhlad ibn Malik narrated to us, Hakam ibn Salm narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Khaithamah, on the authority of Abd al -Aziz ibn Rufay’, who said: “Ata’ was asked about something, and he said: ‘I do not know.’ He said: ‘It was said to him: ‘Why don’t you express your opinion about it?’ He said: ‘I feel too shy before Allah to judge on earth based on my opinion.”

Ismail ibn Aban informed us, Hatim - he is Ibn Ismail - informed me, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ash-Shabi, who said: A man came to him asking him about something, so he said: "Ibn Masud used to say such and such about him." He said: "You tell me your opinion." He said: "Do you not marvel at this?" I told him on  the authority of Ibn Masud  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)and he asked me about my opinion, and my religion is more important to me." From that, by Allah, I would rather sing a song than tell you my opinion.”

Ismail ibn Aban informed us, Hatim - he is Ibn Ismail - told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ash-Shabi, who said: "Beware of analogy. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if you were to adopt an analogy, you would make lawful what is unlawful and forbid what is lawful. But whatever you have heard from those of the Companions of Muhammad (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) who have memorized it, then act upon it."

Said ibn Amir informed us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, on the authority of Al-qamah, who said: A man came to Abdullah and said: He divorced his wife eight times last night. He said: With one word? He said: With one word. He said: Do they want to separate your wife from you? He said: Yes. He said: A man came to him and said: He divorced his wife one hundred times. He said: With one word? He said: With one word. He said: Do they want to separate your wife from you? He said: Yes. Abdullah said: Whoever divorces as Allah has commanded him, Allah has made divorce clear. And whoever confuses himself, we have delegated his confusion to him. By Allah, you will not confuse Yourselves, and we bear it, it is as you say.

Sulayman ibn Harb informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa`id, on the authority of al -Qasim, who said: “For a man to live in ignorance after he has learned the right of Allah upon him is better for him than for him to say what he does not know.”

Sulayman ibn Harb informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Ayyub, who said: I heard al-Qasim being asked, and he said: “By Allah, we do not know everything you are asking about, and if we knew, we would not have wished to conceal it from you, and it is not permissible for us to conceal it from you.”

Saeed bin Aamer told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, who said: Al -Qasim was asked about something that he had named, so he said: “I am not compelled to consult, and I am not one of those who have a say in anything.”

Muhammad ibn Kathir informed us, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Yahya, who said: I said to al -Qasim: How difficult it is for me to be asked about something that you do not know, even though your father was an Imam. He said: “More difficult than that in the sight of Allah and of those who understand from Allah is for me to issue a fatwa without knowledge, or to narrate from someone who is not trustworthy.”

Amr ibn Awn informed us, Hisham informed us, on the authority of al -Awwam, on the authority of al-Musayyab ibn Rafi’, who said: “Whenever a matter arose among them in which there was no trace of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) they would gather and agree on it, and the truth was in what they saw, and the truth was in what they saw.” Abdullah informed us, Yazid informed us, on the authority of al-Awwam.

Yahya ibn Hassan and Muhammad ibn al -Mubarak informed us: Yahya ibn Hamza told us, Abu Salamah al-Himsi told us, that Wahb ibn Amr al -Jumahi told him that the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و 55 آله وسلم) said: “Do not hasten the calamity before it descends, for if you do not hasten it before it descends, the Muslims will not be separated from those among them.” When it is revealed, whoever says it, he will be guided and will be granted success. But if you  hasten it, your desires will differ, and you will take this and that. And he pointed in front of him, to his right, and to his left.

Muhammad ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Yahya ibn Hamza told us, Abu Salamah told me, that the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  was asked about a matter that occurs that is not in the Book or the Sunnah, so he said: “The devout believers will look into it.”

Ahmad ibn Abdullah informed us, Muadh ibn Muadh narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, who said: Al-Qasim said: “You ask about things we never asked about, and you argue about things we never argued about, and you ask about things I do not know what they are, and if we knew them, it would not be permissible for us to conceal them from you.”

Abdullah ibn Salih informed us, Al-Layth told me, Yazid ibn Abi Habib told me, on the authority of Umar ibn Al-Ashja, that Umar ibn Al-Khattab (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) said: “There will come people who will argue with you about the doubts of the Qur’an, so take them to the Sunnah, for the people of the Sunnah are the most knowledgeable about the Book of Allah.”

Muhammad ibn Uyaynah informed us, Ali - he is Ibn Mushir - told us, on the authority of Hisham - he is Ibn Urwah - on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al -Rahman ibn Nawfal - on the authority of Urwah ibn al -Zubayr, who said: “The situation of the Children of Israel remained moderate, with nothing wrong with it, until there arose among them the children of the captives of the nations, the children of the women whom the Children of Israel had taken captive.” Israel from others, so they said about them: By opinion, so they led them astray.

Muslim ibn Ibrahim informed us, Hammad ibn Yazid al -Minqari told us, my father told me, he said: A man came one day to Ibn Umar (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) and asked him about something, but he did not know what it was. Ibn Umar (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) said to him: “Do not ask about what did not happen, for I heard Umar ibn al -Khattab (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) cursing whoever asks about what did not happen.”

Al-Hakam ibn Nafi’ informed us, Shu’ayb informed us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, who said: It has reached us that Zayd ibn Thabit Al -Ansari (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) used to say when he was asked about a matter: “Did this happen?” If they said: “Yes, it did happen,” he would narrate about it what he knew and what he saw. But if they said: “It did not happen,” he said: “Then leave it until it happens.”

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us, Abu Hisham al -Makhzumi informed us, Wahib informed us, Dawud informed us, on the authority of Amir, who said: Ammar ibn Yasir (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) was asked about a matter, and he said: “Has this happened yet?” They said: “No.” He said: “Leave us until it happens, and when it happens, we will bear it for you.”

Muhammad ibn Ahmad informed us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Tawus, who said: Umar (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) said on the pulpit: “I feel embarrassed by Allah over a man who asked about something that did not happen, for Allah has made clear what is going to happen.”

Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Shaybah informed us, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Sa’id, on the authority of Ibn Abbas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “I have never seen a people who were better than the Companions of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) . They only asked him about thirteen matters until he passed away, all of which are mentioned in the Qur’an, including: They ask you about the month.” Al -Haram, Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 217, and they ask you about menstruation, Surah Al -Baqarah, verse 222. He said, “They were only asking about that which would benefit them.”

Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us, Ibn Awn informed us, on the authority of Umair ibn Ishaq, who said: “Those of the Companions of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  whom I met were more numerous than those who preceded me. I have never seen a people who were easier to follow or less strict than them.”

Al-Abbas ibn Sufyan informed me, on the authority of Zayd ibn Hubab, who said: Raja’ ibn Haywah informed me, saying: I heard Ubadah ibn Nusayy al -Kindi, and he was asked about a woman who died with a group of people who had no guardian, so he said: “I knew  people who were not as strict as you are, and they did not ask questions like you.”

Al-Abbas ibn Sufyan informed us, Zayd ibn Hubab informed us, Raja’ ibn Abi Salamah informed me, he said: Khalid ibn Hazim informed me, on the authority of Hisham ibn Muslim al -Qurashi, he said: I was with Ibn Muhayriz in Marj al-Dibaj and I saw him in seclusion, so I asked him about a matter, and he said to me: What do you do with questions? I said: “Were it not for questions, Knowledge would have been lost. He said: “Do not say ‘knowledge is lost,’ for knowledge does not go away as long as the Qur’an is recited. But if you had said: Jurisprudence is lost,’

Sulayman ibn Harb informed us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ash-Sha’bi, that ‘Umar (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) said: “O people, we do not know. Perhaps we command you to do things that are not lawful for you, and perhaps we forbid you things that are lawful for you. The last of the Qur’an to be revealed was the verse on usury, and the Apostle 59 of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) He did not explain it to us until he died, so leave that which makes you doubt for that which does not make you doubt.

Salm ibn Junada informed us, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of his uncle, who said: “I left Ibrahim, and Hammad met me, so he entrusted me with eight chapters of questions, so I asked him, and he answered me about four and left out four.”
Qabisah informed us, Sufyan informed us, on the authority of Abd al -Malik ibn Abjar, on the authority of Zubayd, who said: “I never asked Ibrahim about anything without seeing dislike on his face.”

Muhammad ibn Ahmad informed us, Ishaq ibn Mansur told us, on the authority of Umar ibn Abi Zaydah, who said: “I have never seen anyone who would say more often when asked about something he had no knowledge of than al-Sha’bi.”

Abu Asim informed us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, who said: I heard him mention, he said: Whenever something happened to Al -Sha’bi, he would fear Allah, and Ibrahim would say, and 60 say, and say. Abu Asim said: “Al -Sha’bi was in a better state with Ibn Awn than Ibrahim in this regard.”

Abdullah ibn Said informed us, Ahmad ibn Bashir informed us, Shubah informed us, on the authority of Jafar ibn Iyas, who said: I said to Said ibn Jubayr: Why do you not say anything about divorce? He said: There is nothing about it that I have not aske d about, but I hate to make permissible what is forbidden, or to make forbidden what is permissible.

Abu Nu`aym informed us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of `Ata` ibn al-Sa`ib, who said: I heard `Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla say: “I have seen in this mosque one hundred and twenty Ansar, and none of them narrated a hadith except that he wished that his brother would suffice him in narrating the hadith, and none of them was asked about a fatwa except that he wished that his brother would suffice him in issuing the fatwa.”

Yusuf ibn Yaqub al-Saffar narrated to us, Abu Bakr narrated to us, on the authority of Dawud, who said: I asked al -Shabi, "How did you act when you were asked?" He said, "You acted according to the expert. When a man was asked, he would say to his companion, Give  them a fatwa, and he would continue until he returned to the first opinion."
Ahmad ibn al-Hajjaj told us: I heard Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn al-Munkadir, who said: “The scholar enters between Allah and His servants, so let him seek a way out for himself.”

Muhammad ibn Qudamah told us, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Mis`ar, who said: Ma`n ibn `Abd al -Rahman brought me a letter and swore to me by Allah that it was his father’s handwriting. In it, there was: `Abdullah said: By He besides Whom there is no god, I have never seen anyone more severe with the extremists than the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)And I have never seen anyone more severe with them than Abu Bakr  (رضئ  اللہ  تعالی  عنه) . And I think that Umar (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) was more fearful for them or for them.

Abu Nu`aym informed us, Zam`ah ibn Salih narrated to us, on the authority of Uthman ibn Hadir al-Azdi, who said: I entered upon Ibn Abbas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  and I said: Advise me. He said: Yes. “You must have the fear of Allah and be steadfast. Follow and do not innovate.”

Makhlad ibn Malik ibn Jabir informed us, Al -Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, who said: “They used to think that it was on the road, as it was on the trace.” 62
Yusuf bin Musa informed us, Azhar told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, who said: “As long as he is on the trace, he is on the path.”

Abu Al-Mughira informed us, Al-Awza’i told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, who said: Abdullah bin Mas’ud  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه ) said: “Learn knowledge before it is taken away, and its taking away means that its people go away. Beware of extremism, delving into knowledge, and innovations. Stick to the old.”

Sulayman ibn Harb and Abu al-Nu’man narrated to us, on the authority of Hammad ibn Zayd, on the authority of Ayyub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, who said: Ibn Mas’ud (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) said: “You must seek knowledge before it is taken away, and its taking away means that its people are taken away. You must seek knowledge, for none of you knows when he will need it or when what he has will be in need. You…” You will find people who claim that they are calling you to the Book of Allah, but they have cast it behind their backs. So, stick to knowledge, and beware of innovation, and beware of extremism, and beware of going too deep, and stick to the old.

Abu al-Numan informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, Yazid ibn Hazim told us, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Yasar, that a man called Subaygh came to Madinah and began to ask about the ambiguous verses of the Quran. So, Umar (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) sent it to him while he had prepared palm branch clusters for him. He said, "Who are you?" He said, "I am Abdullah Subaygh." So, Umar (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) took a branch from those are the two humps, so he struck him and said: I am Abdullah Omar, so he struck him until his head bled, so he said: O Commander of the Faithful, that is enough, what I felt in my head has gone away.

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi informed us, Hammad ibn Salamah and Yazid ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Mulaykah, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) recited: “It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book; in it are verses that are entirely clear - they are the foundation of the Book - and others unspecific.” Surah Al Imran, verse 7. So, he said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: “If you see those who follow that which is ambiguous in it, then beware of them.”

Abdullah bin Muhammad informed us, Hafs told us, on the authority of Al -A’mash, on the authority of Shaqiq, who said: Abdullah was asked about something, so he said: “I hate to make permissible for you something that Allah has forbidden to you, or to forbid what Allah has made permissible for you.”

Muhammad ibn Uyaynah informed us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said: 64 “It is more beloved to me to return it to him as it is, than to take upon myself the trouble of doing something for him that I do not know.”

Abdullah ibn Salih informed us, Al-Layth informed me, Ibn Ajlan informed me, on the authority of Nafi’, the freed slave of Abdullah, that Subaygh al-Iraqi kept asking about matters of the Qur’an among the Muslim armies until he arrived in Egypt. Then Amr i bn al-‘As (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) sent him to Umar ibn al-Khattab (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)When the messenger came to him, With the book, he read it, and said: Where is the man? He said: In the saddlebag. Umar (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه ) said: “Look, lest he has gone astray, or you will suffer a painful punishment from me because of him.” So, he brought him to him, and Umar (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  said: “You are asking about something new.” So, Umar (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه )sent for some fresh palm fronds and hit him with them until a scar was left on his back. Then he left him until he recovered, then he came back to him, then he left him until he recovered, then he called So he gave him permission to return to his land and wrote to Abu Musa al-Ashari (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) that no Muslim should sit with him. This was very difficult for the man, so Abu Musa (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه ) wrote to Umar  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) It has become good. His repentance, so Omar (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه ) wrote: Give permission for the people to sit with him.

Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus informed us, Zuhair told us, Ismail ibn Abi Khalid told us, he said: I heard Aamir say: A man asked Ubayy ibn Ka’b for a fatwa, so he said: O Abu al-Mundhir, what do you say about such and such? He said: O my son, did what you asked me about happen? He said: No. He said: “If not, then give me time until it happens, then we will treat it.” ourselves until we tell you 65

Yahya ibn Hammad informed us, Abu Awana informed us, he said: He informed us on the authority of Firas, on the authority of Amir, on the authority of Masruq, he said: I was walking with Ubayy ibn Ka’b (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) and a young man said: What do you say, O my uncle, about such and such? He said: O my nephew, was this the case? He said: No. He said: “Then pardon us until it happens.”

Abdullah ibn Saeed narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, on the authority of Al -A’mash, who said: “Whenever Ibrahim was asked about something, he would only give the answer that he was asked about.”

Al-Husayn ibn Mansur informed us, Al -Husayn ibn Al -Walid informed us, on the authority of Wahib, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, “that he did not issue a fatwa regarding the vagina regarding anything in which there was a difference of opinion.”

Muslim ibn Ibrahim informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd informed us, As -Salt ibn Rashid informed us, he said: I asked Tawus about a matter, and he said to me: Was this? I said: Yes. He said: By Allah. I said: By Allah. Then he said: Our companions informed us on the authority of Muadh ibn Jabal (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  that he said: “O people, do not rush into trials before they come.” If it 66 descends, it will take you here and there. If you do not hasten to bring about the affliction before it descends, the Muslims will always have among them someone who, when asked, will be guided, and when speaking, will be granted success.

Bishr ibn al-Hakam narrated to us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad narrated to us, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: I asked him about a man who had been overtaken by two Ramadans. He said: Was it or was it not? He said: It has not happened yet. He said: Leave his affliction until it comes down. He said: So, we sought out a man for him, and he said: It has happened. He said: He feeds thirty poor people on behalf of the first of them, one poor person each day.

Abdullah ibn Imran informed us, Ishaq ibn Sulayman told us, Al -Umari told us, on the authority of Ubayd ibn Jurayj, who said: I used to sit in Mecca with Ibn Umar one day, and with Ibn Abbas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه ) one day, and Ibn Umar would always say when he was asked, “I have no knowledge,” more than what he issues fatwas about.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, who said: Abdullah said: “Learn, for none of you knows when he will be visited.”

Ibrahim ibn Musa informed us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Ayyub, on the authority of Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Jaafar, who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: “The most daring among you in issuing fatwas will be the most daring among you in Hellfire.”

Abu Al-Mughira informed us, Al-Awza’i told us, on the authority of Abdah bin Abi Lubabah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “Whoever innovates an opinion that is not in the Book of Allah, and that is not supported by a Sunnah from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) will not know what it is when he meets Allah.”

Abdullah ibn Yazid informed us, Saeed ibn Abi Ayyub informed us, Bakr ibn Amr al -Maafiri informed me, on the authority of Abu Uthman Muslim ibn Yasar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) on the authority of the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) who said: "Whoever gives a fatwa without reliable evidence, then the sin is upon the one who gave him the fatwa."

Muhammad ibn Ahmad informed us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  who said: “Whoever issues a fatwa that is not understood, then the sin is upon him.”

Muhammad ibn al-Salt informed us, Zuhayr told us, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Burqan, who told us, Maymun ibn Mihran said: Whenever a litigant came to Abu Bakr  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  he would look into the Book of Allah. If he found in it something that would allow him to decide between them, he would judge according to it. But if there was nothing in the Book, he would learn from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) concerning that matter. A Sunnah, he ruled accordingly. If he was exhausted, he would go out and ask the Muslims, saying: Such and such came to me. Do you know that the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  ruled in this regard? Perhaps a group of people would gather around him, all of them mentioning a ruling from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  and Abu Bakr would say, “Praise be to Allah, who has placed among us someone who will preserve the Sunnah of our Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)If he was unable to find a Sunnah from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  he would gather the leaders and best of the people and consult them. When their opinion was unanimous, he would decide on a decision. An order that he has decreed

Ibrahim ibn Musa and Amr ibn Zurara informed us, on the authority of Abd al -Aziz ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Abu Suhayl, who said: My wife was required to observe i’tikaf for three days in the Sacred Mosque. So I asked Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, while Ibn Shihab was with him. He said: I said: She must be fast. Ibn Shihab said: There is no i’tikaf without fasting. So, he said to him: Umar ibn Abd al -Aziz said: “Is it from the Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) He said: “No.” He said: “And from Abu Bakr?” He said: “No.” He said: “And from Umar?” He said: “No.” He said: “And from Uthman?” He said: “No.” Umar said: “I do not think she has to fast.” So, I went out and found Tawus and Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah, so I asked them. Tawus said: “Ibn Abbas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  did not think…” She is not required to fast unless she makes it her own.” He said: And Ata’ said: That is my opinion.

Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abu Aqil narrated to us, Saeed al-Jurairi narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, who said: When Abu Salamah came to Basra, I came to him with al - Hasan. He said to al-Hasan: Are you al-Hasan? No one in Basra was more beloved to me than you. That is because I have heard that you issue fatwas based on your own opinion. Do not issue fatwas based on your own opinion unless it is a Sunnah. On the authority of the Apostle of Allah (صلى علیه و آله وسلم) or a revealed book.

Ismah ibn al -Fadl informed us, Zayd ibn al-Hubab informed us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Uqbah, who narrated from al-Dahhak, on the authority of Jabir ibn Zayd, that Ibn Umar met him while performing the Tawaf and said to him: “O Abu al -Sha’tha’, you are one of the scholars of Basra, so do no t issue fatwas except based on the eloquent Qur’an or the established Sunnah. If you do anything other than that, you will be ruined and cause others to be ruined.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of ‘Amara ibn ‘Umair, on the authority of Hurayth ibn Zuhair, on the authority of ‘Abdullah ibn Mas’ud (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “A time has come upon us when we could not judge and we were not there. Indeed, Allah has decreed that we have reached what you see. So whoever is faced with a matter of judgment after today, let him judge according to what is in it.” The Book of Allah. If something comes to him that is not in the Book of Allah, then let him rule according to what the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) ruled. If something comes to him that is not in the Book of Allah, and the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  did not rule, then let him rule according to what the righteous ruled. And let him not say, “I fear,” or “I see.” For what is forbidden is clear, and what is lawful is clear, and between them are matters. Doubtful, so leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt. 70

Abdullah ibn Muhammad informed us, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid, who said: “Whenever Ibn Abbas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) was asked about a matter and it was in the Qur’an, he would inform us about it. If it was not in the Qur’an and it was from the Apostle of Allah (may Allah’s prayers and peace be upon him), he would inform us about it. If it was not, then it was from Abu Bakr and Umar (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)If not, he will say what he thinks about it.

Muhammad ibn Uyaynah informed us, on the authority of Ali ibn Mushir, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Shurayh: That ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab wrote to him: “If something comes to you in the Book of Allah, then judge according to it and do not let men distract you from it. If something comes to you that is not in the Book of Allah, then look to the Sunnah of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  and judge according to it. If something comes to you that i s not in the Book of Allah, then look at the Sunnah of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) and judge according to it. The Book of Allah, and there is no Sunnah of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) then look at what the people have agreed upon and accept it. If something comes to you that is not in the Book of Allah, and was not in the Sunnah of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) and no one before you spoke about it, then choose whichever of the two matters you want: If you want to exert your own opinion and then move forward So go ahead, and if you want to stay behind,  then stay behind, and I do not see that staying behind is anything but good for you.”

Yahya ibn Hammad narrated to us, Shu`bah narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Ubayd Allah ath-Thaqafi, on the authority of al-Harith ibn `Amr, the nephew of al-Mughirah ibn Shu`bah, on the authority of some people from Hims, from the companions of Mu`adh  (رضئ تعالی عنه) on the authority of Mu`adh, that when the Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  sent him to Yemen, he said: “If a case is presented to you, how will you judge?” He said: I judge by the Book of Allah. He said, “And if it is not in the Book of Allah?” He said, “Then by  the Sunnah of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) He said, “And if it is not in the Sunnah of the Apostle of Allah?” He said, “I will exert my best judgment and not spare any effort.” He said, “Then he struck his chest and then said, ‘Praise be to Allah, who has guided the messenger of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  to that which pleases the Apostle of Allah.’”

Yahya ibn Hammad informed us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of `Amara ibn `Umayr, on the authority of Hurayth ibn Zuhayr, who said: I think that `Abdullah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) said: “A time has passed over us and we were not asked, and we are not there. Allah has decreed that I should attain what you see. So, if you are asked about something, then look in the Book of Allah. If you do not find it, In the Book of Allah, then in the Sunnah of the Apostle of Allah. If you do not find it in the Sunnah of the Apostle of Allah, then in that upon which the Muslims have agreed. If it is not among that upon which the Muslims have agreed, then strive for your opinion, and do not say: I fear and I dread. For what is lawful is clear, and what is unlawful is clear, and betwee n them are matters of doubt. So, leave that which makes you doubt for that which is not. “He is suspicious.” Yahya ibn Hammad narrated to us, on the authority of Abu ‘Awanah, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of ‘Amara ibn ‘Umayr, on the authority of ‘Abd al -Rahman ibn Yazid, on the authority of ‘Abdullah, something similar. ‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad informed us, Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of al -Qasim ibn ‘Abd al -Rahman, on the authority of his father, on  the authority of ‘Abdullah, something similar.

Harun ibn Mu’awiyah informed us, on the authority of Hafs ibn Ghiyath, who narrated to us from al-A’mash, who said: Abdullah said: “O people, you will innovate, and something will be innovated for you. So, if you see something new, then you should adopt the first course of action.” Hafs said: I used to narrate from Habib, on the authority of Abu Abd al -Rahman, then I became doubtful about it.

Muhammad ibn al-Salt informed us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Muhammad, who said: Umar said to Ibn Mas`ud: “Have I not been informed, or have I not been informed, that you issue fatwas, although you are not an emir? Whoever takes charge of its harem should be appointed to its qaris.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: “The one who gives fatwas to people on every matter for which they are asked is insane.”

Said ibn Amir informed us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of Hudhayfah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: "Only three people give fatwas to the people: a man who is an Imam or a governor, a man who knows what has abrogated the Quran from what has been abrogated." They said: "O Hudhayfah (رضئ  اللہ  تعالی  عنه) and who is that?" He said: "Umar ibn al-Khattab (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)or an ignorant, pretentious person." 73

Abdullah ibn Saeed informed us, Abu Usamah informed us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Hassan, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah ibn Hudhayfah, who said: Hudhayfah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) said: “One of three people can issue fatwas to the people: a man who knows the abrogating verses of the Qur’an from the abrogated ones.” They said: “Who is that?” He said: “Umar ibn al-Khattab (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)He said: “And a ruler who finds no alternative, or…” “A pretentious fool,” then Muhammad said: “I am not one of these two, and I hope that I will not be the third.”

Jafar ibn Awn informed us, on the authority of al -Amash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: "Whoever among you has knowledge, let him speak about it, and whoever does not know, let him say ab out that which he does not know: Allah knows best. For when the scholar is asked about that which he does not know, he says: Allah knows best. And Allah said to His Apostle: Say: I do not ask of you for it any reward, nor do I ask of you for it." I am one of the pretenders. Surah Sad, verse 86

Yazid ibn Harun informed us, Humayd narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Abu al -Muhallab, that Abu Musa  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  said in his sermon: “Whoever learns knowledge, let him teach it to the people, and beware of saying what he has no knowledge of, lest he abandon the religion and become one of the imaginary ones.”

Amr ibn Awn informed us, on the authority of Khalid ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Abu al -Bakhtari and Zadan, who said: Ali  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  said: “How cool it is for the liver when I am asked about something I do not know, that I say: Allah knows best.”

Abu Nu`aym informed us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Abu al-Bakhtari, on the authority of Ali (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “How cool it is for the liver to say about what you do not know: ‘Allah knows best.’”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Umair ibn Urfajah informed us, Razin Abu al -Numan informed us, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  who said: "If you are asked about something you do not know, then flee." They said: "How do you flee, O Commander of the Faithful?" He said: "You say: Allah knows best."

Muhammad ibn Humayd informed us, Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Muslim al-Bateen, on the authority of Azra al -Tamimi, who said: Ali  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) said: “And its coolness on the liver, three times.” They said: “What is that, O Commander of the Faithful?” He said: “That a man is asked about something he does not know, and he says: Allah knows best.” 75

Farwah ibn Abi al-Maghra’ informed us, Ali ibn Mushir informed us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Umar  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  that a man asked him about a matter, and he said: “I have no knowledge of it.” When the man turned away, Ibn Umar said: “What an excellent statement Ibn Umar made! He was asked about something he did not know, and he said: “I have no knowledge of it.”
Yahya bin Hammad told us, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: “I do not know is half of knowledge.”

Abdullah ibn Maslama informed us, Abdullah al -Umari narrated to us, on the authority of Nafi’, that a man came to Ibn Umar asking him about something, so he said: “I have no knowledge.” Then he turned around after the man had left and said: “What an excellent statement Ibn Umar has made! He is being asked about something he has no knowledge of.” So he said: “I have no knowledge,” meaning Ibn Umar himself.

Muhammad ibn Humayd told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, who said: “Whenever Amir was asked about something, he would say: I do not know. If they answered him, he would say: If you wish, I would swear to you by Allah if I had knowledge of it.” 76

Harun ibn Muawiyah informed us, on the authority of Hafs, on the authority of Ashath, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, who said: "I do not care whether I am asked about what I know or what I do not know, because when I am asked about what I know, I say what I know, and when I am asked about what I do not know, I say: I do not know."

Harun narrated to us, on the authority of Hafs, on the authority of Al-A’mash, who said: “I never heard Ibrahim say: ‘It is lawful and not unlawful.’ Rather, he used to say: ‘They disliked it, and they preferred it.”

Ya`la informed us, Al-A`mash narrated to us, on the authority of Shaqiq, who said: `Abdullah said: “How will you be when you are afflicted with a trial in which the elderly grow old and the young grow, and the people take it as a Sunnah, but when it is changed, they say: The Sunnah ha s been changed.” They said: “When will that be, O Abu `Abd ar-Rahman?” He said: “When your reciters become numerous and your Your jurists have become numerous, your leaders have become numerous, your trustees have become few, and the world has been sought through the work of the Hereafter.”

Amr ibn Awn informed us, on the authority of Khalid ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: “How will you be when you are afflicted with a trial in which the old will grow old and the young will grow old? If something of it is abandoned, it will be said: ‘The Sunnah has been abandoned.’ They said: ‘When will that be?’ He said: ‘When your scholars are gone.” Your ignorant people have increased, your reciters have increased, your scholars have decreased, your leaders have increased, your trustworthy people have decreased, and the world has been sought through the work of the Hereafter, and knowledge has been acquired for other than religion.

Abu al-Mughira informed us, al-Awza’i told us, he said: I was informed that it was said: “Woe to those who pursue jurisprudence for purposes other than worship, and those who make permissible what is forbidden by doubtful matters.”

Salih ibn Suhayl, the freed slave of Yahya ibn Abi Zaydah, told us: Yahya told us, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of Ash -Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  who said: “No year will come upon you except that it is worse than the one before it. I do not mean one year more fertile than another, nor one ruler better than another, but rather your scholars and the best of you.” Your jurists will go away, and you will not find any successors among them. Then people will come who will judge matters by their own opinions.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Khalaf informed us, Yahya ibn Sulaym told us, he said: I heard Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, he said: “The first one to make an analogy was Iblis, and the sun and moon were not worshipped except by analogy.” 78

Muhammad ibn Kathir told us, on the authority of Ibn Shawdhab, on the authority of Matar, on the authority of Al -Hasan, that he recited this verse: “You created me from fire and created him from clay.” Surah Al-A’raf, verse 12. He said: “Iblis made a compa rison, and he was the first to make a comparison.”

Amr ibn Awn informed us, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Abi Khalid, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, that he said: “I fear, or I fear that I will measure, and my foot will slip.”

Sadaqah ibn al-Fadl informed us, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said: “By Allah, if you were to adopt analogies, you would forbid what is permissible and permit what is forbidden.”

Al-Hasan bin Bishr told us, my father told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Amir, that he said: He used to say: “What I hate most is, ‘What do you think?’ What do you think? A man asks his companion, saying, ‘What do you think?’ And he did not make comparisons.” 79
Sadaqah ibn al-Fadl told us, Yahya ibn Sa`id told us, on the authority of al-Zubayr, who said: “Abu Wa’il forbade me from sitting with the companions of ‘Have you seen?’”

Sadaqah ibn al -Fadl informed us, Ibn Uyaynah informed us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of al -Sha’bi, who said: “If these people had been alive during the time of the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) the general meaning of the Qur’an would have been revealed: ‘They ask you, they ask you.’”

Ismail ibn Aban informed us, Muhammad - he is Ibn Talha - informed me, on the authority of Maimun Abu Hamza, who said: Ibrahim said to me: “O Abu Hamza, by Allah, I have spoken, and if I had found a way out, I would not have spoken. The time in which I am the jurist of the people of Kufa is a time of evil.”
Abu Nu`aym informed us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Umar (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) said: “Beware of measuring by measure,” meaning: in speech.

Hajjaj al-Basri informed us, Abu Bakr al-Hudhali narrated to us, on the authority of al-Shabi, who said: "I witnessed Shurayh when a man from Murad came to him and said: O Abu Umayyah, what is the blood money for the fingers? He said: Ten by ten. He s aid: Glory be to Allah, are these two the same? He combined the little finger and the thumb. Shurayh said: Glory be to Allah, are your ear and your hand the same? For the ear is covered by hair, and the sleeve and turban are worth half of the blood mon ey, and the hand is worth half of the blood money. Woe to you! The Sunnah preceded your analogy, so follow it and do not innovate, for you will not go astray as long as you adhere to the tradition. Abu Bakr said: Al-Sha’bi said to me: O Hudhaili, if your Ahnaf had been killed while this child was in his cradle, would their blood money be equal to the amount of the blood money? Equally? I said: Yes. He said: “Then where is the analogy?

Marwan ibn Muhammad informed us, Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Rabi’ah ibn Yazid, who said: Mu’adh ibn Jabal (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) said: “The Qur’an will be opened to the people until a woman, a child, and a man read it. A man will say, ‘I read the Qur’an, but I was not followed. By Allah, I will stand up to teach it among them so that I may be followed.’ Then he will stand up to teach it among them, but it will not be followed. Then he will say: I recited the Qur’an but was not followed, and I led it among them but was not followed. I will certainly prepare a mosque in my house so that I may be followed. Then he prepares a mosque in his house but is not followed, so he says: I recited the Qur’an but was not followed, and I led it among them but was not followed, and I prepared a mosque in my house but was not followed. By Allah, I will bring them a hadith that they will not find in the Book of Allah, and they did not hear it from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)so that I might be followed. Muadh said: “Then beware of what he brought, for what he brought is misguidance.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Malik - he is Ibn Mughul - told us: Al -Shabi said to me: "Whatever these people tell you from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم ) take it, and whatever they say based on their own opinion, throw it in the trash can."

Al-Abbas ibn Sufyan informed me, on the authority of Zayd ibn Hubab, who said: Raja’ ibn Abi Salamah informed me, saying: I heard Abdah ibn Abi Lubabah say: “I am satisfied with these people of my time, that they do not ask me, and I do not ask them. Rather, one of them says, ‘What do you think? What do you think?’

Affan informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, Asim ibn Bahdalah told us, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) drew a line for us one day, then he said: “This is the path of Allah.” Then he drew lines to his right and to his left, then he said: “These are paths, on each of which is a devil.” He calls to it, then he recited: “And that this is My path, which is straight, so follow it and do not follow [other] paths, for they will separate you from His path.” Surah Al-An’am, verse 153

Muhammad ibn Yusuf told us, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid: “And do not follow the ways of innovations and doubts.” Surah Al-An’am, verse 153. He said: “Innovations and doubts.”

Al-Hakam ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Amr ibn Yahya informed us, he said: I heard my father narrating, on the authority of his father, he said: We used to sit at the door of Abdullah ibn Mas`ud (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) before the dawn prayer, and when he came out, we would walk with him to the mosque. Then Abu Musa al -Ash`ari (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  came to us and said: Abu Abdur -Rahman after that? We said: No. So, he sat with us until he left. When he left, we all stood up to him. Abu Musa said to him: O Abu Abdur -Rahman, I saw in the mosque just now something that I disapproved of, but I did not see, praise be to Allah, except good. He said: What was it? He said: If you live, you will see it. He said: I saw in the mosque some people sitting in circles. They wait for the prayer, and in each circle, there is a man, and in their hands are pebbles. He says: “Glorify Allah” one hundred times, and they say “Allah is great” one hundred times. He says: “Praise Allah” one hundred times, and they say “There is no God but Allah” one hundred times. He says: “Glorify Allah” one hundred times, and they say “Glorify Allah” one hundred times. He said: “What did you say to them?” He said: “I did not say anything to them, waiting for your opinion or your command.” He said: “Why didn’t you order them to count?” Their bad deeds, and you guaranteed them that none of their good deeds would be lost? Then he went on, and we went with him until he came to one of those circles. He stopped among them and said, “What is this that I see you doing?” They said, “O Abu Abd al -Rahman, pebbles with which we count our takbir, tahlil, and tasbih.” He said, “Then count your bad deeds, for I guarantee that none of your good deeds will be lost. Woe to you, O nation of Muhammad! How swiftly you will perish!” These are the Companions of your Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  in abundance. These are his clothes that have not worn out, and his utensils that have not been broken. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, you are either on a religion that is more guided than the religion of Muhammad, or you are opening the door to misguidance.” They said: “By Allah, O Abu Abd al-Rahman, we only wanted good.” He said: “And how many a person  wants good but will never attain it? Indeed, The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) told us that there are people who recite the Qur’an, but it does not go beyond their collarbones. By Allah, I do not know, perhaps most of them are from among you. Then he turned away from them, and Amr ibn Salamah said: We saw most of those circles fighting us on the Day of Nahrawan along with the Khawarij.

Ya`la informed us, Al-A`mash told us, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Abu Abd al- Rahman, who said: Abdullah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  said: “Follow, and do not innovate, for you have been sufficed.”

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Khalaf informed us, Yahya ibn Sulaym informed us, Ja’far ibn Muhammad informed me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah al- Ansari (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم ) addressed us, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: “The best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  and the worst guidance is the guidance of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)All matters are newly invented, and every innovation is misguidance.

Muhammad ibn Uyaynah informed us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, on the authority of Aslam al-Minqari, on the authority of Bilad ibn Ismah, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Mas`ud (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) say: When it was the evening of Thursday, the night of Friday, he would stand and say: “The most truthful speech is the speech of Allah Almighty, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)And peace be upon him, and the wretched one is he who was wretched in his mother’s womb, and the worst of stories are the stories of lies, and the worst of matters are their innovations, and everything that is coming is near.”

Muhammad ibn Uyaynah informed me, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al -Fazari, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Ayyub, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, who said: “No man takes up an innovation and then turns back to the Sunnah.”

Sulayman ibn Harb informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Ayyub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Abu Asma’, on the authority of Thawban  (رضئ تعالی عنه) on the authority of the Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  that he said: “I only fear for my nation the misguiding Imams.”

Ahmad ibn Abdullah Abu al-Walid al-Harawi informed us, Muadh ibn Muadh narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Amr ibn Sa`id, on the authority of Abu Zur`ah ibn Amr ibn Jarir, on the authority of Hayyah bint Abi Hayyah, who said: A  man entered upon us at noon, so I said: O Abdullah, where have you come from? He said: I came with a friend of mine for our prostitution. My companion set out seeking, and I entered to seek shade and drink from the drink. I went to a sour labneh (a kind o f milking vessel) - or perhaps she said: I went to a sour milking vessel - and gave him some to drink from, so he drank, and I drank. She said: I looked at him and said: O servant of Allah, who are you? He said: I am Abu Bakr. I said: You are Abu Bakr, the companion of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)What did you hear about?" He said, "Yes." She said, "Then I remembered our campaign against Khatham, and our campaign against each other during the pre -Islamic period, and what Allah brought of unity and tent ropes." Ibn Awn interlocked his fingers, and Muadh described it to us, and Ahmad interlock ed his fingers. I said, "O Abdullah, until when will you see this situation of the people?" He said: “The Imams have not been upright.” I said: “What are the Imams?” He said: “Have you not seen the Master being in the hollow and they following Him and obeying Him? So those have not been upright.” 85

Muhammad ibn al-Salt informed us, Ibrahim ibn Sa`d told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of a brother of `Adi ibn Artah, on the authority of Abu al-Darda`, who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: “What I fear most for you are the misguiding imams.”

Abu al-Numan informed us, Abu Awanah told us, on the authority of Bayan ibn Bishr, on the authority of Qais ibn Abi Hazim, who said: Abu Bakr  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  entered upon a woman from Ahmas called Zaynab. He said: He saw that she was not speaking, so he said: "Why is she not speaking?" They said: "She intended to perform Hajj silently." So he said to her: "Speak, for this one does not..." It is permissible. Th is is from the deeds of the Jahiliyyah.” He said: “So she spoke and said: Who are you? He said: I am a man from the Muhajireen. She said: From which of the Muhajireen? He said: From Quraysh. She said: From which Quraysh a re you? He said: You are a questioner. I am Abu Bakr. She said: How long will we remain upon this righteous matter that Allah brought after the Jahiliyyah? He said: You will remain upon it as long as your leaders are steadfast with you. She said: And what are the leaders? He said: Didn’t your people have leaders and nobles who would command them and they would obey them? She said: Yes. He said: They are like those among the people.

Abdullah ibn Muhammad informed us, Abd al -Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Wasil, on the authority of a woman called A’idhah, who said: I saw Ibn Mas’ud  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه ) advising men and women, and saying: “Whoever among you, whether a woman or a man, has reached puberty, then take the first path, for you are upon the fitrah.” Abdullah said: The path is the way. 86

Muhammad ibn Uyaynah informed us, Ali ibn Mushir informed us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Shabi, on the authority of Ziyad ibn Hudayr, who said: Umar said to me: Do you know what destroys Islam? I said: No. He said: “It is destroyed by the slip of a scholar, the argument of a hypocrite with the Book, and the judgment of misguiding imams.”

Harun informed us, on the authority of Hafs ibn Ghiyath, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ali, who said: “Do not sit with those who engage in disputes, for they engage in arguments about the verses of Allah.”

Al-Husayn ibn Mansur informed us, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Mubarak, on the authority of Al -Hasan, who said: “Your Sunnah, by Allah, besides whom there is no Allah, is between them: between the one who is excessive and the one who is harsh. So be patient with it, may Allah have mercy on you, for the people of the Sunnah were the fewest of people in the past, and they are the fewest of people in what remains: those who did not go with the people of luxury in Their lu xury, nor with the people of innovations in their innovations, and they were patient in their Sunnah until they met their Lord, so likewise you, Allah willing, so be

Musa ibn Khalid informed us, ‘Isa ibn Yunus told us, on the authority of al -A’mash, on the authority of ‘Umarah and Malik ibn al-Harith, on the authority of ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, on the authority of ‘Abdullah  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  who said: “Moderation in following the Sunnah is better than striving in innovation.”

Mansur ibn Salamah al-Khuzai informed us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: "I knew people who, if one of them had not gone beyond a fingernail, I would not have gone beyond it. It is enough of a disgrace for a people that their actions are contrary to theirs."

Ya`la informed us, `Abd al -Malik told us, on the authority of `Ata`: “Obey Allah and obey the Apostle and those in authority among you.” Surah An -Nisa, verse 59. He said: “Those of knowledge and understanding, and obedience to the Apostle: following the Book and the Sunnah.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Ibrahim ibn Adham told us, he said: I asked Ibn Shubrumah about something, and I had a difficult question, so I said: May Allah have mercy on you, look into it, he said: “If the path is made clear to me, and I find the trace, I will not detain.”

Uthman ibn al-Haytham informed us, Awf told us, on the authority of a man called Sulayman ibn Jabir from the people of Hajar, who said: Ibn Mas`ud said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said to me: “Learn knowledge and teach it to the people. Learn the inheritance laws and teach them to the people. Learn the Qur’an and teach it to the people, for I am a man who will be taken away, and knowledge…” It will decrease and tribulations will appear until two people differ over an obligation and they will not find anyone to decide between them.

Yaqub ibn Ibrahim informed us, Umar ibn Abi Khalifa told us, he said: I heard Ziyad ibn Mikhraq mention, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) he said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آلهوسلم)  sent Muadh ibn Jabal and Abu Musa to Yemen, and he said: “Support each other and cooperate, and give good tidings and do not scare away.” So, they arrived in Yemen, and Muadh addressed the people. So, he urged them to embrace Islam and ordered them to study the Qur’an, saying: “When you do that, ask me and I will tell you who are the people of Paradise and who are the people of Hellfire.” So, they stayed for as long as Allah willed them to stay. Then they said to Mu’adh: “You had ordered us, when we studied and recited, to ask you and you would tell us who are the people of Paradise and who are the people of Hellfire.” So, he said to them: Muadh: If a man is mentioned in a good way, he is one of the people of Paradise, and if he is mentioned in a bad way, he is one of the people of Hell.

Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Yahya ibn Said al-Qattan narrated to us, on the authority of Ubaydullah, who said: I heard Said ibn Abi Said narrating, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  who said: It was said: O Apostle of Allah (صلى علیه و  آله وسلم) which of the people is the most honorable? He said: "The most righteous of them." They said: "We are not asking you about this." He said: "Then Yusuf ibn Yaqub, the Prophet of Allah Son of the Prophet of Allah, son of the Friend of Allah. They said: We are not asking you about this. He said: “Then you are asking me about the mines of the Arabs? The best of them in the Age of Ignorance are the best of them in Islam if they understand.” 89

Abdullah ibn Salih informed us, Al -Layth told me, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn Usamah ibn Al-Hadi, on the authority of Abdul-Wahhab, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Humayd ibn Abdul -Rahman, on the authority of Muawiyah  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  who said: I heard the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) say: “Whoever Allah wants good for, He grants him understanding of the religion.”

Sa`id ibn Sulayman informed us, on the authority of Isma`il ibn Ja`far, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn Sa`id ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  said: “Whoever Allah wants good for, He grants him understanding of the religion.”

Yazid ibn Harun informed us, Hammad ibn Salamah informed us, on the authority of Jabalah ibn Atiyyah, on the authority of Ibn Muhayriz, on the authority of Muawiyah, who said: I heard the Apostle of Allah  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم ) say: “Whoever Allah wants good for, He gives him understanding of the religion.”

Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Zahrani informed us, Ismail ibn Ja`far informed us, `Amr ibn Abi `Amr informed us, on the authority of `Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Huwayrith, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut`im, on the authority of his father (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) that he witnessed the sermon of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) on the Day of `Arafah during the Farewell Pilgrimage: “O people, I By Allah, I do not know if I will meet you again after this day in this place of mine. May Allah have mercy on whoever hea rd my words today and understood them. Many a person carries knowledge but does not have knowledge of it, and many a person carries knowledge to someone who is more knowledgeable than him. Know that your wealth and your blood are sacred to you, just as sacred as this day, in this month, in this country. Know that Hearts do not deprive oneself of three things: sincerity in one’s actions for the sake of Allah, giving sincere advice to those in authority, and adherence to the Muslim community, for their suppli cation encompasses them from behind them.

Ahmad ibn Khalid informed us, Muhammad - he is Ibn Ishaq - told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut’im, on the authority of his father, who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) stood in al-Khaif in Mina and said: “May Allah make the radiant the soul of a servant who hears my words, remembers them, and then conveys them to someone who did not hear them. Many a bearer of knowledge has no knowledge, and many a bearer of knowledge h as no knowledge.” Three things that the heart of the believer will not be deceived by: Sincerity in action for the sake of Allah, obedience to those in authority, and adherence to the group, for their call will be behind them.

Ismah ibn al-Fadl informed us, Harami ibn Umarah told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Umar ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Aban ibn Uthman, on the authority of his father, who said: Zayd ibn Thabit left Marwan ibn a l-Hakam at noon. He said: I said, “He did not leave Marwan at this hour except that he had asked him about something.” So I came to him and asked him, and he said: Yes, he asked me about a hadith that I heard from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آلهوسلم) He said: “May Allah make radiant the face of a man who hears a hadith from us, memorizes it, and conveys it to someone who has memorized it better than him. Many a bearer of knowledge is not a scholar, and many a bearer of knowledge conveys it to someone who has more knowledge than him. The heart of a Muslim does not believe in three things except that he will enter Paradise: He said: I said: What are they? He said: Sincerity in action for the sake of Allah, sincere advice to those in authority, and adherence to the community, for their supplication encompasses them from behind them. Whoever’s intention is the Hereafter, Allah will make his richness in his heart, and gather his affairs for him, and the world will come to him reluctantly. Whoever’s int ention is the world, Allah will scatter his affairs and make his poverty between them. His eyes, and nothing came to him from this world except what was decreed for him.” He said: “And I asked him about the middle prayer. He said: It is the noon prayer.”

Yahya ibn Musa informed us, Amr ibn Muhammad al -Qurashi informed us, Isra’il informed us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Zubayd al-Yami, on the authority of Abu al-Ajlan, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’ (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) addressed us and said: “May Allah make radiant a man who hears a hadith from us and conveys it as he heard it, for many a conveyor is more retentive than one who conveys it.” Listen, there are three things that a Muslim’s heart will not be deceived about: doing one’s work sincerely for th e sake of Allah, giving sincere advice to every Muslim, and adhering to the Muslim community, for their supplication encompasses those behind them.

Muhammad ibn Isa informed us, Hisham informed us, Abu al-Zubayr informed us, on the authority of Jabir (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  said: “Whoever lies about me intentionally, let him take his seat in Hellfire.” 92

Muhammad ibn Isa informed us, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Abd al -A’la, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas  (رضئ اللہ تعالیعنه)  on the authority of the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) who said: “Whoever lies about me intentionally, let him take his seat in Hellfire.”

Abdullah ibn Salih informed us, Al-Layth told me, Yazid ibn Abdullah told me, on the authority of Amr ibn Abdullah ibn Urwah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Urwah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Az -Zubayr, on the authority of Az -Zubayr (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه )that he heard the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) say: “Whoever tells a lie about me, let him take his seat in Hellfire.”

Muhammad ibn Humayd informed us, Al-Sabbah ibn Muharib told me, on the authority of Umar ibn Abdullah ibn Ya’la ibn Murrah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, that the Apostle of Allah  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم ) said: “Whoever lies about me intentionally, let him take his seat in Hellfire.”

Asad ibn Musa informed us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of ‘Attab, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) say: Were it not that I feared making a mistake, I would have narrated to you things that I heard from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  or that the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said. That is because I heard him (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) say: “Whoever lies about me…” Deliberately, let him take his seat in Hellfire.”

Muhammad ibn Abdullah informed us, Abu Dawud informed us, on the authority of Shubah, on the authority of Abd al-Aziz, on the authority of Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, on the authority of al-Taymi, and on the authority of Attab, the freed slave of Ibn Hurmuz , that they heard Anas ibn Malik (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) on the authority of the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) that he said: "Whoever lies about me intentionally, let him take his seat in Hellfire."

Ahmad ibn Khalid informed us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq informed us, on the authority of Mabad ibn Kab, on the authority of Abu Qatada  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  who said: I heard the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) say on the pulpit: "O people, beware of talking too much about me. Whoever says something about me, let him say only what is true or honest. Whoever says something about me that I did not say, Let him take his seat in Hellfire.

Harun ibn Muawiyah informed us, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Asim al-Ahwal, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Bishr, on the authority of Anas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم ) said: "Whoever lies about me intentionally, let him take his seat in Hellfire." 94

Jafar ibn Awn informed us, Hisham informed us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr   (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: "Allah does not take away knowledge by snatching it away from the people, but the taking away of knowledge is the taking away of the scholars. So if He does not leave any scholar, the people will take ignorant people as leaders." They were asked, an d they gave fatwas without knowledge, so they went astray and led others astray.

Musa ibn Khalid informed us, Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman informed us, on the authority of al -Hajjaj, on the authority of al-Walid ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Malik, on the authority of al-Qasim Abu Abd al-Rahman, the client of Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, on the authority of Abu Umamah, on the authority of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  that he said: “Take knowledge before it disappears.” They said: How can it disappear? Knowledge, O Prophet of Allah, and we have the Book of Allah among us? He said: He  became angry, then said: “May your mothers lose you! Were not the Torah and the Gospel among the Children of Israel, so they did not benefit them at all? Indeed, the loss of knowledge is that its bearers are lost. Indeed, the loss of knowledge is that its bearers are lost.”

Abu al-Numan narrated to us, Thabit ibn Yazid narrated to us, Hilal - he is Ibn Khabab - narrated to us, he said: I asked Said ibn Jubayr, I said: O Abu Abdullah, what is the sign of the destruction of people? He said: "When their scholars perish." 95

Malik ibn Ismail informed us, Mas`ud ibn Sa`d al -Ju`fi told us, on the authority of `Ata` ibn al - Sa`ib, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn Rubay`ah, on the authority of Salman  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “People will continue to be well as long as the first generation remains, until they learn or teach the last.
