If the first generation perishes before the last generation can teach or learn, the people will perish.

Muhammad ibn al -Salt informed us, Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “Do you know what the loss of knowledge is?” We said: “No.” He said: “The loss of scholars.”

Muhammad ibn Asad informed us, Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Wail, who said: Hudhayfah  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه ) said: Do you know how knowledge decreases? I said: Just as a garment is dusted off, and just as a dirham hardens. He said: No, and that is from Him. The withholding of knowledge is the withholding of scholars.

Muhammad ibn al-Salt informed us, on the authority of Mansur ibn Abi al-Aswad, on the authority of Husayn, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al -Jad, on the authority of Abu al -Darda (رضئ تعالی عنه)who said: "Why do I see your scholars passing away while your ignorant people do not learn? Learn before knowledge is taken away, for the taking away of knowledge is the passing away of scholars." 96

Ahmad ibn Asad Abu Asim informed us, Abthar told us, on the authority of Burd, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Musa, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’ (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “People are scholars and learners, and there is no good in what comes after that.”

Ahmad ibn Asad Abu Asim informed us, Abthar told us, on the authority of Al -A’mash, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Abu Al -Darda’ (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “The one who teaches good and the one who seeks it are equal in reward, and there is no good after that for the rest of the people.”

Qabisah informed us, Sufyan informed us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “Be a scholar, a student, or a listener, but do not be the fourth, or you will perish.”

Amr ibn Awn informed us, Khalid informed us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al -Sa’ib, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Rubay’ah, who said: Salman  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه ) said: “People will continue to be well as long as the first ones remain, until the last ones learn. If the first ones perish before the last ones learn, then the people will perish.” 97
Wahb ibn Jarir and Uthman ibn Umar told us: Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of Al -Ahnaf, who said: Umar said: “Learn jurisprudence before you become leaders.”

Yazid ibn Harun informed us, Baqiyah informed us, Safwan ibn Rustum informed me, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Maysarah, on the authority of Tamim al -Dari (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: The people competed in building during the time of Umar  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  so Umar said: “O people of the Arabs, the land, the land, there is no Islam without a community, and there is no community without leadership.” There is no leadership except through obedience. So whoever is made a leader by his people based on knowledge, it will be a life for him and for them. And whoever is made a leader by his people based on something other than knowledge, it will be a destruction for him and for them.

Muhammad ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Baqiyah informed us, Sadaqah ibn Abdullah ibn Suhayb informed us, that al-Muhasir ibn Habib said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: Allah the Most High said: “I do not accept all the words of the wise, but I accept his concern and his desires. If his concern and his desires are in obedience to Me, I make his silence a praise to Me.” And dignity, even if he does not speak

Makhlad ibn Malik informed us, on the authority of Hajjaj ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Layth ibn Sad, on the authority of Muawiyah ibn Salih, on the authority of Abu al -Zahiriyyah, who traced the hadith back to the Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  that Allah said: "I will spread knowledge at the end of time until it is known to men and women, slaves and free people, young and old. When I do that with them, I will hold them accountable for My right over them."

Makhlad ibn Malik informed us, Makhlad ibn Husayn told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: “Whoever seeks something of this knowledge, seeking thereby what is with Allah, will attain it, Allah willing. But whoever seeks thereby the world, then that, by Allah, is his portion of it.”

Yala informed us, Muhammad ibn Awn narrated to us, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Isa, who said: Ibn Masud said: "Do not learn knowledge for three reasons: to argue with fools, to debate with scholars, to attract peoples attention, and to seek with your speech what is with Allah, for it is permanent and lasting, while everything else is lost."

And with this chain of transmission, he said: “Be springs of knowledge, lamps of guidance, lights of homes, lamps of the night, renewal of hearts, and well-mannered in clothing. You will be known among the people of heaven but hidden from the people of earth.” 99

Abu Asim informed us, Muhammad ibn ‘Umarah ibn Hazm informed us, ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abd al - Rahman informed me, he said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: No one seeks this knowledge, desiring nothing by it but this world, except that Allah will forbid him the fragrance of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection.

Mujahid ibn Musa informed us, Abdullah ibn Numayr informed us, on the authority of Malik ibn Mughul, who said: A man said to al-Sha’bi: Give me a fatwa, O scholar. He said: “The scholar is the one who fears Allah.”

Uthman ibn Umar informed us, Umar ibn Mazid told us, on the authority of Awfa ibn Dalham, that it reached him, on the authority of Ali (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “Learn knowledge, and you will be known by it, and act upon it, and you will be among its people, for after this there will come a time in which nine-tenths of them will not know what is right, and none will be saved from it except every sleeper, and those are the ones…” The imams of guidance and lamps of knowledge are not the Messiahs, nor the  gossipers. Abu Muhammad said: “Nu’mah is heedless of evil, the gossiper is a talkative person, and the gossipers are the slanderers.”

Marwan ibn Muhammad informed us, Saeed ibn Abd al -Aziz told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Jabir, who said: Muadh ibn Jabal  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  said: “Do whatever you wish after you have learned, for Allah Almighty will not reward you for knowledge until you act.”

Abdullah ibn Khalid ibn Hazim informed us, Al-Walid ibn Mazid told us, he said: I heard Abd al- Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir narrating, on the authority of Sa`d, that he came to Ibn Munabbih and asked him about al-Hasan, and said to him: How is his mind? So, he informed him, then he said: We are talking, or we find in the books that: “If Allah Almighty gives a servant knowledge and he acts upon it in the path of guidance, then He takes away his mind until Allah takes him to Himself.”

Ismail ibn Aban informed us, on the authority of Ibn al-Qasim ibn Qays, who said: Yunus ibn Saif al-Himsi told me, who said: Abu Kabsha al-Saluli told me, who said: I heard Abu al-Darda’ (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) say: “The worst of people in status before Allah on the Day of Resurrection will be a scholar whose knowledge is of no benefit to anyone.”

Amr ibn Awn informed us, Abu Qudamah informed us, on the authority of Malik ibn Dinar, who said: Abu Darda’ said: “Whoever increases in knowledge, increases in pain.” He informed us, and Abu Darda’ said: “I do not fear for myself that it will be said to me: You did not know, but I fea r that it will be said to me: What did you do?”

Harun ibn Mu’awiyah informed us, on the authority of Hafs ibn Ghiyath, who said: I heard Ibn Jurayj mentioning, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Ibn Abbas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: Studying knowledge for an hour at night is better than spending it all night praying.

Abu Hurairah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) told us that he said: “I divide the night into three parts: I sleep for a third, stand for a third, and remember the hadiths of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) for a third.”

Al-Hasan ibn Arafah informed us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al -Hasan ibn Amr, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: “Whoever seeks some knowledge, seeking thereby the Face of Allah, the Most High, Allah will give him from it what is sufficient for him.”

Abu al-Numan informed us, Thabit ibn Yazid told us, Asim told us, he said: I asked al -Shabi about a hadith, so he told it to me. I said: It is traced back to the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)He said: "No, for someone less than the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه وآله وسلم)  to narrate it is more beloved to us. But if there is an addition or omission in it, it is for someone less than the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه 102

Ishaq ibn Isa informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Abu Hashim, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: “The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) forbade muhaqala and muzabana.” It was said to him: “Do you not memorize a hadith from the Apostle of Allah (صلى علیه و آله وسلم) other than this?” He said: “Yes, but I say: ‘Abdullah said: ‘Alqamah said,’ is more beloved to me.”

Muhammad ibn Kathir informed us, on the authority of al -Awza’i, on the authority of Ismail ibn Ubayd Allah, who said: Whenever Abu al -Darda’ (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  narrated a hadith from the Apostle of Allah (blessings and peace of Allah be upon him), he would say: “This or something similar, or something similar to it.”

Asad ibn Musa informed us, Muawiyah informed us, on the authority of Rabi’ah ibn Yazid, who said: Whenever Abu al-Darda’ (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) narrated a hadith, he would say: “O Allah, except like this, or something similar to it.”

Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us, Ibn Awn informed us, on the authority of Muslim Abu Abdullah, on the authority of Ibrahim al -Taymi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Amr ibn 103 Maymun, who said: “I would not miss a Thursday evening without visiting Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, may Allah be pleased with him. I never heard him say anything about: The Apostle of Allah said, until one evening, He said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  said: His eyes welled up and his veins bulged, and I saw his buttons undone. And he said: Or something like it, or something similar, or something similar to it.

Yazid ibn Harun informed us, Ashath informed us, on the authority of Ash -Shabi and Ibn Sirin, that whenever Ibn Masud (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) narrated a hadith from the Apostle of Allah (blessings and peace of Allah be upon him) during the days, his face would turn red, and he would say: "Like this or something like that, like this or something like that."

Sahl ibn Hammad informed us, Shu’bah told us, Tawbah al -‘Anbari told us, he said: Ash -Sha’bi said to me: “What do you think of so-and-so who says: The Apostle of Allah said, The Apostle of Allah said? I sat with Ibn ‘Umar for two years, or a year and a half, and I did not hear him narrate anything from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) except this hadith.”

Asad ibn Musa informed us, Shu’bah informed us, Abdullah ibn Abi al-Safar informed us, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said: “I sat with Ibn Umar for a year, and I did not hear him mention a hadith from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)”.

Asim ibn Yusuf informed us, Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Ash-Sha’bi, on the authority of Thabit ibn Qutbah Al-Ansari, who said: “Abdullah (رضئتعالی عنه) used to narrate to us two or three hadiths a month.”

Uthman ibn Umar informed us, Yunus informed us, on the authority of Abd al -Malik ibn Ubayd, who said: Anas ibn Malik passed by us, so we said: Tell us some of what you heard from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)He said: “And I will be released from my state of ihram.”

Sulayman ibn Harb informed us, saying: Hammad ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Ibn ‘Awn, on the authority of Muhammad, who said: Anas  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  narrated from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) and whenever he narrated from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) he would say: “Or as the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said.”

Uthman ibn Muhammad informed us, Ismail told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Muhammad, who said: Anas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) narrated a hadith on the authority of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) in which he said: “Or as the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said:

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa`id, who said: As-Sa`ib ibn Yazid narrated to me, saying: I went out with Sa`d (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) to Mecca, and I did not hear him narrate a hadith from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) until we returned to Medina.

Sahl ibn Hammad informed us, Shu’bah told us, Bayan told us, on the authority of Ash-Sha’bi, on the authority of Qaraza ibn Ka’b: That ‘Umar (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) accompanied the Ansar when they left Medina, and he said: “Do you know why I accompanied you?” We said: “For the sake of the Ansar.” He said: “You are coming to a people whose tongues shake with the Qur’an like palm trees, so do not…” You repel them with the hadith of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) and I am your partner.” He said: “I did not narrate anything, and I heard as my companions heard.”

Yazid ibn Harun informed us, Ash’ath ibn Sawwar informed us, on the authority of Ash -Sha’bi, on the authority of Qurazah ibn Ka’b, who said: ‘Umar ibn Al -Khattab (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  sent a group of Ansar to Kufa, and he sent me with them. He walked with us until he came to a well on the road to Madinah, and he began to shake the dust off his feet, then he said: You come to Kufa and you come to a people who have a buzzing sound with the Qur’an. They come to you and say: The companions of Muhammad have arrived! The companions of Muhammad have arrived! They come to you and ask you about the hadith. Know that three complete ablutions are sufficient, and two are sufficient. Then he said: You come to Kufa, and you come to a people who have a buzzing sound With the Qur’an, and they say: The companions of Muhammad have arrived! The companions of Muhammad have arrived! So, they come to you and ask you about hadith, so reduce 106 the narrations from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) and I am your partner in it.” Qaraza said: “And I would sit among the people, and they would mention hadith from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) and I am from I memorized them for him, and when I mentioned the will of Umar (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  I kept silent. Abu Muhammad said: Its meaning, in my opinion, is the hadith from the days of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) not the Sunnah and the obligatory acts.

Mujahid ibn Musa informed us, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Malik ibn Mughul, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Alqamah, who said: Abdullah  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  said: “The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  said, then he trembled, then he said something like that or even more so.”

Bishr ibn al-Hakam informed us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: I accompanied Ibn Umar (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) to Madinah, and I did not hear him narrate a hadith on the authority of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) except that he said: I was with the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) and a burning coal was brought to him, and he said: “There are trees among which there is a tree the size of a man “The Muslim,” I wanted to say: “It is the palm tree,” but I looked and saw that I was the youngest of the people, so I remained silent. Umar (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) said: “I wish you had said it, and I have such and such.”

Bishr ibn al -Hakam informed us, Khalid ibn Yazid al -Haddadi informed us, Salih al -Dahhan informed us, he said: I never heard Jabir ibn Zayd say: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said, out of respect and fear that someone would lie about him. 107

Muhammad ibn Abdullah informed us, Rawh informed us, on the authority of Kahams ibn al - Hasan, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Shaqiq, who said: Abu Hurayrah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) came to Ka’b (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) asking about him, and Ka’b was among the people. Ka’b said: What do you want from him? He said: “As for me, I do not know of any of the companions of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) who had a better memory of his hadith than I.” Ka’b said: “You will not find anyone seeking something who will not be satisfied with it one day in this life, except a seeker of knowledge or a seeker of this world.” He said: “Are you Ka’b?” He said: “Yes.” He said: “For this reason I have come.”

Yaqub ibn Ibrahim informed us, Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr informed us, Shibl informed us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Tawus, who said: It was said: O Apostle of Allah, who is the most knowledgeable of people? He said: "He who combines the knowledge of the people with his own knowledge, and every seeker of knowledge is hungry for knowledge."

Said ibn Amir informed us, on the authority of Al -Khalil ibn Murrah, on the authority of Muawiyah ibn Qurrah, who said: "I was in a circle in which there were elders and they were discussing matters. Among them was Abid ibn Amr. A young man in a corner of the group said: Exhaust yourself in the remembrance of Allah, may Allah bless you. The people looked at each other, wondering what they saw us doing. Then some of them said: Who ordered you to do this? Go ahead, if you return, we will do it and we will do it. 108

Yusuf ibn Musa informed us, Abu Amir informed us, Qurrah ibn Khalid informed us, on the authority of Awn ibn Abdullah, who said: Abdullah said: “What an excellent assembly is an assembly in which wisdom is spread, and mercy is hoped for.”

Abdullah ibn Salih informed us, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr, on the authority of his father Jubayr ibn Nufayr, on the authority of Abu al -Darda’ (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: We were with the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) and he fixed his gaze upon the sky, then said: “This is the time when knowledge will be snatched away from the people, until they will not be able to gain anything from it.” Something. Ziyad ibn Labid al - Ansari said: O Apostle of Allah, how can it be stolen from us when we have recited the Quran? By Allah, we will recite it and teach it to our women and children. He said: May your mother lose you, O Ziyad! I used to count you among the scholars of Medina. This is the Torah and the Gospel according to the Jews and Christians, but what good will it do them? "Jubair said: So I met Ubadah ibn as-Samit, may Allah be pleased with him. He said: I said, Do you not hear what your brother Abu ad-Darda is saying? So I told him what he said. He said, Abu ad-Darda has spoken the truth. If you wish, I will tell you about the first knowledge to be taken away from the people: humility. You will soon enter the congregational mosque, and you will not see a single humble man in it."

Yaqub ibn Ibrahim informed us, Yazid ibn Harun informed us, Al -Walid ibn Jamil Al -Kattani informed us, Makhul informed us, he said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه وآله وسلم)  said: “The superiority of the scholar over the worshipper is like my superiority over the lowest of you.” Then 109 he recited this verse: “It is only those who have knowledge among His servants who fear Allah.” Surah Fatir, verse 28. Then he said: “Allah…” And His angels and the inhabitants of His heavens and His earth, and the Nun in the sea, send blessings upon those who teach people good.

Ahmad ibn Asad Abu Asim informed us, Yahya ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ibn Umar  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “A man is not a scholar until he does not envy those above him, nor does he look down on those below him, nor does he seek a price for his knowledge.”

Sa`id ibn Sulayman informed us, on the authority of Abu Usamah, on the authority of Mis`ar, who said: I heard `Abd al-A`la al-Taymi say: “Whoever has been given knowledge that does not make him cry is likely not to have been given knowledge that benefits him, because Allah the Most High described the scholars, then he recited: “Indeed, those who have been given knowledge weep” until His saying “they weep” (Surat al-Isra’, verse 107).

Ismah ibn al-Fadl informed us, Zayd ibn Hubab told us, on the authority of Mubarak ibn Fadalah, on the authority of Ubayd Allah ibn Umar al -Umari, on the authority of Abu Hazim, who said: “You will not be a scholar until you have three characteristics: you do not transgress against those above you, you do not belittle those below you, and you do not take worldly gain fo r your knowledge.”

Ahmad ibn Asad informed us, Abthar told us, on the authority of Burd ibn Sinan, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Musa al-Dimashqi, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’ (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: You will not be a scholar until you are a student, and you will not be a scholar of knowledge until you are an agent of it. It is enough sin for you that you continue to dispute, and it is enough sin for you that you continue to argue, and it is enough sin for you. It is a lie that you continue to narrate about things other than Allah.

Al-Hasan ibn Arafah informed us, Al -Mubarak ibn Saeed informed us, on the authority of his brother Sufyan Al-Thawri, on the authority of Imran Al-Minqari, who said: I said to Al-Hasan one day about something, and he said to him: O Abu Saeed, this is not what the jurists say. So he said: Woe to you! Have you ever seen yourself as a jurist? The jurist is the one who is ascetic in this world, desirous of the Hereafter, and discerning in the affairs of His religion, he who is persistent in worshipping his Lord.

Al-Hasan ibn Arafah informed us, Al -Nadr ibn Ismail Al-Bajali informed us, on the authority of Mis`ar, on the authority of Sa`d ibn Ibrahim, who said: It was said to him: Who is the most knowledgeable of the people of Madinah? He said: “The one who is most pious to his Lord.”
Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us, Al-Husayn bin Ali told us, on the authority of Layth bin Abi Sulaym, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: “The jurist is the one who fears Allah Almighty.” 111

Ismail ibn Abaan informed us, on the authority of Yaqub al -Qummi, who said: Layth ibn Abi Sulaym told me, on the authority of Yahya - he is Ibn ‘Abbad - on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  who said: “The true faqih is he who does not make people despair of Allah’s mercy, nor does he permit them to disobey Allah, nor does he give them security from Allah’s punishment, nor does he abandon the Qur’an.” Out of a desire to turn away from it to something else, for there is no good in worship without knowledge, no knowledge without understanding, and no reading without contemplation.

Al-Hasan ibn Arafah narrated to us, Ismail ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abbad, who said: Ali said: “The true faqih is the one who does not make people despair of Allah’s mercy, nor does he give them s ecurity from Allah’s punishment, nor does he give them permission to disobey Allah. Indeed, there is no good in worship without knowledge, and there is no good in knowledge without understanding, nor…” Better to read without contemplation

Abu al-Numan informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd informed us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Hazim, who said: My uncle Jarir ibn Zayd informed me that he heard Tubay narrating, on the authority of Kab, who said: "I find the description of a people who learn for other than action, and who acquire knowledge for other than worship, and who seek the world by working for the Hereafter, and who wear sheepskins, while their hearts are more bitter." From patience, so they are deceived by me, or they deceive me? So, I swore by me that I would surely bring upon them a trial that would leave the forbearing person bewildered.” 112

Bishr ibn al-Hakam informed us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Abd al-Samad al-Ammi told us, Abu Imran al- Jawni told us, on the authority of Harim ibn Hayyan, that he said: “Beware of the immoral scholar.” This news reached Umar ibn al-Khattab (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) so he wrote to him and was concerned about it. “What is the immoral scholar?” Harim wrote to him: “O Commander of the Faithful, By Allah, I only intended good for him: There will be an imam who speaks with knowledge, but acts with immorality, so he will make people mislead, and they will go astray.

Said ibn al-Mughira informed us, al -Walid ibn Muslim told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Mutarrif and Abd al-Aziz ibn Ismail ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Abi al-Muhajir, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Masud, who said: "Whoever wants his religion to be honored, let him not enter upon the ruler, let him not be alone with women, and let him not quarrel with the people of whims."

Said ibn Amir informed us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of Yunus, who said: Maymun ibn Mihran wrote to me: "Beware of quarreling and disputing about religion, and do not debate with a scholar or an ignorant person. As for the scholar, he withholds his knowledge from you and does not care what you do. As for the ignorance, he will make you feel harsh and will not obey you."

Abu Al-Mughira informed us, Al-Awza’i told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, who said: Sulayman bin Dawud, peace be upon him, said to his son: “Abandon disputation, for its benefit is little, and it incites enmity between brothers.”

Yahya ibn Hassan informed us, Abdullah ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Abi Hakim, who said: I heard Umar ibn Abd al -Aziz say: “Whoever makes his religion a target for disputes will move around a lot.”

Marwan ibn Muhammad informed us, Saeed ibn Abd al -Aziz told us, he said: Umar ibn Abd al - Aziz wrote to the people of Medina: “Whoever worships without knowledge, what he corrupts will be more than what he reforms. Whoever considers his speech as part of his deeds, his speech will be few except in what concerns him. Whoever makes his religion a target for disputes, his movement will be frequent.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Burqan, on the authority of Umar ibn Abd al -Aziz, who said: A man asked him about something related to his desires, so he said: “Adhere to the religion of the Bedouin and the young man in the school and forget about everything else.” Abu Muhammad said: He often changed opinions, meaning he would switch from one opinion to another. 114

Muhammad ibn Kathir told us, on the authority of al -Awza’i, who said: Umar ibn Abd al -Aziz said: “If you see a people who produce something that is not the case with their general public, then they are establishing misguidance.”

Ibrahim ibn Ishaq informed us, on the authority of Ibn al-Mubarak, on the authority of al-Awza’i, who said: “Iblis said to his followers: ‘From what source do you approach the children of Adam?’ They said: ‘From everything.’ He said: ‘Do you approach them by seeking forgiveness?’ They said: ‘Never!’ That is something that is linked to monotheism. He said: ‘I will surely spread among them something for which they will not seek forgiveness from Allah.” From him, he said: So, he spread desires among them.

Ibrahim ibn Ishaq informed us, on the authority of al-Muharibi, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: “I do not know which of the two blessings upon me is greater: that He guided me to Islam, or that He spared me from these desires.”

Musa ibn Khalid informed us, Isa ibn Yunus told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim al-A’war, on the authority of Hubbah ibn Juwayn, who said: I heard Ali, or he said: Ali (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) say: “If a man fasted his entire life and stood in prayer his entire life, then was 115 killed between the Corner and the Maqam, Allah would gather him on the Day of Resurrection with those who believe that he was on the right path.”

Muhammad ibn Humayd informed us, on the authority of Harun, who is the son of al -Mughirah, on the authority of Shu’ayb, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhayl, on the authority of Abu Sadiq, who said: Salman (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  said: “If a man were to place his head on the Black Stone, fast during the day, and pray at night, Allah would resurrect him on the Day of Resurrection with his desires.”

Muhammad ibn al -Salt informed us, Mansur, who is the son of Abi al -Aswad, told us, on the authority of al-Harith ibn Hasira, on the authority of Abu Sadiq al-Azdi, on the authority of Rabi’ah ibn Najidh, who said: Ali  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  said: “Be among people like the bee among birds. There is no bird that does not consider it weak, and if the bird knew what is in its interior of…” Blessing, they did not do that with it. Mix with people with your tongues and bodies, and separate from them with your deeds and hearts, for a person will get what he has earned, and on the Day of Resurrection he will be with those he loved.
Al-Walid bin Shuja’ informed us, Baqiya told me, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, who said: “The best minister of knowledge is good opinion.”

Ahmad ibn Abdullah informed us, Zaydah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Masruq, who said: “It is sufficient knowledge for a person that he fears Allah, and it is sufficient ignorance for a person that he is impressed by his knowledge.” He said: Masruq said: “It is true that a person should have gatherings in which he can be alone, remember his sins, and seek forgiveness from Allah, the Most High.” From it.

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Khalaf informed us, Man told me, on the authority of Muawiyah ibn Salih, on the authority of Al -Ala ibn Al-Harith, on the authority of Makhul, on the authority of Wathilah ibn Al -Asqa (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه ) who said: "If we narrate to you a hadith with its meaning, then that is sufficient for you."

Asim bin Yusuf informed us, Fadil bin Iyadh informed us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Ibn Sirin: “Whenever he narrated, he did not advance or delay, and whenever Al - Hasan narrated, he advanced or delayed.”
Muslim ibn Ibrahim told us, Jarir ibn Hazim told us, he said: “Al -Hasan used to narrate hadiths whose origin was the same, but whose words were different.”

Muhammad ibn Ahmad informed us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Suqah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn, who said: Ubayd ibn Umair told Abdullah ibn Umar (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه ) who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  said: “The example of a hypocrite is like that of a sheep between two pastures or between two sheep.” Ibn Umar said: “No, he only said so -and-so.” Likewise, he said: When Ibn Umar heard the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) he did not add to it, nor subtract from it, nor go beyond it, nor fall short of it.

Abdullah ibn Saeed informed us, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, who said: Al- Sha’bi, Al-Nakha’i, and Al-Hasan used to narrate a hadith one time like this and another time like that. I mentioned that to Muhammad ibn Sirin, and he said: “If only they ha d narrated it as they heard it, it would have been better for them.”

Muhammad ibn al -Ala’ informed us, ‘Uthman told us, on the authority of al -A’mash, on the authority of ‘Umara ibn ‘Umair, on the authority of Abu Ma’mar, who said: “I hear a hadith with a mistake, so I make a mistake in accordance with what I heard.”

Bishr ibn al-Hakam informed us, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Maysarah, who said: Mujahid saw a peacock in a dream, as if he were in the Kaaba praying, covering his face, and the Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  was at the door of the Kaaba. So he said to him: “O 118 servant of Allah, uncover your face and show your recitation.” He said: It was as if he interpreted it as knowledge, so he relaxed. After that in the hadith.

Abdullah ibn Muhammad informed us, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ibn Thawban, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Damrah, on the authority of Ka’b, who said: “The world is cursed, and everything in it is cursed, except the one who learns goodness or the one who teaches it.”

Muhammad ibn Kathir informed us, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Buhayr ibn Sa’d, on the authority of Khalid ibn Ma’dan, who said: “People are scholars and learners, and those in between are savages with no good in them.”

Bishr ibn al-Hakam informed us, Abdullah ibn Raja’ told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: They used to say: “The death of a scholar is a breach in Islam that nothing can fill as long as night and day alternate.”

" 119 Yusuf ibn Musa informed us, Ibrahim ibn Musa informed us, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Sanani informed us, Mundhir - he is Ibn al-Numan - informed us, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: "A gathering in which knowledge is disputed is dearer to m e than its value as a prayer, perhaps one of them will hear a word and benefit from it for a year, or for the remainder of his life."

" Yaqub ibn Ibrahim informed us, Wakee informed us, he said: Sufyan said: "I do not know of any deed better than seeking knowledge and memorizing it for whomever Allah the Most High intends good for." And he said: Al -Hasan ibn Salih said: "People need this  knowledge for their religion, just as they need food and drink for their worldly life."

Abu Nuaym and Jafar ibn Awn informed us: Misar narrated to us, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Jad, who said: Abu al-Darda (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) said: "Learn before knowledge is taken away, for the taking away of knowledge is the taking away of scholars, and the scholar and the student are equal in reward."

Harun ibn Muawiyah informed us, on the authority of Hafs ibn Ghiyath, on the authority of Abu Abdullah al-Khurasani, on the authority of al -Dahhak: “But be rabbis because you have been teaching the Scripture.” Surah Al Imran, verse 79. He said: “It is incumbent upon everyone who recites the Qur’an to be a faqih.”

Harun ibn Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Hafs, on the authority of Ash’ath ibn Sawwar, on the authority of Al-Hasan: “Why do not the rabbis and scholars forbid them?” Surah Al-Ma’idah, verse 63. He said: “The wise and knowledgeable.”

Muhammad ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, who said: “Be devout scholars.” Surah Al Imran, verse 79. He said: “Scholars and jurists.”
Ubaydullah ibn Sa`id told us: I heard Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah say: “Knowledge is sought through memorization, action, listening, paying attention, and dissemination.”

He said: Ahmad bin Muhammad Abu Abdullah informed me, on the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah, who said: “The most ignorant of people is he who abandons what he knows, and the most knowledgeable of people is he who acts upon what he knows, and the best of people is he who is most humble before Allah.”

Abdullah ibn Jafar al-Ruqi informed us, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Amr, on the authority of Zayd - he is the son of Abi Unaysah - on the authority of Sayyar, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: "Two greedy people will never be satisfied: one who is greedy for knowledge and will never be satisfied with it, and one who is greedy for this world and will never be satisfied with it. So whoevers concern, his worries, and his sorrows will be relieved of his loss by Allah, and his wealth will be placed in his heart." Whoevers concern, worries, and sorrow is the world, Allah will expose his loss to him and make his poverty before his eyes. Then he will not wake up except poor, and he will not go to bed except poor.

Jafar ibn Awn informed us, Abu Umais informed us, on the authority of Awn, who said: Abdullah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) said: "Two greedy people are never satisfied: the one with knowledge and the one with worldly life. They are not equal. As for the one with knowledge, his satisfaction with the Most Merciful increases, while as for the one with the worldly life, he persists in transgression." Then Abdullah recited: "No indeed! Indeed, Man is bound to transgress { 6} because he sees himself self -sufficient {7} Surah Al -Alaq, verses 6-7 #, He said: And the other said: # Only those fear Allah, from among His servants, who hav e knowledge. Surah Fatir, verse 28 #

Muhammad ibn Humayd informed us, Ibrahim ibn Mukhtar informed us, Simaak ibn Harb informed us, Ikrimah informed us, Ibn Abbas informed us, may Allah be pleased with them both: “Only those fear Allah, from among His servants, who have knowledge.” Surah Fatir, verse 28. He said: “Whoever fears Allah is knowledgeable.”

Ismail ibn Aban told us, Abdullah ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “Two greedy people are never satisfied: a seeker of knowledge and a seeker of this world.”

Marwan ibn Muhammad informed us, Yazid ibn Rabiah al-Sanani told us, Rabiah ibn Yazid told us, he said: I heard Wathilah ibn al -Asqa (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) say: The Apostle of Allah (blessings and peace of Allah be upon him) said: "Whoever seeks knowledge and attains it, will have a double reward. But if he does not attain it, he will have a single reward."

Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Shaybah informed us, Marwan ibn Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Abbas al -Ammi, who said: It has reached me that Prophet David (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  used to say in his supplication: “Glory be to You, O Allah, You are my Lord, You are exalted above Your Throne, and You have made Your fear over everyone in the heavens and the earth, so the closest of Your creation to You in status is…” Who among them fears You most? What is the knowledge of one who does not fear You? And what is the wisdom of one who does not obey Your command?!

Al-Mualla ibn Asad informed us, Sallam, who is the son of Abi Mutee, told us: I heard Abu al- Hizhaaz narrating, on the authority of al -Dahhak, who said: Abdullah ibn Masud  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) said: "Become a scholar or a student, for there is no good in anything other than them." 123

Al-Hakam ibn al-Mubarak informed us, al-Walid ibn Muslim informed us, al-Walid ibn Sulayman informed us, on the authority of Ali ibn Yazid, on the authority of al-Qasim Abu Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu Umamah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)on the authority of the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)who said: “There will be tribulations in which a man will be a believer in the morning and a disbeliever in the evening, except for the one whom Allah revives with knowledge.”

Abu Al-Mughira informed us, Al -Awza’i told us, Harun bin Ri’ab told me, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) that he used to say: “Go out in the morning as a scholar or a student, and do not go out in between, because what is in between is ignorance. The angels spread their wings for a man who goes out in the morning seeking knowledge out of satisfaction with what he does.”

Abu al-Mughira informed us, al-Awzai narrated to us, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) was asked about two men who were among the Children of Israel: One of them was a scholar who prayed the prescribed prayers, then sat and taught people good, and the other fasted during the day and prayed at night. Which of them was better? The Apostle of Allah  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم ) said: “The superiority of this scholar who prays the prescribed prayers and then sits and teaches people goodness over the worshipper who fasts during the day and stands in prayer at night is like my superiority over the lowest of you in rank.” 124

Al-Hasan ibn al-Rabi’ informed us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ubaydullah, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Dhakwan, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, who said: “I entered the mosque, and there was al-Aswad ibn Sari’ narrating, and Humayd ibn Abd al -Rahman discussing knowledge in a corner of the mosque. I turned towards which of the two I should sit, and I fell asleep. Then someone came to me and said: ‘You turned towards Which of the two will you sit on? If you wish, I will show you the place of Gabriel, peace be upon him, with Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman.”

Nasr ibn Ali informed us, Abdullah ibn Dawud told us, on the authority of Asim ibn Raja’ ibn Haywah, on the authority of Dawud ibn Jamil, on the authority of Kathir ibn Qays, who said: I was sitting with Abu al-Darda’ (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) in the mosque of Damascus, when a man came to him and said: O Abu al -Darda’, I have come to you from Medina, the city of the Apostle of Allah (may Allah’s prayers and peace be upon him). According to a hadith that reached me from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) he said: “What brought you here, trade?” He said: “No.” He said: “And nothing else brought you here?” He said: “No.” He said: “I heard the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  say: ‘Whoever takes a path in search of knowledge,  Allah will make easy for him a path to Paradise. The angels spread their wings in pleasure for the seeker of knowledge. ’” Knowledge, and the seeker of knowledge, everyone in the heavens and the earth, even the fish in the water, seeks forgiveness for him . The superiority of the scholar over the worshipper is like the superiority of the moon over the rest of the stars. The scholars are the inheritors of the prophets. The prophets did not leave behind dinars or dirhams, but they left behind knowledge. So whoever takes it, takes his portion, or a portion. Abundant

Muhammad ibn ‘Uyaynah informed us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al -Fazari, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Shimr ibn ‘Atiyyah, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “Everything seeks forgiveness for the one who teaches good, even the fish in the sea.”

Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus informed us, Zaydah told us, on the authority of al -A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم ) said: “There is no man who takes a path in search of knowledge, except that Allah will make easy for him a path to Paradise. And whoever is slowed down by his deeds, his lineage will not hasten him.” "

Ismail ibn Aban informed us, on the authority of Yaqub (he is al -Qummi), on the authority of Harun ibn Antara, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “No man takes a path in search of knowledge except that Allah makes easy for him a path to Paradise. And whoever is slowed down by his deeds, his lineage will not hasten him.”

Muhammad ibn Kathir informed us, on the authority of Ibn Shawdhab, on the authority of Mutar: “And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?” Surah Al-Qamar, verse 17. He said: “Is there one who seeks good s o that he may be aided in it?” Marwan informed us, on the authority of Damrah, who said: “A seeker of knowledge.”

Ismail ibn Aban informed us, Yaqub al-Qummi informed us, on the authority of Amir ibn Ibrahim, who said: Whenever Abu al-Darda’ (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) saw students of knowledge, he would say: “Welcome to students of knowledge.” And he would say: “The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) has recommended you.”

Abdullah ibn Yazid informed us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad ibn An’am told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Rafi’, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) that the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) passed by two gatherings in his mosque and said: “Both of them are doing good, and one of them is better than the other. As for these, they are supplicating.” Allah, and they desire Him, so if He wills He will give them, and if He wills, He will withhold from them. As for these, they learn jurisprudence and knowledge, and they teach the ignorant, so they are better. I was only sent as a teacher.” He said: Then he sat among them.

Abdullah ibn Yazid told us, Al -Mas’udi told us, on the authority of Awn ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Mutarrif ibn Abdullah ibn Ash-Shakhir, that he said to his son: “O my son, knowledge is better than action.”

Abdullah bin Yazid informed us, Haywah told us, Shurahbil bin Sharik told us that he heard Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hubbli say: “There is no gift better than a word of wisdom that you give to your brother.” 127

Abdullah ibn Imran informed us, Yahya ibn Yaman told us, Muhammad ibn Ajlan told us, on the authority of al -Zuhri, who said: “The superiority of the scholar over the diligent scholar is one hundred degrees, and the distance between the two degrees is five hundred years, the length of a fast, well-trained horse.”

Abdullah bin Yazid told us, Haywah told us, he said: As -Sakn bin Abi Karimah told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, by degrees.” Surah Al-Mujadila, verse 11. He said: “Allah will raise those who have been given knowledge, by degrees above those who have believed.”

Bishr ibn Thabit al-Bazzar informed us, Nasr ibn al-Qasim told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ismail, on the authority of Amr ibn Kathir, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  said: “Whoever is visited by death while he is seeking knowledge to revive Islam thereby, then between him and the Prophets is one degree in Paradise.”

Muhammad ibn Humayd informed us, Mihran informed us, Abu Sinan informed us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun, who said: “Umar took two-thirds of knowledge, so I mentioned it to Ibrahim, and he said: ‘Umar took nine-tenths of knowledge.

Bishr ibn Thabit informed us, Shu`bah informed us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Khalid, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “A group of people do not gather in one of the houses of Allah, discussing the Book of Allah and studying it among themselves, except that the angels shade them with their wings until they engage in another conversation. And whoever takes a path Whoever seeks knowledge through it, Allah will make his path to Paradise easy, and whoever is slowed d own by his deeds, his lineage will not hasten him.”

Amr ibn Asim informed us, Hammad - he is Ibn Salamah - told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, who said: I went out in the morning to Safwan ibn Assal al -Muradi, and I wanted to ask him about wiping over the socks. He said: What brought  you here? I said: Seeking knowledge. He said: Shall I not give you good news? I said: Yes. He said: He traced the hadith back to the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) He said: “The angels spread their wings for the seeker of knowledge, pleased with what he seeks.”

Abdullah ibn Imran informed us, Yahya ibn Yaman told us, he said: I heard Sufyan forty years ago, he said: “Seeking hadith has never been better than today.” They said to Sufyan: “They seek it without intention?” He said: “Their seeking it is with intention.” 129

Abdullah ibn Saeed informed us, Abdullah ibn al -Ajlah informed us, my father informed me, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: “We sought this knowledge without a great intention in it, then Allah later granted us intention in it.”

Bishr ibn Thabit al-Bazzar informed us, Hassan ibn Muslim told us, on the authority of Yunus ibn Ubayd, on the authority of al -Hasan, who said: “There were people who sought knowledge, but they did not seek by it Allah the Most High, nor what is with Him. So, knowledge continued with them until they sought by it Allah and what is with Him.”

" Sulayman ibn Harb informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Ayyub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, who said: Abu Muslim al -Khawlani said: “Scholars are of three types: a man who lived in his knowledge and the people lived with him in it, a  man who lived in his knowledge but no one lived with him in it, and a man in whose knowledge the people lived but it was a burden upon him.”

Ubaydullah ibn Musa informed us, on the authority of Uthman ibn al -Aswad, on the authority of Ata’, who said: Moses, peace be upon him, said: “O Lord, which of Your servants is the most just?” He said: “The one who judges for the people as he judges for himself.” He said: “O Lord, which of Your servants is the richest?” He said: “The one who is satisfied with what I have apportioned for him.” He said: “O Lord, wh ich of Your servants is the most fearful of You?” He said: “The most knowledgeable of them.” with me "

Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, on the authority of Sufyan, who said: “It was said that scholars are of three types: One who is knowledgeable about Allah and fears Allah, but is not knowledgeable about Allah’s commands; one who is knowledgeable about Allah and fears Allah, and that is the perfect scholar; and one who is knowledgeable about Allah’s commands but is not knowledgeable about Allah and does not fear Allah, and that is the wicked scholar.”

Makki ibn Ibrahim informed us, Hisham informed us, on the authority of al -Hasan, who said: “Knowledge is of two types: knowledge in the heart, and that is beneficial knowledge, and knowledge on the tongue, and that is Allah’s proof against the son of Adam.” Asim ibn Yusuf informed us, on the authority of Fudayl ibn ‘Iyad, on the authority of His ham, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) something similar to that.

Amr ibn Awn informed us, Khalid ibn Abdullah informed us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: “Learn, learn, and when you have learned, then act.” 131

Abu Ubaid al -Qasim ibn Sallam informed us, Abu Ismail, he is Ibrahim ibn Sulayman al- Mu’addib, told us, on the authority of Asim al -Ahwal, on the authority of the one who told him, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: “Whoever seeks knowledge for four reasons will enter Hellfire,” or something similar to this statement: to show off to scholars, to argue with fools, or to be diverted. To draw people’s attention to him, or to take it from the princes.”

Sa`d ibn Amir informed us, on the authority of Hisham, the companion of al-Dastawa`i, who said: I read in a book that reached me that it was from the words of Jesus, peace be upon him: “You work for this world, and you are provided for in it without workin g, and you do not work for the Hereafter, and you are not provided for in it except through working. Woe to you, scholars of evil: you take the reward, but you waste the work. The Lord of deeds is about to demand his deeds, and you are about to leave this vast world for the darkness and narrowness of the grave. Allah forbids you from sins, just as He has commanded you to pray and fast. How can one be among the people of knowledge who is dissatisfied with his provision and despises his status, knowing that t his is from Allah’s knowledge and power? How can one be among the people of knowledge who He accuses Allah of what He has decreed for him, yet is not satisfied with anything that befalls him. How can a person be among the people of knowledge if he prefers his worldly life to his Hereafter, while he has the best desire for this world? How can a person be among the people of knowledge if his destiny is his Hereafter, while he is focused on his worldly life, and what harms him is more desirable to him —or he co uld say, more beloved to him —than what benefits him? How can someone be a person of knowledge who seeks knowledge in order to convey it, but does not seek it in order to act upon it?

Ubaydullah ibn Abd al -Majid informed us, Hariz narrated to us, on the authority of Habib ibn Ubayd, who said: It used to be said: “Learn knowledge and benefit from it, and do not learn it to adorn yourselves with it, for it is likely that if you live long, the man of knowledge will adorn himself with his knowledge, just as the man of finery adorns himself with his finery.”

" Nuaym ibn Hammad informed us, Baqiyah narrated to us, on the authority of Al -Ahwas ibn Hakim, on the authority of his father, who said: A man asked the Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) about evil, so he said: “Do not ask me about evil, but ask me about good.” He said it three times, then he said: “Beware, the worst of evil are the worst of scholars, and the best of good are the best of scholars.”

Sa`id ibn `Amir informed us, Humayd ibn al -Aswad informed us, on the authority of `Isa, who said: I heard al-Sha`bi say: “This knowledge was sought only by one in whom two characteristics were combined: reason and devotion. If he was a devotional person but was not wise, he said: This is something that only wise people can attain, so he did not seek it. Even if he was wise but was not wise.” Ascetic, he said: This is something that only ascetics can attain. But he did not seek it. Al-Sha’bi said: I fear that it would be sought today by someone who does not have either of these two qualities: neither reason nor asceticism.
Abu Asim told us, he said: Sufyan claimed to me, he said: “A man would not seek knowledge until he had worshipped Allah for forty years before that.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Burd ibn Sinan Abu al-Ala’, on the authority of Makhul, who said: “Whoever seeks knowledge to dispute with fools, to show off to scholars, or to attract people’s attention to himself, will be in the fire of Hell.”

Yahya ibn Bastam informed us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Hamza, who said: An-Numan told me, on the authority of Makhul, who said: The Apostle of Allah  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم ) said: "Whoever seeks knowledge to show off to scholars, or to argue with fools, or to attract peoples attention, Allah will admit him to Hell."

Ismail ibn Aban informed us, Yahya ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Al-Minhal ibn Khalifa, on the authority of Matar Al-Warraq, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Ibn Abbas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “A man’s hadith is preserved according to the extent of his intention.”
Ya`la informed us, Al-Mas`udi told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim, who said: `Abdullah said to me: “I think that a man forgets the knowledge he used to have because of the sin he used to commit.”

Al-Hakam ibn Nafi’ informed us, Shu’ayb ibn Abi Hamza informed us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Husayn, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: It has reached me that Luqman the Wise used to say to his son: “O my son, do not learn knowledge in orde r to show off to scholars, or to argue with fools, or to show off in gatherings, and do not abandon knowledge out of aversion to it.” And out of a desire for ignorance, O my son, choose the gatherings that suit you, and if you see people remembering Allah, then sit with them, for if you are knowledgeable, your knowledge will benefit you, and if you are ignorant, they will teach you, and perhaps Allah will look upon them with His mercy and make you suffer with it along with them. And if you see people who do not remember Allah, then do not sit with them. If you are knowledgeable, your knowledge will not benefit you, and if you are ignorant, they will increase your ignorance. Perhaps Allah will bring down a punishment upon them and afflict you with them.”

Yusuf ibn Musa informed us, Ishaq ibn Sulayman informed us, Hariz informed us, on the authority of Salman ibn Sumair, on the authority of Katheer ibn Murrah, who said: “Do not speak falsehood to the wise, lest they detest you. Do not speak wisdom to fools, lest they  disbelieve you. Do not withhold knowledge from its people, lest you sin. Do not give it to those who are not worthy of it, lest you be treated ignorantly. Indeed, there is a right upon you in your knowledge.” Just as you have a right over your wealth.

Abdullah ibn Salih informed us, Muawiyah told me, that Abu Farwa told him, that Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, used to say: “Do not withhold knowledge from its people, lest you sin, and do not spread it to those who are not worthy of it, lest you become ignorant. Be a gentle physician who puts your medicine where you know it will be beneficial.”
Abu al-Nu’man told us, Mahdi told us, on the authority of Ghailan, on the authority of Mutarrif, who said: “Do not feed your food to someone who does not desire it.”

Muhammad ibn Ahmad informed us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Shabur, who heard Shahr ibn Hawshab say: Luqman said to his son: “O my son, do not learn knowledge to show off to scholars, or to argue with fools, or to show off in gatherings, and do no t abandon knowledge out of aversion to it and a desire for ignorance. And if you see…” If you see people who do not remember Allah, then do not sit with them. If you are knowledgeable, your knowledge will benefit you, and if you are ignorant, they will teach you. Perhaps Allah will bestow His mercy upon them and cause you to be afflicted with it along with them. And if you see people who do not remember Allah, then do not sit with them. If you are knowledgeable, your knowledge will not benefit you, and if you are ignorant, they will increase your error or blindness. Perhaps Allah will bestow His mercy upon you. He looks at them with wrath and afflicts you with it along with them.

Al-Hasan ibn Bishr told us: My father told me, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Thuwayr, on the authority of Yahya ibn Ja’dah, on the authority of Ali (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “O bearers of knowledge, act upon it, for the knowledgeable person is he who acts upon what he knows and whose knowledge agrees with his actions. There will be people who carry knowledge but it does not go beyond their collarbones, and their actions will contradict their knowledge, and their actions will contradict their knowledge.” Their private life is their public life. They si t in circles and boast to one another, to the point that a man becomes angry with his companion for sitting with someo ne other than him and leaves him. Those are the ones whose deeds in those gatherings do not ascend to Allah, the Most High.

Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus informed us, Zaydah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Masruq, who said: “It is sufficient knowledge for a person that he fears Allah, and it is sufficient ignorance for a person that he is impressed by his knowledge.”

Al-Hakam ibn al -Mubarak informed us, Yahya ibn Saeed informed us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Bujayr, on the authority of Muawiyah ibn Qurrah, who said: “If the least knowledgeable person of this nation were to take his knowledge from a nation, that n ation would be rightly guided.”

" Ahmad ibn Abdullah informed us, Zaydah told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: “If a man were to acquire a chapter of knowledge and act upon it, it would be better for him than the world and everything in it, if he had it and put it aside for the Hereafter.” 137 He said: al-Hasan said: “When a man sought knowledge, it would not take long for that to be seen in his eyes.” And his piety, his tongue, his hand, his prayers, and his asceticism.” He said: And Muhammad said: “Look from whom you take this hadith, for it is your religion.”
Bishr ibn al-Hakam told us: I heard Sufyan say: “A servant does not increase in knowledge and increase in desire for this world except that he increases in distance from Allah.”

Abu Al-Mughira informed us, Al-Awza’i told us, on the authority of Hassan, who said: “A servant of Allah does not increase in knowledge except that people increase in closeness to Allah’s mercy.” And he said in another hadith: “A servant of Allah does not increase in knowledge except that he increases in moderation, and Allah does not bestow upon a servant a necklace better than tranquility.”

Al-Qasim ibn Kathir told us: I heard Abd al -Rahman ibn Shurayh narrating, on the authority of Umayrah, that he heard him say: A man said to his son: “Go and seek knowledge.” So he went out and was absent from him for a long time, then he came back and narrated to him some hadiths, so his father said to him: “O my son, go and seek knowledge.” So, he was absent from him for a while again, then he came back. With papers containing books, he read them to him, and he said to him: This is black in white, so go and seek knowledge. So, he went out and was lost to what was lost to him, then he came and said to his father: Ask me whatever comes to your mind. So, his father said to him: What do you think if you passed by a man who praised you, and you passed by another who found fault with you? He said: “Then I would not blame the one who found fault with me, 138 and I would not praise the one who He praised me, so he said: What if you passed by a plate? Abu Shuraih said: I do not know if it is made of gold or silver. He said: Then I will not stir it up or come near it. He said: Go, for you know.

Al-Hakam ibn al -Mubarak informed us, Baqiyah informed us, on the authority of al -Sakn ibn Umair, who said: I heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say: “O my son, you must have wisdom, for goodness is in all of it. It makes the young superior to the old, and the slave superior to the free. It increases the master’s prestige and seats the poor in the company of kings.”

Al-Hakam ibn al-Mubarak told us: Baqiyah told me, on the authority of Utbah ibn Abi Hakim, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’ (رضئ اللہ تعالیعنه)  who said: “And what would we be were it not for the words of the scholars?”

Sulayman ibn Harb informed us, on the authority of Hammad ibn Zayd, on the authority of Ayyub, who said: Abu Qilabah said: “Do not sit with the people of whims and do not debate with them, for I do not feel safe that they will immerse you in their misguidance or confuse you about what you used to know.”

Sulayman ibn Harb informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Ayyub, who said: Saeed ibn Jubayr saw me sitting with Talq ibn Habib, so he said to me: “Didn’t I see you sitting with Talq ibn Habib? Don’t sit with him.”

Abu Asim informed us, Haywah ibn Shurayh informed us, Abu Sakhr informed me, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) that a man came to him and said: So-and-so sends his greetings to you. He said: “I have been informed that he has broken his ablution. If he has broken his ablution, do not send his greetings to him.”
Makhlad ibn Malik informed us, Abd al -Rahman ibn Maghra’ informed us, al -A’mash informed us, he said: “Ibrahim did not see any need to backbite an innovator.”
Muhammad ibn Humayd told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ibn Shubrumah, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said: “It was called ‘desire’ because it causes its owner to fall.”

Affan informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, Muhammad ibn Wasi’ told us, he said: Muslim ibn Yasar used to say: “Beware of argumentation, for it is the hour of the scholar’s ignorance, and through it Satan seeks to cause him to slip up.” 140

Said ibn Amir informed us, on the authority of Asma ibn Ubayd, who said: Two men from among the followers of whims entered upon Ibn Sirin and said: O Abu Bakr, may we narrate to you a hadith? He said: No. They said: Shall we recite to you a verse from the Book of Allah? He said: No, you must either get up from me or I will get up. So, they left, and some of the people said: O Abu Bakr, what was that? You should recite to you a verse from the Book of Allah Almighty. He said: “I was afraid that they would recite to me a verse from the Book of Allah and distort it, and that would settle in my heart.”

Sa`id informed us, on the authority of Sallam ibn Abi Mut`i`, that a man from the people of desires said to Ayyub: O Abu Bakr, may I ask you about a word? He said: “So he turned away and pointed with his finger, not even half a word,” and Sa`id pointed to us with his right little finger.

Sulayman ibn Harb informed us, on the authority of Hammad ibn Zayd, on the authority of Kulthum ibn Jabr, that a man asked Sa`id ibn Jubayr about something, but he did not answer him. So he was asked, and he said: “Azishan.”

Ahmad ibn Abdullah informed us, Fadil told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Abu Ja`far Muhammad ibn `Ali, who said: “Do not sit with those who engage in disputes, for they are the ones who engage in arguments about the verses of Allah.”

Ahmad informed us, Zaydah told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin, that they said: “Do not sit with the people of whims, do not debate with them, and do not listen to them.”
Ahmad informed us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Umayy, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: “They were called the people of desires because they fall into the Fire.”

Bishr ibn al-Hakam told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Maysarah, who said: “I have never seen anyone among the people who, in his view, regarded the noble and the lowly as equal, except Tawus, and he would swear an oath to him.”

" Bishr ibn al-Hakam informed us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, who said: “We used to dislike writing down knowledge until the ruler forced us to do so, so we disliked preventing anyone from doing so.” 142

Yusuf ibn Musa informed us, Muadh ibn Muadh informed us, Ibn Awn informed us, he said: They spoke to Muhammad about a man, meaning he was talking to him, so he said: “If he had been a Zanj man, he would have been with me, and Abdullah ibn Muhammad would be the same in this.”

Yahya ibn Hassan informed us, on the authority of Hammad ibn Zayd, on the authority of al-Salt ibn Rashid, that Salm ibn Qutaybah asked Tawus about a matter, but he did not answer him. So, it was said to him: This is Salm ibn Qutaybah. He said: “That is easier for him than for me.”
Ibrahim bin Ishaq told us, on the authority of Baqiyah, who said: Habib bin Salih told me, saying: “I have never feared anyone among the people as much as I fear Khalid bin Ma’dan.”
Abu Nu`aym informed us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mughirah, who said: “We used to fear Ibrahim with the fear of a prince.”

Sulayman ibn Harb informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd informed us, on the authority of Ayyub, who said: Sa`id ibn Jubayr narrated a hadith one day, so I went to him and asked him about it. He said to me, “Why do I milk every hour and then drink?”

Muhammad ibn Humayd informed us, Harun - he is the son of al-Mughira - and Yahya ibn Durays informed us, on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Qays, on the authority of Ata’, “that Abu Abd al - Rahman disliked hadith on the road.”

Abdullah ibn Imran informed us, Yahya ibn Durays told us, Abu Sinan told us, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit, who said: We were with Said ibn Jubayr, and he narrated a hadith. A man said to him: Who narrated this to you, or from whom did you hear this? He became angry and prevented us from narrating his hadith until he stood up.

Abu Mamar Ismail ibn Ibrahim informed us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al- Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Salamah, who said: “If I had been kind to Ibn Abbas, I would have acquired a great deal of knowledge from him.”
Al-Hakam bin Al-Mubarak informed us, Baqiyah informed us, on the authority of Umm Abdullah bint Khalid, who said: “I have never seen anyone more generous with knowledge than my father.”

Muhammad ibn al-Mubarak informed us, on the authority of Isa ibn Yunus, on the authority of al- Awza’i, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Musa, who said: I said to Tawus: So -and-so told me such-and-such. He said: “If your companion is intelligent, then take it from him.”
Muhammad ibn Ahmad informed us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mis`ar, who said: Sa`d ibn Ibrahim said: “Only trustworthy people narrate from the Apostle of Allah.”

Muhammad ibn Humayd informed us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, who said: “They did not ask about the chain of transmission, then they asked later to know who was a follower of the Sunnah and from whom they took, an d who was not a follower of the Sunnah, they did not take from him.” Abu Muhammad said: I do not think he heard it from Asim.

Muhammad ibn Humayd informed us, Jarir informed us, on the authority of Asim, who said: Muhammad ibn Sirin said: “Whatever you narrate to me, do not narrate to me on the authority of 145 two men, for they do not care from whom they take their hadith.” Abu Muhammad Abdullah said: I do not think he heard it.

Muhammad informed us, Jarir told us, on the authority of ‘Umarah ibn al-Qa’qa’, who said: Ibrahim said: “If you narrate to me, narrate to me on the authority of Abu Zur’ah, for he narrated to me a hadith, then I asked him a year later, and he did not omit a single letter of it.”
Affan informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Muhammad, who said: “This knowledge is religion, so let a man look from whom he takes his religion.”

Ismail bin Ibrahim informed us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: “When they came to a man to learn from him, they would look at his prayer, his bearing, and his appearance.”

Amr ibn Zurara informed us, Hisham informed us, Mughira informed us, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: “When they came to a man to learn from him, they would look at his prayer, his bearing, and his appearance, then they would learn from him.” Abu Ma’mar Ismail ibn Ibrahim 146 informed us, on the authority of Rawh, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Al -Hasan, something similar to the hadith of Ibrahim
Abu Asim told us, he said: I do not know whether I heard it from him, or from Ibn Awn, on the authority of Muhammad: “This knowledge is religion, so be careful from whom you take your religion.”

Marwan ibn Muhammad informed us, Said ibn Abd al -Aziz narrated to us, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Musa, who said: I said to Tawus: So-and-so narrated to me such-and-such. He said: "If your companion is intelligent, then take it from him."

Muhammad ibn Ahmad informed us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Hujayr, on the authority of Tawus, who said: Bushair ibn Ka’b came to Ibn Abbas and began to narrate to him. Ibn Abbas said: Repeat to me the first hadith. Bushair said to him: I do not know whether you recognized all of my hadith and rejected this one, or whether you recognized this one and rejected all of my hadith. Ibn Abbas: “We used to narrate from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) when no one would lie about h im. But when people embarked on the difficult and the easy, we stopped narrating from him.”

Ismail ibn Aban told us: Abdullah ibn al -Mubarak told us, on the authority of Mamar, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abbas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) said: “We used to memorize hadith, and hadith is memorized from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) until you rode on difficult and easy mounts.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “It is likely that devils will appear, whom Solomon, peace be upon him, had bound, and they will teach people about religion.”
Ahmad ibn Abdullah told us, Zaydah told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Muhammad, who said: “Look from whom you take this hadith, for it is your religion.” 148

Musa ibn Khalid informed us, Mutamir told us, on the authority of his father, who said: “One should be wary of interpreting the hadith of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) just as one should be wary of interpreting the Qur’an.”

Sadaqah ibn al-Fadl informed us, Mutamir told us, on the authority of his father, who said: Ibn Abbas said: “Do you not fear that you will be punished, or that the earth will swallow you up, because you say: The Apostle of Allah said, and so-and-so said?”

Al-Hasan ibn Bishr informed us, Al-Muafa told us, on the authority of Al-Awzai, who said: Umar ibn Abd Al-Aziz, may Allah Almighty have mercy on him, wrote: "No one has an opinion in the Book of Allah. Rather, the opinion of the Imams is in that which no book has been revealed about, and no Sunnah has been established by the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)No one has an opinion in a Sunnah that he established." The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)

Musa ibn Khalid narrated to us, Mutamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Umar, that Umar ibn Abd al -Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him, delivered a sermon and said: “O people, Allah did not send a prophet after your Prophet, nor did He reveal a 149 book after this book that He revealed to him. So whatever Allah made lawful through the tongue of His Prophet is lawful until the Day of Resurrection.” And what He has forbidden through the tongue of His Prophet is forbidden until the Day of Resurrection. Beware, I am not a judge, but I am an enforcer. I am not an innovator, but I am a follower. I am not better than you, except that I am heavier than you. Beware, none of Allah’s creation has the right to be obeyed in disobeying Allah. Have I not heard?

Ubaydullah ibn Sa`id informed us, Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah narrated to us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Hujayr, who said: Tawusi used to pray two rak`ahs after the `Asr prayer, so Ibn `Abbas said to him: “Leave it.” He said: “It was only forbidden because it was used as a ladder.” Ibn `Abbas said: “It was forbidden to pray after the `Asr prayer, so I do not know whether I will be punished for it or rewarded.” Because Allah says: “It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Apostle have decided a matter, that they should have any option in their decision. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Apostle has certainly strayed into clear error. Surah Al-Ahzab, verse 36. Sufyan said: “It is taken as a ladder. He says: He prays after the afternoon prayer until the night.”

Muhammad ibn al -Ala’ informed us, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of Aamir, on the authority of Jabir (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) that Umar ibn al-Khattab (رضئ تعالی عنه) came to the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) with a copy of the Torah and said: O Apostle of Allah, this is a copy of the Torah. He remained silent, then he began to read and the face of the Apostle of Allah changed, so he said: Abu Bakr, may Allah have mercy on him: May the widows be bereaved of you! What do you see on the face of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)Umar looked at the face of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  and said: I seek refuge in Allah from the wrath of Allah and from the wrath of His Apostle (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) . We are satisfied with Allah as our Lord, with Islam as our religion, and with Muhammad as our 150 Prophet. The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: “By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, if Moses appeared to you and you followed him, and if you had abandoned me, you would have strayed from the right path. Had he been alive and known of my prophethood, he would have followed me.”

Qubaysah narrated to us, Sufyan informed us, on the authority of Abu Rabah, an elder from the family of Umar, who said: Saeed ibn al -Musayyib saw a man praying two rakahs after the Asr prayer, saying Allahu Akbar. So he said to him: O Abu Muhammad, will Allah punish me for praying? He said: "No, but Allah will punish you for going against the Sunnah."

Abdullah ibn Salih informed us, Al-Layth told me, Ibn Ajlan told me, on the authority of Al-Ajlan, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah (رضئاللہ تعالی عنه)  on the authority of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) who said: “While a man was swaggering around in two cloaks, Allah caused the earth to swallow him up, and he will continue to sink in it until the Day of Resurrection.” A young man, whom he had named and who was wearing a garment of his, said to him: O Ab u Hurairah, was this how the boy who was swallowed up by the earth walked? Then he struck his hand and stumbled and almost broke from it. Abu Hurairah said to his nostrils and mouth: # Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers. Surah Al-Hijr, verse 95 #

Muhammad ibn Humayd informed us, Harun - he is Ibn al-Mughira - told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Qais, on the authority of al -Zubayr ibn Adi, on the authority of Khirash ibn Jubayr, who said: I saw a young man throwing stones in the mosque, so an o ld man said to him: Do not throw stones, for I heard the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  forbid throwing stones. The young man was distracted and thought that the old man was not He noticed it, so he threw it away. The old man said to him: I tell you that I heard the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) forbidding throwing away the goats, and then you throw away the goats? By Allah, I will not attend your funeral, nor visit you when you are sick, nor will I ever speak to you again. So I said to a friend of mine called Muhajir: Go to Khirash and ask him. So, he went to him and asked him about him, and he told him

Sulayman ibn Harb informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Ayyub, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn Mughaffal (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  forbade throwing stones and said: “It does not catch game, nor does it wound an enemy, but it breaks teeth and puts out eyes.” Then a man stood between him and Sa`id. A relative of something from the land, so he said: This? And what is this? Saeed said: Do I not see myself narrating to you from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) and then you neglect it? I will never speak to you again.

Abdullah ibn Yazid informed us, Kahams ibn al -Hasan told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Buraydah, who said: Abdullah ibn Mughaffal  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه ) saw one of his companions throwing stones at people, so he said: Do not throw stones at people, for the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) used to forbid throwing stones, or he disliked throwing stones,” and he said: “It does not cause injury.” An enemy, and no game is hunted with it, but it may put out an eye and break a tooth.” Then he saw him after those throwing stones, so he said to him: Didn’t I tell you that the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  used to forbid it, then I see you throwing stones, and by Allah I will never speak to you again. 152
