Marwan ibn Muhammad informed us, Sa`id ibn Bashir informed us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Ibn Sirin told a man a hadith on the authority of the Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) A man said: So-and-so said such-and-such. Ibn Sirin said: “I tell you on the authority of the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) and you say: So-and-so and so-and-so said such-and-such. I will never speak to you again.”

Muhammad ibn Kathir informed us, on the authority of al-Awza’i, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) that the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  said: “If one of yours wife asks permission to go to the mosque, he should not prevent her.” So -and-so ibn ‘Abdullah said: “Then, by Allah, I will prevent her.” Ibn ‘Umar turned to him and insulted him with an insult I had never seen before. No one had ever insulted her before him. Then he said: I will tell you about the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) and you say: Then, by Allah, I will prevent her.

Muhammad ibn Humayd informed us, Harun ibn al -Mughira narrated to us, on the authority of Maruf, on the authority of Abu al -Mukhariq, who said: Ubadah ibn as -Samit (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) mentioned that the Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم ) forbade exchanging two dirhams for one dirham.” So-and-so said: “I do not see anything wrong with this, hand to hand.” Ubadah said: “I say: The Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  said, and you say: No.” I see no harm in it, and by Allah, no roof will ever shade me and you. 153

Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Rifai informed us, Abu Amir al-Aqdi told us, on the authority of Zam’ah, on the authority of Salamah ibn Wahram, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) on the authority of the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) who said: “Do not approach women at night.” He said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  returned, and two men slipped away to their families, and both of them found His wife is a man

Abu al-Mughira informed us, al-Awza’i told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Harmalah al-Aslami, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al -Musayyib, who said: Whenever the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  returned from a journey, he would stop at al -Mu’arras, then he would say: “Do not approach women at night.” Two men who had heard his words went out and approached their families, and each one of them found One of them, with his wife, is a man. This Hadith will not be preserved as its authenticity is questionable as it is narrated by Sa’id Al - Mussayyeb who was hired by Umayyed rulers.

Abu al-Mughira informed us, al-Awza’i told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Harmalah told us, he said: A man came to Sa’id ibn al-Musayyib to bid him farewell with a Hajj or Umrah, so he said to him: Do not leave until you pray, for the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  said: “No one leaves the mosque after the call to prayer except a hypocrite, except a man who…” A need took him out while he was wanting to return to the mosque. He said: My companions are in Al-Harrah. He said: So, he went out. He said: Saeed continued to be fond of mentioning him until he was informed that he had fallen from his mount and his thigh was broken. 154

Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith informed us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: “Do not bore people with boredom.”

Yazid ibn Harun informed us, Ashath informed us, on the authority of Kurdus, on the authority of Abdullah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: "The hearts have a state of activity and acceptance, and they have a turning away and a retreat, so tell the people how they are turning towards you."

Sulayman ibn Harb informed us, Abu Hilal told us, he said: I heard al-Hasan say: It was said: “Tell the people what they are turning their faces to you for when they turn their faces, then when they turn around, know that they have needs.”

Yazid ibn Harun informed us, Hammam informed us, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al -Khudri (رضئ اللہ تعالیعنه)  that the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: “Do not write anything from me except the Qur’an. Whoever writes anything from me other than the Qur’an, let him erase it.” 155

Abu Mamar informed us, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, who said: Zayd ibn Aslam told us, on the authority of Ata ibn Yasar, on the authority of Abu Said al -Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him: They asked the Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  for permission to write on his authority, but he did not give them permission.

Bishr ibn al-Hakam informed us, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Ibn Shubrumah, on the authority of al-Shabi, that he used to say: "O Shibak, should I respond to you?" meaning: the hadith. "I never wanted a hadith to be responded to me."

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Khalaf told us: I heard Abd al -Rahman ibn Mahdi say: I heard Malik ibn Anas say: Al-Zuhri came with a hadith, so I met him on the way. I took hold of his bridle and said: O Abu Bakr, repeat to me the hadith that you narrated to u s. He said: “And you are repeating the hadith?” I said: “And you were not…” Do you want to repeat the hadith? He said: No. I said: And are you not write it? He said: No.

Muhammad ibn Kathir informed us, on the authority of al -Awza’i, who said: “Qatadah disliked writing, but when he heard the sound of writing, he would reject it and seek it with his hand.” Abu al-Mughira informed us, who said: “Al-Awza’i disliked it.” 156
Muhammad ibn Yusuf told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, “that Abraham hated the Book,” meaning knowledge.
Yusuf ibn Musa informed us, Azhar informed us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, who said: “If I were to have a book, I would have taken the letters of the Prophet  (صلى

Ismail ibn Aban told us, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, who said: “I saw Hammad writing for Ibrahim, so Ibrahim said to him: ‘Did I not forbid you?’ He said: ‘They are only the edges.”

Ismail ibn Aban told us, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al - Hakam, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: Ubaydah said to me: “Do not write a letter against me forever.”
Sa`id ibn `Amir told us, on the authority of Hisham, who said: “I did not write anything from Muhammad except the hadith of Al-A`maq, and when I memorized it, I erased it.”
Marwan bin Muhammad told us: I heard Saeed bin Abdul Aziz say: “I never wrote a hadith.”
Abdullah bin Imran informed us, Abu Dawud told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: “I never wrote anything.”

Abdullah ibn Imran informed us, Abu Dawud informed us, Shu’bah informed us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Raja’, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: I asked Ubaidah for a piece of leather on which to write, so he said: “O Ibrahim, do not immortalize a letter from me.” Abdullah informed us, Abu Dawud informed us, Shu’bah informed us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Ubaida, like him

Yahya ibn Hammad informed us, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Sulayman ibn ‘Atik, on the authority of Abu Ma’shar, on the authority of Ibrahim: “He disliked writing hadiths in notebooks, and he said: It resembles the copies of the Qur’an.” Yahya sai d: “And I found in my 158 book, on the authority of Ziyad al -Katib, on the authority of Abu Ma’shar, ‘Then write however you wish.’”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf and Ubaydullah informed us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Nu’man ibn Qays, that Ubaydah called for his books and erased them at the time of his death, and said, “I fear that some people will take over and will not put them in their proper places.”

Al-Hakam ibn al-Mubarak and Zakariya ibn Adi informed us, on the authority of Abd al -Wahid ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, that he disliked that knowledge be written in notebooks.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Salih informed us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of al-Awza’i, who said: “This knowledge remained rare, and men would gather around it until it appeared in the books, and then it was carried or entered into by those who were not worthy of it.”

Yusuf ibn Musa informed us, Abu Dawud al -Tayalisi informed us, Shu’bah informed us, on the authority of Yunus, who said: “Al -Hasan used to write and write, but Ibn Sirin did not write and did not write.” 159

Yazid informed us, Al-Awwam informed us, on the authority of Ibrahim At -Taymi, who said: It reached Ibn Mas`ud (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) that some people had a book that they admired, so he kept pestering them until they brought it to him. He erased it, then said: “The People of the Book before you were destroyed because they turned to the books of their scholars and abandoned the Book of their Lord.”

Abu al-Numan informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Muhammad, who said: I said to Ubaydah: "Should I write what I hear from you?" He said: "No." I said: "What if I find a book that I can read?" He said: "No."

Yazid ibn Harun informed us, Al-Jariri informed us, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, who said: I said to Abu Sa’id Al -Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him: “Why don’t you write it down for us, for we do not memorize it?” He said: “No, we will not write it down for you, and we will not make it the Qur’an. Rather, memorize it from us as we memorized it from the Apostle of Allah
Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, who said: I heard Abu Kathir say: I heard Abu Hurairah say: “Abu Hurairah does not write, and he is not written.” 160

Asad ibn Musa told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Musa, on the authority of Humayd ibn Hilal, on the authority of Abu Burdah: “He was writing down his father’s hadith, and Abu Musa saw it and erased it.”
Al-Walid ibn Shuja’ informed us, Quraysh ibn Anas told me, he said: Ibn ‘Awn said to me: “By Allah, I have never written a hadith.”

He said: Ibn Sirin (رضئاللہ تعالی عنه)  said: “No, by Allah, I have never written a hadith.” Ibn Awn said: Ibn Sirin said to me: On the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit, may Allah be pleased with him: Marwan ibn al-Hakam, who was the governor of Medina, wanted me to write something for him. He said: “But I did not do so.” He said: “So he placed a screen between his sitting place and the rest of his house.” He said: “So his companions…” They would enter upon him and talk about that place. Marwan turned to his companions and said, “I think we have betrayed him.” Then he turned to me and said, “I said, ‘What is that?’ He said, ‘I think we have betrayed you.’ I said, ‘What is that?’ He said, ‘We have ordered a man to sit behind this curtain and write down what you issue fatwas to these people and what you say.’”

Affan informed us, Yahya ibn Saeed al-Qattan told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, who said: I said to Ibrahim: Is Salim more complete in hadith than you? He said: “Salim used to write.”

Al-Walid ibn Hisham informed us, Al-Harith ibn Yazid Al-Himsi informed us, on the authority of Amr ibn Qays, who said: I went with my father to Yazid ibn Mu’awiyah in Hawarin when Mu’awiyah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) passed away, to offer my condolences to him and congratulate him on the caliphate. Suddenly, a man was in its mosque saying: “Indeed, among the signs of the Hour is that the wicked will be removed and the weak will be placed…” The best, beware, among the signs of the Hour is that the word will be made apparent, and the action will be stored. Beware, among the signs of the Hour is that the Mathnat will be recited, and there will be no one to change it. It was said to him: What is the Mathnat? He said: What was written in a book other than the Qur’an. So stick to the Qur’an, for by it you are guided, by it you will be rewarded, and about it you will be asked. I did not know who the man was. Then I narrated this hadith after that in Homs, and a man from the people said to me: Do you not know him? I said: No. He said: That is Abdullah ibn Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both.

Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus informed us, Abu Zubayd told us, Husayn told us, on the authority of Murrah al-Hamdani, who said: Abu Qurrah al -Kindi brought a letter from Syria. He carried it and gave it to Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, may Allah be pleased with him. He looked at it, then called for a basin, then called for water, dipped it in it and said: “Those who came before you perished only because of the By following the books and abandoning their book,” Husayn said: Murrah said: “If it had been from the Qur’an or the Sunnah, He would not have erased it, but it was from the books of the People of the Book.” 162

Muhammad ibn Ahmad informed us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Yahya ibn Jadah, who said: The Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم ) was brought a shoulder strap containing a book, and he said: It is enough for a people to be misguided that they turn away from what their prophet brought in exchange for what a prophet other than their prophet brought, or a book other than their book. So, Allah revealed: Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book which is recited to them. Indeed, in that is mercy and a reminder for people who believe. Surah Al-Ankabut, Verse 51

Sahl ibn Hammad informed us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of al-Ash`ath, on the authority of his father, who was one of the companions of `Abdullah, who said: I saw a man with a scroll in which was written: Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no Allah but Allah, and Allah is the Greatest. So, I said to him: Copy it for me, but he seemed to be stingy with it, then he promised to give it to me, so I went to `Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him. On his authority, it was before him. He said: “What is in this book is an innovation, a trial, and  a misguidance. What destroyed those who came before you was this and things similar to this. They wrote it down, their tongues found pleasure in it, and their hearts were filled with it. So, I call upon every person who knows the location of a book to point to it, and I swear by Allah.” Shu’bah said: : So, he swore by Allah? He said: I think he swore: If she had mentioned to him the monastery of India, which we see as being far away, I would have come to it even on foot.

Zakariya ibn Adi informed us, Ubaydullah ibn Amr informed us, on the authority of Abd al-Malik ibn Umair, on the authority of Abu Burdah, on the authority of Abu Musa  (رضئ اللہ تعالیعنه)  that the Children of Israel wrote a book, followed it, and abandoned the Torah. 163

Abu Nu`aym informed us, Isra`il told us, on the authority of `Uthman ibn Abi al-Mughira, on the authority of `Affaq al-Muharibi, on the authority of his father, who said: I heard Ibn Mas`ud (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) say: “There are people who hear my words, then they go and write them down, and I do not permit anyone to write anything except the Book of Allah.”
Malik ibn Ismail informed us, Muhammad ibn Fadil informed us, on the authority of Ibn Shubrumah, who said: I heard Al-Sha’bi say: “I never wrote black on white, nor did I seek a hadith from anyone.”

Muhammad ibn Ahmad informed us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, on the authority of his brother, who heard Abu Hurayrah  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) say: “None of the Companions of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) narrated more hadiths from the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) than me, except for what was from Abdullah ibn Amr, for he used to write, and I did not.”

Musaddad informed us, Yahya told us, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn al -Akhnas, who said: Al-Walid ibn Abdullah told me, on the authority of Yusuf ibn Mahak, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: I used to write down everything I heard from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) wanting to memorize it. The Quraysh forbade me, saying: You write down everything you hear from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)Allahs Apostle (may Allahs peace and blessings be upon him) is a human being who speaks in anger and pleasure. So, I stopped writing and mentioned that to the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلمHe pointed with his finger to his mouth and said, "Write, for by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, nothing comes out of it except the truth."

Abdullah ibn Salih informed us, Al -Layth informed me, Khalid ibn Yazid informed me, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Hilal, on the authority of Abdul -Wahid ibn Qays, who said: An informant informed me, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr   (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) that he came to the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) and said: O Apostle of Allah, I want to narrate some of your hadith, so I wanted to Should I seek help with the book of my hand along with my heart if you see that? The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: If he said it: “Recite my hadith, then seek help with your hand along with your heart.”

Uthman ibn Muhammad informed us, Yahya ibn Ishaq informed us, Yahya ibn Ayyub informed us, on the authority of Abu Qabil, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Amr  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  say: While we were around the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  writing, the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) was asked: Which of the two cities will be conquered first: Constantinople? Or Roman? The Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: “No, rather the city of Heraclius first.”

Ismail ibn Ibrahim Abu Mamar informed us, on the authority of Abu Damrah, on the authority of Yahya ibn Said, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Dinar, who said: Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him, wrote to Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm: “Write to me what you have established of the hadith from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  and the hadith of Umrah.” For I fear the loss of knowledge and its disappearance.

Yahya ibn Hassan narrated to us, Abd al -Aziz ibn Muslim narrated to us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Dinar, who said: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz wrote to the people of Medina: “Look at the hadith of the Apostle of Allah  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم ) and write it down, for I fear the loss of knowledge and the passing of its people.”

Sulayman ibn Harb informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Ayyub, on the authority of Abu al-Malih, who said: “They criticize the Book for us, while Allah the Most High said: ‘The knowledge thereof is with my Lord in a Book.’ Surah Ta-Ha, verse 52.”

Ubaydullah ibn Abd al-Majid informed us, Sawada ibn Hayyan told us, he said: I heard Muawiyah ibn Qurrah Abu Iyas say: It was said: “Whoever does not write down his knowledge, his knowledge is not considered knowledge.” 166
Muslim ibn Ibrahim informed us, Abdullah ibn al -Muthanna told us, Thamama ibn Abdullah ibn Anas told me: Anas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) used to say to his sons: “O my sons, record this knowledge.”

Ismail ibn Aban told us, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Mahdi ibn Maymun, on the authority of Salm al-Alawi, who said: “I saw Aban writing on a blackboard in the presence of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him.”

Ahmad ibn Isa informed us, Ibn Wahb told us, on the authority of Muawiyah, on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Jabir, that he asked Abu Umamah Al -Bahili (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  about the book of knowledge, and he said: “There is nothing wrong with that.”

Makhlad ibn Malik informed us, Muadh told us, Imran ibn Hudayr told us, on the authority of Abu Mijlaz, on the authority of Bashir ibn Nahik, who said: I used to write down what I heard from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him. When I wanted to lea ve him, I brought him his letter, read it to him, and said to him: Did I hear this from you? He said: Yes.

Muhammad ibn Sa`id informed us, Sharik informed us, on the authority of Tariq ibn `Abd al - Rahman, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, who said: “I used to hear hadiths at night from Ibn `Umar and Ibn `Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them, and I would write them down in the middle of the saddle.”

Muhammad ibn Said informed us, Sharik informed us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: "Nothing in life makes me desire anything except the truthful and the deceitful. As for the truth, it is a document that I wrote from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)As for the deceit, it is land that Amr ibn al-As (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) gave in charity and he used to look after it."

Abu Asim informed us, Ibn Jurayj informed me, on the authority of Abd al -Malik ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Sufyan, on the authority of his uncle Amr ibn Abi Sufyan, that he heard Umar ibn al - Khattab (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) say: “Bind knowledge with the Book.”

Makhlad ibn Malik informed us, Yahya ibn Saeed informed us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: Abd al-Malik ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Sufyan al-Thaqafi informed me, on the authority of Ibn Umar (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) that he said: “Restrict this knowledge to the Book.” 168

Abu al-Numan informed us, Abd al-Wahid informed us, Uthman ibn Hakim informed us, he said: I heard Said ibn Jubayr say: "I was traveling with Ibn Abbas  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  on the road to Mecca at night, and he would narrate a hadith to me, so I would write it down in the middle of the saddle until morning, when I would write it down."

Ismail ibn Aban informed us, on the authority of Yaqub al-Qummi, on the authority of Ja`far ibn Abi al-Mughira, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, who said: “I used to write on a page with Ibn Abbas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) and I used to write on my sandals.”

Malik ibn Ismail informed us, Mandal ibn Ali al -Anazi informed us, Ja`far ibn Abi al -Mughira informed me, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, who said: “I used to sit with Ibn Abbas and write on the page until it was full, then I would turn my sandals over and write on the backs of them.”
Amr ibn Awn informed us, Fadil informed us, on the authority of Ubayd al-Muktab, who said: “I saw them writing the interpretation with Mujahid.”
Muhammad ibn Sa`id informed us, Wakee` informed us, my father informed us, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn Hanash, who said: “I saw them writing at Al-Bara` with the tips of reeds on their palms.”

Ismail ibn Aban informed us, on the authority of Ibn Idris, on the authority of Harun ibn Antara, on the authority of his father, that Ibn Abbas told me a hadith, so I said: Shall I write it down from you? He said: “So he gave me permission, but he did not do it.”

Al-Walid ibn Shuja informed us, Muhammad ibn Shuayb ibn Shabur informed us, Al -Walid ibn Sulayman ibn Abi Al-Saib informed us, on the authority of Raja ibn Haywah, that he told him, saying: Hisham ibn Abd Al-Malik wrote to his governor asking him to ask me about a hadith. Raja said: "I would have forgotten it had it not been written down with me."

Al-Walid ibn Shuja’ informed us, Muhammad ibn Shu’ayb informed us, Hisham ibn al -Ghazz informed us, he said: “Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah used to be asked a question, and his answers would be written down in front of him.”

Al-Walid ibn Shuja’ informed us, Muhammad ibn Shu’ayb ibn Shabur informed us, Al-Walid ibn Sulayman ibn Abi Al -Sa’ib informed us, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Musa, “that he saw Nafi’, the freed slave of Ibn Umar, dictating his knowledge, and it was written down before him.”
Al-Walid ibn Shuja’ informed us, Al-Mubarak ibn Sa’id told us, he said: “Sufyan used to write the hadith at night in the wall, and when morning came he would copy it and then erase it.”

Al-Husayn ibn Mansur informed us, Abu Usamah told us, Abu Ghaffar al-Muthanna ibn Sa’id al- Ta’i told us, ‘Awn ibn ‘Abdullah told me, saying: I said to ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz: So-and-so, a man from among the Companions of the Apostle of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), told me, and ‘Umar recognized him. I said: He told me that the Apostle of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Modesty, chastity, and shamelessness are the shame of the tongue, not the shame of the heart. Understanding is part of faith, and they are among the things that increase in the Hereafter and detract from t his world, but what they increase in the Hereafter is more. Vulgarity, rudeness, and miserliness are among the things that increase in this world and detract in the Hereafter, but what they detract from in the Hereafter is more.” Al-Husayn informed us. Ibn Mansur narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, Sulayman ibn al -Mughira narrated to me, he said: Abu Qilabah said: Umar ibn Abd al -Aziz came out to us for the noon prayer, and he had a piece of paper with him. Then he came out to us for the afternoon pr ayer, and he had it with him. So I said to him: O Commander of the Faithful, what is this book? He said: “This is a hadith narrated to me by Awn ibn Abdullah.” I liked it, so I wrote it down. It contained this hadith.

Ismail ibn Aban informed us, Mas`ud told us, on the authority of Yunus ibn `Abdullah ibn Abi Farwah, on the authority of Shurahbil ibn Abi Sa`d, who said: Al -Hasan (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) called his sons and his brother’s sons and said: “O my sons and my brother’s sons, you are young among a people who will soon become old, so learn knowledge. Whoever among you is unable to narrate it, Or he said: Let him memorize it, write it down, and put it in his house.

Al-Walid ibn Shuja informed us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah informed us, Asim informed us, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Jarir  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: "Whoever establishes a good practice which is followed after him, will have a reward like that of those who act upon it, without that detracting from his reward in the slightest. And whoever establishes bad practice, will bear the burden of sin like that of those who act upon it." Without diminishing anything from their burdens.”

Al-Walid ibn Shuja’ informed us, Ismail ibn Ja’far told us, on the authority of Al-Ala’ ibn Abd al- Rahman ibn Ya’qub, the freed slave of Al-Huraqah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) that the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: “Whoever calls to guidance will have a reward like that of those who follow him, without that detracting from their reward in the slightest. And whoever…” He called to misguidance, and upon him was a sin equal to the sins of those who followed him, without that detracting from their sins in the slightest.”

Al-Walid ibn Shuja’ informed us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Muslim, meaning Ibn Subaih, on the authority of Abd al -Rahman ibn Hilal al -Absi, on the authority of Jarir ibn Abdullah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) addressed us and urged the people to give charity, but they were slow to do so until anger was evident on his face. Then he A man from the Ansar came with a purse, and the people followed one another until joy could be seen on his face. He said, “Whoever establishes a good practice will have a reward similar to that of those who act upon it, without that detracting from their reward in the slightest. And whoever establishes a bad practice will bear its burden, similar to that of those who act upon it, without that detracting from their burden in the slightest.

Abdul Wahhab ibn Saeed informed us, Shuaib - he is Ibn Ishaq - told us, Al-Awza’i told us, Hassan ibn Atiyyah told us, that the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: “I will have the greatest reward among you on the Day of Resurrection, because I have my reward and the same reward as those who follow me.”

Malik ibn Ismail informed us, Abd al-Salam told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Bishr, on the authority of Anas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: “Whoever calls to a matter, even if one man calls another, will be stopped by it on the Day of Resurrection, adhering to its west.” Then he recited: “And stop them, for indeed, they will be questioned.” Surah as-Saffat, verse 24

Amr ibn Asim informed us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Ash-Sha’bi, that Ibn Mas’ud (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) said: “Four things are given to a man after his death: a third of his wealth if he was obedient to Allah before that, a righteous son who supplicates for him after his death, a good Sunnah that a man establishes and then acts upon after his death, and a t hird of his wealth if he was obedient to Allah before that, a righteous son who supplicates for him after his death, and a good Sunnah that a man establishes and then acts upon after his death.” His death, and if a hundred intercede for a man, their intercession for him will be accepted.”
Ahmad ibn al-Hajjaj informed us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah informed us, on the authority of al-A’mash, who said: “We tried hard to make Ibrahim sit next to a pillar, but he refused.”
Affan informed us, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, “that he hated to lean against the column.”
Al-Hakam bin Al-Mubarak informed us, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Mughirah, who said: “Ibrahim would not begin a conversation until he was asked.”

Abdullah ibn Saeed informed us, Yunus ibn Bukayr told us, Al -A’mash told us, on the authority of Khaithamah, who said: Al -Harith ibn Qays Al-Ju’fi, who was one of Abdullah’s companions, and they were impressed by him, “A man or two men would sit with him a nd he would talk to them, and when they became numerous, he would get up and leave them.”

Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus informed us, Abu Shihab told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, who said: When Abdullah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) died, it was said to him: Why don’t you sit and teach the people the Sunnah? He said: “Do you want my heel to be trampled on?”

Muhammad ibn al-Ala’ informed us, Ibn Idris told us, he said: I heard Harun ibn Antara, on the authority of Sulaym ibn Hanzala, he said: We came to Ubayy ibn Ka’b to talk to him, and when he stood up, we stood up, and we were walking behind him, and Umar  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) became exhausted, so he followed him, and Umar struck him with the whip. He said: He protected him with his arms, and said: O Commander of the Faithful, what We do? He said: “Don’t you see? A trial for the one being followed, a humiliation for the one who follows.”
Muhammad ibn Isa told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: “They hated for their heels to be trampled on.”
Abu Nu`aym informed us, Hasan ibn Salih informed us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: “Beware of having your heels trampled upon.

Makhlad ibn Malik informed us, Hajjaj ibn Muhammad told us, Shubah told us, on the authority of Al-Haytham, on the authority of Asim ibn Damrah, that he saw some people following Said ibn Jubayr. He said: I think he said: He forbade them and said: "This action of yours or this walking of yours is a humiliation for the follower and a trial for the one being followed."

" Sa`id ibn `Amir informed us, Humayd ibn Aswad narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn `Awn, who said: “I consulted Muhammad about a building I wanted to build in Al-Kala`. He said: So he advised me and said: If you want to lay the foundation of the buildin g, then inform me so that I may come with you. So I came to him. While we were walking, a man came and walked with him. He stood up and said: Do you have a Do you need anything? He said: No. He said: If not, go. Then he turned to me and said: You also go. He said: So I went until I took a different path. 176

Ahmad ibn al -Hajjaj informed us, Abd al -Rahman ibn Mahdi informed us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Nusayr, that whenever they came to him, al -Rabi’ would say: “I seek refuge in Allah from your evil,” meaning his companions.

Makhlad ibn Malik informed us, Yahya ibn Saeed narrated to us, from Al-Amash, from Raja Al- Ansari, from Abd Al-Rahman ibn Bishr, who said: We were with Khabbab ibn Al-Aratt (رضئ تعالی عنه) and his companions gathered around him while he was silent. It was said to him: Why dont you tell your companions? He said: I am afraid that I will say to them what I do not do.
Muhammad ibn Yusuf told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Salih, who said: I heard al-Sha’bi say: “I wish I had been saved from my work with enough for myself and no burden on me.”

Yazid ibn Harun informed us, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, that Ibn Mas`ud (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) was walking and people were stepping on his heels, so he said: “Do not step on my heels, for by Allah, if you knew why I close my door, not a single man among you would follow me.” 177

Muhammad ibn Humayd told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, who said: “A trial for the one being followed, and a humiliation for the one who follows.”

Shihab ibn Abbad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Umayy, who said: They walked behind Ali (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) and he said: “Refrain from me from the flapping of your sandals, for it corrupts the hearts of the weak-willed men.”
Abu al-Numan informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Hazim, who said: I heard al-Hasan say: "The flapping of sandals around men rarely keeps fools awake."

Muhammad ibn Hatim al-Muktab informed us, Qasim - he is Ibn Malik - told us, Layth told us, on the authority of Tawus, who said: “Whenever a man or two men sat next to him, he would stand up and move away.”

Aswad ibn Amir told us, Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Al -A’mash, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Abdullah ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abu Barzah Al -Aslami, who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: “The feet of a servant will not move on the Day of Resurrection until he is asked about his life and how he spent it, about his knowledge and what he did with it, and about his wealth and where he acquired it and in what way.” He spent it, and his body in what it wore out.

Sa`id ibn Mansur informed us, `Abd al -`Aziz ibn Muhammad informed us, on the authority of `Umarah ibn Ghaziyah, on the authority of Yahya ibn Rashid, who said: So -and-so al -`Urni informed me, on the authority of Mu`adh ibn Jabal  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  who said: “Allah will not leave His servants on the Day of Resurrection, the day when people will stand before the Lord of the Worlds, until He asks them about four things: how they spent their lives, how they will test their bodies therein, and what they  have earned, and what they have spent, and what they have done in what they have learned.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Adi ibn Adi, on the authority of Abu Abdullah as-Sunabihi, on the authority of Muadh ibn Jabal  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه ) who said: “The feet of a servant will not move on the Day of Resurrection until he is asked about four things: about his life and how he spent it; about his body and how he wore it out; about his wealth and where he acquired it and how he spent it; and ab out his knowledge and what it was.” He worked in it

Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Layth, who said: Tawus said to me: “Whatever you have learned, learn for yourself, for people have lost their trustworthiness.”

Sulayman ibn Harb informed us, on the authority of ‘Umarah ibn Mihran, on the authority of al - Hasan, who said: “I met people, and when a person performs an act of worship, he is not known by his speech, but rather he is known by his actions. That is beneficial knowledge.”

Abu al-Mughira informed us, al -Awzai told us, on the authority of Hassan, on the authority of Abu Kabsha, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Amr  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  say: I heard the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) say: "Convey from me even if it is just one verse, and narrate from the Children of Israel, and there is no blame upon you. Whoever lies about me intentionally, let him take his seat in Hellfire."

Ali ibn Hujr al-Sadi informed us, Yazid ibn Harun informed us, al-Awam ibn Hawshab Abu Isa al-Shaybani informed us, al -Qasim ibn Awf al -Shaybani informed us, on the authority of Abu Dharr (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) commanded us not to be overcome in three things: to enjoin what is right, to forbid what is wrong, And we teach people the Sunnah. 180

Abu al-Mughira informed us, Safwan told us, Sulaym ibn Amir told me, he said: Whenever we sat with Abu Umamah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) he would come to us with a hadith with a great matter, and he would say: “Listen to us, understand, and convey from us what you hear.” Sulaym said: “In the position of one who bears witness to what he knows.”

Abd al-Wahhab ibn Said informed us, Shuayb (Ibn Ishaq) informed us, al -Awzai informed us, Abu Kathir informed me, my father informed me, he said: I came to Abu Dharr (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) while he was sitting at the middle Jamrah, and the people had gathered around him seeking his legal opinion. A man came to him, stood over him, and then said: Were you not forbidden from issuing legal opinions? He raised his head to him and said, "Are you  watching over me? If you were to place the sword on this" - and he pointed to the back of his head - then I thought I would carry out a word I heard from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  before you allowed me to do so, I would carry it out.

Muhammad ibn Isa informed us, ‘Abbad, who is Ibn al-‘Awwam, told us, on the authority of ‘Awf, on the authority of Abu al -‘Aliyah, who said: I asked Ibn ‘Abbas  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه ) about something, and he said: O Abu al-Aliyah, do you want to be a mufti? I said: “No, but I do not feel safe that you will go and we will remain.” He said: “Abu al-Aliyah spoke the truth.”

Muhammad ibn Isa informed us, ‘Abbad told us, on the authority of Husayn, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: “Ubaydah used to come to ‘Abdullah  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  every Thursday and ask him about things he had forgotten. Most of what was memorized from ‘Abdullah was what ‘Ubaydah used to ask him about.”
Al-Hakam ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Ghassan ibn Mudar informed us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Yazid, who said: I heard Ikrimah say: “Why do you not ask me? Are you not bankrupt?”
Muhammad ibn Hatim al-Muktab informed us, Amir ibn Salih informed us, Yunus informed us, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, who said: “Knowledge is treasures, and questioning opens them.”

Ibrahim ibn Ishaq informed us, on the authority of Jarir, who said: Ibrahim said: “Whoever has a gentle face, his knowledge will be gentle.” Wakee’ informed us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ash-Sha’bi, who said: “Whoever has a gentle face, his knowledge will be gentle.” And on the authority of Damrah, on the authority of Hafs ibn ‘Umar, who said : ‘Umar ibn Al - Khattab said: “Whoever has a gentle face, his knowledge will be gentle.”
Ibrahim bin Ishaq told us, on the authority of Jarir, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: “He who is ashamed and arrogant will not learn.” 182

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Khalaf informed us, Anas ibn Ayyadh told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, that he used to gather his sons and say: “O my sons, learn, for if you are young among a people, perhaps you will be old among others. How ugly it is for an old man to be asked a question while he has no knowledge.”

Abu al-Numan informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of al-Zubayr ibn al-Kharit, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Ibn Abbas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) used to put chains on my feet and teach me the Quran and the Sunnah."

Muhammad ibn Humayd informed us, Yahya ibn al -Durais told us, he said: I heard Sufyan say: “Whoever takes leadership quickly will harm a lot of knowledge, and whoever does not take leadership will seek and seek until he reaches it.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Salih ibn Khabab, on the authority of Husayn ibn Uqbah, on the authority of Salman (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  who said: “Knowledge that is not spoken about is like a treasure from which no one spends.” 183

Ahmad ibn Abdullah informed us, Abu Shihab told us, Ibrahim told me, on the authority of Abu Ayyad, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: “The example of knowledge that is not benefited from is like the example of a treasure from which no money is spent in the way of Allah.”

Ya`la informed us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, on the authority of Musa ibn Yasar, his paternal uncle, who said: It has reached me that Salman (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) wrote to Abu al-Darda`, may Allah be pleased with him: “Knowledge is like springs that people flock to, and this one and that one take it, but Allah benefits more than one by it. Wisdom that is not spoken is like a body without a soul in it, and knowledge that is not spoken is like a body without a soul in it.” It is not taken out like a treasure from which no one can spend. Rather, the example of the  scholar is like that of a man who carried a lamp on a dark road, illuminating whoever passed by it, and everyone prays for his well-being.

Muhammad ibn al-Salt informed us, Mansur ibn Abi al -Aswad told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: “Three things follow a man after his death: charity that continues after him, his children’s prayers for him, and knowledge that he divulged that is acted upon after him.”

Musa ibn Ismail narrated to us, Ismail ibn Jafar al-Madani narrated to me, on the authority of al- Ala ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) on the authority of the Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  who said: "When a person dies, his deeds come to an end except for three: beneficial knowledge, ongoing charity, or a righteous child who prays for him."

Ubayd ibn Yaish informed us, Yunus told us, on the authority of Salih ibn Rustum al-Muzani, on the authority of al -Hasan, on the authority of Abu Musa  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  that he said when he arrived in Basra: "Umar ibn al-Khattab (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) sent me to you to teach you the Book of your Lord and your Sunnah, and to clean your roads."

Muhammad ibn Humayd informed us, Muhammad ibn al -Mualla informed us, Ziyad ibn Khaithamah informed us, on the authority of Abu Dawud, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Sakhbarah, on the authority of Sakhbarah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) on the authority of the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) who said: "Whoever seeks knowledge, it is an expiation for what has passed."

Muhammad ibn Isa informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Ayyub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, who said: “I stayed in Medina for three days, and I had no need that I did not fulfill, except that a man whom they were waiting for came, and he was narrating a hadith. So I stayed until he came, and I asked him.” 185

Al-Hakam ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, on the authority of Abd al- Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir, who said: I heard Busr ibn Ubayd Allah say: “I would ride to any city in Egypt to hear single hadith.”

Amr ibn Zurara informed us, Abu Qattan Amr ibn al -Haitham informed us, on the authority of Abu Khalda, on the authority of Abu al-Aaliyah, who said: “We used to hear the narration in Basra from the Companions of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) but we were not satisfied until we rode to Madinah, and we heard it from their mouths.”

Nuaym ibn Hammad informed us, Baqiyah narrated to us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Qushayri, who said: Dawud, the Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  said: “Tell the one who has knowledge to take an iron staff and two iron sandals and seek knowledge until the staff breaks and the sandals become torn.”

Makhlad ibn Malik informed us, Yahya ibn Saeed al -Umawi told us, al -Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman from the family of Saad ibn Muadh, who said: Ibn Abbas 186 (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  said: “I sought knowledge but did not find it more abundant than among the Ansar. So I would go to a man and ask about him, and it would be said to me: ‘He is asleep,’ so I would use my cloak as a pillow.” Then I lie down until he comes out at noon, and he says: “When were you here, O cousin of the Apostle of Allah?” I say: “A long time ago.” He says: “What you did is bad. Why didn’t you tell me?” I say: “I wanted you to come out to me after you had fulfilled your need.”

Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus informed us, Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah ibn Abd al -Rahman, on the authority of Ibn Abbas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “Most of the hadith of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) were found with this tribe of the Ansar. By Allah, if I were to come to a man from among them, it would be said: He is asleep, so if I wanted him to be awakened for me, so I left him until he came out so that I could enjoy his conversation.

Abu Mamar Ismail ibn Ibrahim informed us, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Salamah, who said: “If I had been kind to Ibn Abbas, I would have acquired a great deal of knowledge from him.”

Bishr ibn al -Hakam informed us, Abd al -Razzaq informed us, Ma’mar informed us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, who said: “I used to come to the door of Urwah and sit by the door. If I had wanted to enter, I would have entered, but out of respect for him.” 187

Yazid ibn Harun informed us, Jarir ibn Hazim told us, on the authority of Ya’la ibn Hakim, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “When the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  passed away, I said to a man from the Ansar: ‘O so -and-so, come and let us ask the Companions of the Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  for they are many today.’ He said: ‘How strange! O Ibn Abbas, do you think that people need you, while among them are the Companions of the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) ?So, he left that, and I turned to asking questions. If I heard a hadith from a man, I would go to him while he was talking, and I would rest my cloak on his door, and the wind would blow dust on my face. Then he would come out, see me, and say: O cousin of the  Apostle of Allah, what brought you? Did you not send it to me so that I might come to you? I said, “No, I am more deserving of coming to you and asking him about the hadith.” The man stayed until he saw me and the people had gathered around me. He said, “This young man was more intelligent than me.”

Yazid ibn Harun informed us, Al-Jariri narrated to us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Buraydah, “A man from among the companions of the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) traveled to Fadalah ibn Ubayd (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) while he was in Egypt. He came to him while he was extending the water for his camel, and he said: Welcome. He said: As for me, I did not come to visit you, but you and I heard a hadith from the Apostle of Allah.” May Allah bless him and grant him peace. I hope you have some knowledge of it. He said: So-and-so.

Muhammad ibn Said informed us, Abd al -Salam ibn Harb told us, on the authority of Abd al - Ala, on the authority of al -Hasan, that he entered the market and bargained with a man for a 188 garment, saying: "It is yours for such and such. By Allah, if it had been someone other than you, I would not have given it to him." He said: "You have done it." After that, he was not seen buying or selling from the market until he met Allah.
Al-Haytham bin Jameel told us, on the authority of Hussam, on the authority of Abu Ma’shar, on the authority of Ibrahim, that he “did not buy from anyone he knew.”

Muhammad ibn Sa`id informed us, `Abd al-Salam informed us, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn al-Walid al-Muzani, on the authority of `Ubayd ibn al -Hasan, who said: Mus`ab ibn al -Zubayr distributed money among the reciters of the Qur’an in Kufa when the mon th of Ramadan began. He sent two thousand dirhams to `Abd al-Rahman ibn Ma`qil, saying to him: Use it for your benefit this month. But he returned it. Abd al -Rahman ibn Maqil said: “We did not read the Qur’an for this reason.”

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Khalaf informed us, Anas ibn Ayyad told us, Ubaydullah ibn Umar told me, that Umar ibn al-Khattab (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) said to Abdullah ibn Salam, may Allah be pleased with him: “Who are the masters of knowledge?” He said: “Those who act upon what they know.” He said: “What removes knowledge from the hearts of men?” He said: “Greed.”
Muhammad ibn Ahmad informed us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Zayd, on the authority of Ata’, who said: “Nothing is more beautiful than a dream that leads to knowledge.”
Affan informed us, Hammad bin Salamah informed us, Asim Al -Ahwal informed us, on the authority of Amir Al -Sha’bi, who said: “The adornment of knowledge is the patience of its people.”

Yaqub ibn Ibrahim informed us, Abd al -Rahman informed us, Zam’ah ibn Salih informed us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Wahram, on the authority of Tawus, who said: “Knowledge has not been carried in anything like the bag of patience.”
Muhammad ibn Humayd told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ibn Shubrumah, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said: “The adornment of knowledge is the patience of its people.”

Al-Hakam ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Mutarrif ibn Mazin informed us, on the authority of Ya’la ibn Miqsam, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: “Wisdom resides in the gentle and tranquil heart.” 190

Muhammad ibn Ahmad told us: I heard Sufyan say: Ubaydullah said: “You have denigrated knowledge and extinguished its light. If Umar  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) had lived to see me and you, he would have hurt us.”

Shihab ibn Abbad informed us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, on the authority of Umayy al- Muradi, who said: Ali  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  said: “Learn knowledge, and when you acquire it, then conceal it and do not mix it with laughter or playfulness, lest the hearts reject it.”

Muhammad ibn Humayd told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of al -Fudayl ibn Ghazwan, on the authority of Ali ibn Husayn, may Allah have mercy on him, who said: “Whoever laughs a laugh will spit out a mouthful of knowledge.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf told us, on the authority of Sufyan, that Umar  (رضئ اللہ تعالیعنه)  said to Ka’b: “Who are the people of knowledge?” He said: “Those who act upon what they know.” He said: “What drove knowledge from the hearts of scholars?” He said: “Greed.”

Muhammad ibn Humayd informed us, Muhammad ibn Bishr informed us, Abdullah ibn al-Walid informed us, on the authority of Umar ibn Ayyub, on the authority of Abu Iyas, who said: I was staying with Amr ibn al -Nu’man, and the Apostle of Mus’ab ibn al -Zubayr came to him when Ramadan came with two thousand dirhams. He said: The emir sends his greetings to you, and he said: We have not left out a noble reciter. Except that a favor has reached him from us, so use these two to help you with your expenses for this month. He said: Give the prince my greetings and say to him: “By Allah, we did not recite the Qur’an seeking the world and its dirhams.”

Asad ibn Musa informed us, Muawiyah told us, Al-Hasan ibn Jabir told us, on the authority of Al- Miqdam ibn Ma’di Karib Al -Kindi (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) that the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) prohibited certain things on the day of Khaybar: donkeys and other things.” Then he said, “Soon a man will come, reclining on his couch, and he will be told my hadith, and he will say, ‘Between us and you is the Book of Allah.’” Whatever we find in it to  be lawful, we consider it lawful, and whatever we find in it to be forbidden, we consider it forbidden. Verily, what the Apostle of Allah has forbidden is like what Allah Almighty has forbidden.

Muhammad ibn Uyaynah informed us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, on the authority of al-Awza’i, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, who said: “The Sunnah is the judge over the Qur’an, but the Qur’an is not the judge over the Sunnah.”

Muhammad ibn Kathir informed us, on the authority of Al -Awza’i, on the authority of Hassan, who said: “Gabriel used to come down to the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) with the Sunnah, just as he came down to him with the Qur’an.”

Muhammad ibn Kathir informed us, on the authority of al -Awza’i, on the authority of Makhul, who said: “The Sunnah is of two types: a Sunnah which, if followed, is obligatory, and if abandoned, is disbelief; and a Sunnah which, if followed, is virtuous, and  if abandoned, is not inconvenient.”

Sulayman ibn Harb informed us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Ya`la ibn Hakim, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, “That he narrated one day a hadith from the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) and a man said: ‘Is there anything in the Book of Allah that contradicts this?’ He said: ‘I do not see myself narrating to you from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) and then you are making an insinuation about it with the Book of Allah.’ The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  used to May Allah’s prayers and peace be upon him, he knows more about the Book of Allah Almighty than you do.

Nu`aym ibn Hammad informed us, `Abd al-`Aziz ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Ibn `Ajlan, on the authority of `Awn ibn `Abdullah, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) that he said: “When you are told a hadith from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  then think of it as the one who is most prepared, most guided, and most pious.” 193

Abu Nu`aym informed us, Mis`ar told us, on the authority of `Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Abu al-Bakhtari, on the authority of Abu `Abd al -Rahman al-Sulami, on the authority of `Ali (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “If you are told something about the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) then think of it as being more rightly guided, more pious, and more prepared.”

Abu Mamar Ismail ibn Ibrahim informed us, on the authority of Salih ibn Umar, on the authority of Asim ibn Kulayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: Whenever he narrated from the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  he would say: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  said: “Whoever lies about me intentionally, let him take his seat in Hellfire.” So, Ibn Abbas When he spoke, he said: If you hear me speaking about the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) and you do not find it in the Book of Allah, or it is good among the people, then know that I have lied about him.

Abdullah bin Imran informed us, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Sulayman al - Ahwal, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: “The people who are most uninterested in a scholar are his family.”

Asad ibn Musa informed us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of al-Jariri and Abu Maslamah, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “Review hadith, for hadith arouses others.”

Abu Nu`aym informed us, Abu `Awanah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Abu Nadra, on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “Review hadith, for hadith arouses other hadiths.”

Abu Mamar informed us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Said al -Khudri (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  who said: "Review hadith, for hadith arouses others." Abu Mamar informed us, on the authority of Abu Muawiyah, on the authority of al-Amash, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Said, and Ibn Ulayyah,  on the authority of al -Jariri, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, On the authority of Abu Saeed, Abu Maslamah told us, meaning, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Saeed, and there is more discussion about it than this.
Muhammad ibn Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr, who said: Tawus said to me: “Let us go and sit with the people.”

Ismail ibn Aban informed us, Yaqub ibn Abdullah al -Qummi informed us, Ja’far ibn Abi al - Mughira informed us, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas (رضئ تعالی عنه) who said: “Remember this hadith, do not let it slip away from you, for there is nothing like the Qur’an, which is collected and preserved. If you do not remember this hadith, It will escape you, and let none of you say, “I narrated yesterday, so I will no t narrate today.” Rather, narrate yesterday, and narrate today, and narrate tomorrow.

Malik ibn Ismail informed us, Mandal ibn Ali told us, Ja’far ibn Abi al-Mughira told us, Sa’id ibn Jubayr told us, he said: Ibn Abbas  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) said: “Return the hadith and remember it, because if you do not remember it, it will disappear. And let no man say about a hadith that he has narrated, ‘I narrated it to him once,’ because whoever has heard it will increase in knowledge.” He has knowledge of it, and he who has not heard hears.

Al-Hakam ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Abu Awana informed us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Abd al -Rahman ibn Abi Laila, who said: “Discuss, for the revival of hadith is its discussion.”

Qubaysah and Muhammad ibn Yusuf told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al -A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, who said: “Remember the hadith, for its remembrance is its life.” 196
Muhammad ibn Qudamah told us, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Ziyad ibn Sa`d, who said: “Ibn Shihab used to narrate to the Bedouins.”

Muhammad ibn Sa`id informed us, Muhammad ibn Fadil informed us, on the authority of al - A`mash, who said: “Ismail ibn Raja` used to gather the children of the school and narrate to them, being careful about that.”

Abu al-Numan informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd informed us, on the authority of Abu Abdullah al- Shaqri, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: "Tell your hadith to whoever desires it, and whoever does not desire it, for it will become to you as if he were an imam whom you read."

Abu Mamar and Muhammad ibn Said informed us, on the authority of Abd al -Salam, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Ata, on the authority of Ibn Abbas  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: "If you hear a hadith from us, then discuss it among yourselves."
Abu Mamar informed us, on the authority of Hisham, who informed us on the authority of Yunus, who said: “We used to visit Al -Hasan, and when we left him, we would discuss things among ourselves.”

Sadaqah ibn al -Fadl informed us, Abdullah ibn Wahb told us, on the authority of Amr ibn al - Harith, on the authority of Hunayn ibn Abi Hakim, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  who said: “If one of you wants to narrate a hadith, let him repeat it three times.”

Muhammad ibn Said informed us, Muhammad ibn Fadil informed us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Abd al -Rahman ibn Abi Layla, who said: "Reviving hadith is discussing it." Abdullah ibn Shaddad said to him: "May Allah have mercy on you. How many hadiths have you revived in my chest that had died?"

Abdullah ibn Saeed informed us, Muhammad ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of his father, who said: “When Al -Harith ibn Yazid Al-Ukli, Ibn Shubrumah, Al -Qaqa’ ibn Yazid, and Mughirah prayed the last ‘Isha’ prayer, they would sit and study jurisprudence, and nothing would separate them except the dawn call to prayer.”

Malik ibn Ismail told us: I heard Sharik mention, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Ata’, Tawus, and Mujahid, who said: On the authority of two of them: “There is nothing wrong with talking about jurisprudence.”
Muhammad ibn Sa`id told us, `Abd al -Salam told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: “There is nothing wrong with talking about jurisprudence.”

Muhammad ibn Sa`id told us, Hafs told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه)  said: “Studying knowledge for an hour at night is better than spending it all night.”

Abu Mamar and Muhammad ibn Isa informed us, on the authority of Hisham, who informed us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Ata, who said: "We used to visit Jabir ibn Abdullah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) and when we left him, we would discuss things, and Abu al-Zubayr was the one among us who had the best memory of his hadith."

Marwan ibn Muhammad told us: I heard Al -Layth ibn Sa`d say: “Ibn Shihab discussed a hadith one night after the evening meal while he was sitting in a state of ritual purity. He continued to sit in that position until morning.” Marwan said: “He continued to discuss the hadith.”

Abdullah ibn Muhammad informed us, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of al-Zuhri, who said: “Whenever I met Ubayd Allah ibn Abdullah, it was as if I were drowning in a sea.”
Muhammad ibn Humayd told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Uthman ibn Abdullah, who said: “Al-Harith al-Ukli and his companions used to sit together at night and discuss jurisprudence.”

Abu Nu`aym informed us, Abu Isra`il told us, on the authority of `Ata` ibn al -Sa`ib, on the authority of his father, who narrated on the authority of Abu al -Ahwas, on the authority of `Abdullah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) who said: “Review this hadith, for his life is his discussion.”

Abu Nu`aym informed us, Al -Mas`udi narrated to us, on the authority of `Awn, who said: `Abdullah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) said to his companions when they came to him: “Do you sit together?” 200 They said: “We will not abandon that.” He said: “Do you visit each other?” They said: “Yes, O Abu `Abd al-Rahman. One of us may miss his brother, so he will walk to the farthest part of Kufa in search of him until he reaches the end of the city.” He met him and said: “You will not cease to be well as long as you do that.”
Muhammad ibn al -Mubarak told us, al -Walid told us, on the authority of al -Awza’i, on the authority of al -Zuhri, who said: “The scourge of knowledge is forgetfulness and abandoning discussion.”
Ja`far ibn `Awn informed us, Abu `Umais informed us, on the authority of al -Qasim, who said: `Abdullah (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) said: “The plague of hadith is forgetfulness.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Tariq, on the authority of Hakim ibn Jabir, who said: Abdullah said: “Everything has a affliction, and the affliction of knowledge is forgetfulness.”

Abdullah ibn Saeed informed us, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Al -A’mash, who said: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) said: “The scourge of knowledge is forgetfulness, and its loss is that you tell it to other than its people.” 201
Affan informed us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, Abu Hamza al-Thumali told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: “The loss of knowledge is forgetfulness.”
Uthman ibn Umar informed us, Kahams informed us, on the authority of Ibn Buraidah, who said: Ali said: “Review this hadith and visit one another, for if you do not do so, it will be forgotten.”
Bishr ibn al -Hakam told us: I heard Sufyan say: Al -Zuhri said: “I thought I had acquired some knowledge, so I sat with Ubayd Allah, and it was as if I were in a valley.”

Yazid ibn Harun informed us, on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Humayd, who said: It was said to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, may Allah Almighty have mercy on him: “Why don’t you bring the people together on something?” He said: “I would not be pleased if they did not differ.” He said: “Then he wrote to the horizons and to the cities, so that each people would rule according to what their jurists agreed upon.”

Yazid informed us, on the authority of Al -Masudi, on the authority of Awn ibn Abdullah, who said: "I do not like it if the Companions of the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) did not differ, because if they agreed on something and a man abandoned it, he would have abandoned the Sunnah. And if they differed, and a man took the opinion of someone, he would have taken the Sunnah."
Abu Nu`aym informed us, Hasan told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Tawus, who said: “Ibn Abbas sometimes had an opinion, then abandoned it.”

Al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal informed us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, Hisham ibn Urwah told us, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Marwan ibn al-Hakam, who said: Uthman ibn Affan said to me: Umar (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) said to me: I have seen an opinion regarding the serious matter, so if you see that you should follow it, then follow it. Uthman said: “If we follow your opinion, For it is guidance, and if we follow the opinion of the Sheikh before you, then he was a good man of opinion.” He said: And Abu Bakr used to consider him a father.

Ibrahim ibn al -Mundhir al-Hizami informed us, Marwan ibn Muawiyah informed us, Asim al - Ahwal informed us, he said: “I presented the hadiths of jurisprudence to al-Sha’bi, and he approved them for me.”

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir informed us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, he said: I said to Amr ibn Dinar: Did you hear Jabir ibn Abdullah say: The Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  said to a man who passed by the mosque with arrows: “Hold their heads”? He said: Yes.

Ibrahim ibn al -Mundhir informed us, Sufyan told us, he said: I said to Abd al -Rahman ibn al - Qasim: Did you hear your father narrating, on the authority of Aisha, that the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) used to kiss her while he was fasting? He said: Yes.

Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad informed us, Miskeen ibn Bukayr told us, Shu’bah told us, he said: Mansur wrote to me with a hadith, so I met him and said: Shall I narrate it from you? He said: “If I write to you, has it not been that I have narrated it to you?” He said: I asked Ayyub al -Sakhtiyani, and he said: Something like that.

Zakariya ibn Adi informed us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak informed us, on the authority of Mamar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, who said: I showed him a book and said: Shall I narrate it from you? He said: Who narrated it to you other than me?

Ibrahim ibn al -Mundhir al -Hizami informed us, Dawud ibn Ata’, the client of al -Muzaniyyin, informed us, Hisham ibn Urwah informed us, on the authority of his father, who said: “The presentation of the Book and the Hadith are the same.”

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir informed us, Dawud ibn Ata’ informed us, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, who said: “The presentation of the Book and the Hadith are the same.”

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir informed us, Dawud ibn Ata’ told us, he said: “Zayd ibn Aslam used to consider the presentation of the Book and the Hadith to be the same, and Ibn Abi Dhi’b also held the same view.”
Ibrahim told us, Mutarrif told us, on the authority of Malik bin Anas, “He used to see the presentation and the hadith as the same.”

Qabisah informed us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al -A’mash, who said: Ibrahim used to say: He stands on his left. So, I told him on the authority of Sami’ Al -Zayyat, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) made him stand on his right,” and he took hold of him. 205

Muhammad ibn Humayd informed us, Harun ibn al -Mughira narrated to us, on the authority of Anbasa ibn Said, on the authority of Khalid ibn Zayd al-Ansari, on the authority of Aqqar ibn al- Mughira ibn Shuba, on the authority of his father, al-Mughira ibn Shuba, who said: Umar asked the people: Has anyone among you heard from the Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) about the fetus? Then Al-Mughirah ibn Shubah stood up and said: "He ruled that it should be a male or female slave." He also asked the people.  The one in whose favor the judgment was made stood up and said: "The Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  ruled that it should be a male or female slave." He also asked the people. The one against whom the judgment was made stood up and said: "The Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) ruled that it should be a male or female slave." I said: "Are you ruling that it should be a male or female slave?" In it, while he did not eat, nor drink, nor cry, nor speak? That you extend it, for it is more deserving of extension.” The Prophet (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) was about to bring him something with him, so he said, “Do you have a hair?” Umar said, “Had I not heard of the Prophet’s ruling  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  I would have made it a blood money between two blood moneys.”
Saeed bin Aamer told us: Sallam used to mention, on the authority of Ayoub, who said: “If you want to know your teacher’s mistake, sit with someone else.”

Affan informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, Ayyub told us, he said: “We were discussing in Mecca about a man dying, so I said: Its waiting period is from the day the news reaches it, according to the saying of Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and our companions. He said: Then Talq ibn Habib Al-Anazi met me and said: You are generous to me, and you are from the people of a land to which the spring is quick, and I am not…” I trust you. He said: You have said something here that is contrary to the opinion of the people of the town, and I do not trust you. I said: Is there a difference of opinion on this? He said: Yes, her waiting period is from the day of death. I met Sa`id ibn Jubayr and asked him, and he said: Her waiting period is from the day of death. I asked Mujahid, and he said: Her waiting period is from the day of death. I asked `Ata` ibn Abi Rabah, and he said: From The day he died. I asked Abu Qilabah, and he said: From the day he died. I asked Muhammad ibn Sirin, and he said: From the day he died. He said: Nafi’ told me that Ibn Umar  (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) said: From the day he died. I heard  Ikrimah say: From the day he died. He said: Jabir ibn Zayd said: From the day he died. He said: Ibn Abbas used to say: From The day he died. Hammad said: I heard Layth narrate, on the authority of Al-Hakam, that Abdullah bin Masoud said: From the day he died. He said: And Ali said: From the day the news reaches her. Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman said: I say: From the day he died.

Ahmad ibn Humayd informed us, Ibn al -Mubarak told us, on the authority of Mamar, on the authority of Simak ibn al -Fadl, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, on the authority of al - Hakam ibn Masud, who said: We came to Umar regarding the polytheism, but he did not associate partners with Allah. Then we came to him the following year, and he associated partners with Allah. So we said to him: He said: "That was as we had decreed, and this is as we had decreed."

Yaqub ibn Ibrahim informed us, Rawh told us, Hajjaj al -Aswad told us, he said: Ibn Munabbih said: “The people of knowledge in the past were stingy with their knowledge towards the people of this world, so the people of this world would desire their knowled ge, so they would give them their worldly life. But the people of knowledge today have given their knowledge to the people of 207 this world. The people of this world became indifferent to their knowledge, so they were stingy with their worldly possessions.

Yaqub ibn Ibrahim informed us, Muhammad ibn Umar ibn al-Kumait informed us, Ali ibn Wahb al-Hamdani informed us, Ad-Dahhak ibn Musa informed us, saying: “Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik passed by Madinah on his way to Makkah, and he stayed there for a few days. He then said: ‘Is there anyone in Madinah who met any of the Companions of the Prophet  (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) ’? They said to him: Abu Hazim, O Commander of the Faithful. So, he sent for him. When he entered upon him, he said to him: O Abu Hazim, what is this rudeness? Abu Hazim said: O Commander of the Faithful, what rudeness did you see from me? He said: The notables of the people of Medina came to me, and you did not come to me. He said: O Commander of the Faithful, I seek refuge for you in Allah that you say what did not happen, what You knew me before this day, and I have not seen you. He said: So, Sulayman turned to Muhammad ibn Shihab al-Zuhri and said: The old man was r ight, and I was wrong. Sulayman said: O Abu Hazim, why do we hate death? He said: Because you have ruined the Hereafter and built up the world, so you hate to move from prosperity to ruin. He said: You are right, Abu Hazim! How will we approach Allah tomorrow? He said: As for the good-doer, he is like the absent one approaching his family, and as for the evil -doer, he is like the fugitive approaching his master. So, Sulayman wept and said: Would that I knew what we have with Allah. He said: Compare your deeds to the Book of Allah. He said: And what place will I find? He said: # Indeed, the righteous will be in pleasure {13} And indeed, the wicked will be in Hellfire. {14} Surah Al-Infitar, verses 13-14 #, Solomon said: So where is the mercy of Allah, O Abu Hazim? Abu Hazim said: The mercy of Allah is close to the doers of good. Solomon said to him: O Abu Hazim, which of Allah’s servants is the most honored? He said: Those of chivalry and understanding. Solomon said to him: O Abu Hazim, which deeds are best? A bu Hazim said: Performing the obligatory duties while avoiding the forbidden. Sulayman said: Which supplication is most heard? Abu Hazim said: The application of the one who is benevolent to him for the one who is benevolent. He said: Which charity is best? He said: For the needy beggar, and the effort of the poor, in which there is no favor or harm. He said: Which statement is most just? He said: The statement of the truth according to the one who You fear Him or hope for Him. He said: Which of the believers is the most intelligent? He said: A man who acts in obedience to Allah and guides people to it. He said: Which of the believers is the most foolish? He said: A man who deviates from the path of his brother while being unjust, so he sells his afterlife f or the worldly life of someone else. Sulayman said to him: You are right. What do you say about what we are in? He said: O Commander of the Faithful, or Will you excuse me? Solomon said to him: No, but give me some advice. He said: O Commander of the Faith ful, your fathers subjugated the people with the sword and took this kingdom by force without consulting the Muslims or their consent, until they killed a great number of them. They have now departed from it. If you were informed of what they said and what was said to them? So he said to him: A man from among his companions said: What a bad thing you have said, O Abu Hazim. Abu Hazim said: You have lied. Indeed, Allah has taken a covenant from the scholars that they will make it clear to the people and not conceal it. Sulayman said to him: Then how can we reform? He said: You abandon arrogance, hold fast to chivalry, and distribute equally. Sulayman said to him: How can we do what is taken from us? Abu Hazim said: :You take it from its rightful place and place it among its people. Sulayman said to him: Would you like, Abu Hazim, to accompany us so that you may take from us and we may take from you? He said: I seek refuge in Allah. Solomon said to him: Why is that? He said: I fear that if I rely on you a little, Allah will make me taste double in life and double in death. Solomon 209 said to him: Submit your needs to us. He said: Save me from the Fire and admit me to Paradise. Solomon said: That is not up to me. Abu Hazim said: I have no other need of you. He said: Sulayman said to him: Why is that? He said: I fear that if I rely on you a little, Allah will make me taste double in life and double in death. Sulayman said to him: Submit your needs to us. He said: Save me from the Fire and admit me to Paradise. Sulayman said: That is not up to me. Abu Hazim said: Then I have no other need of you. He said: Then pray for me. Abu Hazim said: O Allah, if Solomon is Your friend, then make his path easy for the good of this world and the Hereafter. And if he is Your enemy, then take him by the forelock to what You love and are pleased with. Solomon said to him: Never. Abu Hazim said: I have been brief and at length if you are one of his people. But if you are not one of his people, then what benefit will it bring me to shoot from a bow that has no string? Solomon said to him: Advise me. He said: I  will advise you and I will be brief: Magnify your Lord and keep Him far above seeing you where He has forbidden you or missing you where He has commanded you. So when he left him, he sent him one hundred dinars and wrote to him: Spend it and I have many more like it for you. He said: So, he returned it to him and wrote to him: O Commander of the Faithful, I seek refuge for you in Allah that your asking of me be in jest, or I will return to you with an offering that pleases you, but how can I please myself with it? And he wrote to him: When Moses, son of Imran, came to the water of Midian, he found shepherds there watering their flocks, and he found two young women behind them driving them back. So he asked them, and they said: # We will not water [their flocks] until the shepherds depart, and our father is an old man. {23} So he watered their flocks for them, then he turned away to the shade and said, "My Lord, indeed I, for whatever good You send down to me, am in need." {24} Surah Al-Qasas, verses 23-24 # This is because he was hungry, afraid, and not secure. So he asked his Lord and did not ask people. The shepherds did not realize this, but the two slave girls did. When they returned to their father, they told him the story and what he had said. Their father, who was Shu`ayb, said, “This is a hungry man.” So he said to one of them, “Go and call him.” When she came to him, she honored him and covered her face. And she said: “Indeed, my father invites you that he may reward you for having watered our flocks.” Surah Al-Qasas, Verse 25. But it was hard for Moses when she mentioned: “The reward for having watered our flocks.” And he had no choice but to follow her, for he was among the mountains, hungry and lonely. So when he followed her, the wind blew and she began to flap her clothes on her back, describing her buttocks to him, and she had a buttock. And Moses made He would turn away at one time and lower his gaze at another. When his patience ran out, he called out to her, “O servant of Allah, stand behind me and show me the way you are by saying this.” When he entered upon Shu’ayb, he saw dinner being prepared. Shu’ayb said to him, “Sit down, young man, and eat your dinner.” Moses said to him, “I seek refuge in Allah.” Shu’ayb said to him, “Why?” Are you not hungry? He said: Yes, but I fear that this is compensation for what I watered for them. We are from a family that does not sell anything of our religion for the earth full of gold.
