Shu’ayb said to him: No, young man, but it is my custom and the custom of m y fathers to welcome the guest and feed the food. So Moses sat down and ate. If these hundred dinars are a compensation for what I have narrated that dead animals, blood, and pork are permissible in cases of necessity, and if I have a right to it from the public treasury, then I have counterparts in it, so if you treat us equally, then fine, otherwise I have no need for it.

Abu Uthman al-Basri informed us, on the authority of Abd al -Aziz ibn Muslim al-Qasmali, who informed us that Zayd al-Ammi informed us, on the authority of some of the jurists, that he said: “O man of knowledge, act upon your knowledge, give the excess of your wealth, and withhold the excess of your speech, except for something from the hadith that will benefit you with your Lord. O man of knowledge, that which you have learned and then…” If you do not act upon it, it will cut off your argument and excuse before your Lord when you meet Him. O man of knowledge, what you have been commanded to do of obeying Allah will distract you from what you have been forbidden of disobeying Allah. O man of knowledge do not be strong in the work of others and weak in your own work. O man of knowledge do not let what is for others distract you from what is for you. O man of knowledge. Knowledge, sit with scholars, compete with them, listen to them, and leave disputing with them, O man of knowledge, esteem scholars for their knowledge, and belittle the ignorant for t heir ignorance, and do not distance yourself from them, but bring them close and teach them, O man of knowledge, do not speak in a gathering until you understand it, and do not respond to a man’s statement until you know what he said to you, O man of knowledge, do not be deceived by Allah, nor by people, for to be deceived by Allah is to abandon His command, and to be deceived by people is to follow their desires. Beware of Allah for what He has warned you about Himself, and beware of people and their temptations, O man of knowledge. Indeed, the light of the day is not complete except with the sun, and likewise, wisdom is not complete except with obedience to O man of knowledge, verily, plants are not good without water and soil. Likewise, faith is not good without knowledge and action. O man of knowledge, every traveler has provisions, and when he needs provisions, he will find what he has taken. Likewise, every worker, when he needs his work in the Hereafter, will find what he did in this world. O man of knowledge, If Allah wants to urge you to worship Him, then know that He only wants to show you your honor in His sight. So do not turn to someone other than Him, lest you return from His honor to His humiliation. O man of knowledge, if you move stones and ir on, it is easier for you than to speak to someone who does not understand your speech. The example of the one who speaks to someone who does not understand his speech is like the example of the one who calls out The dead and sets the table for the people of the graves

Abdul Malik bin Sulayman Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Antaki informed us, on the authority of Abbad bin Abbad Al -Khawwas Al-Shami Abu Utbah, who said: “As for what follows, be rational, for reason is a blessing. Many a rational person’s heart has been preoccupied w ith thinking deeply 212 about what is harmful to him, from benefiting from what he needs, until he has become heedless of that. Among the bounty of A person’s intellect is to refrain from looking into that which is not worth looking into, so that his superior intellect does not b ecome a burden upon him in not competing with those who are below him in righteous deeds. Or a man whose heart is preoccupied with an innovation in which he imitates in his religion men who are below the Companions of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه وآله وسلم)  or he is content with his opinion in that which he sees as the only guidance in it and does not see as misguidance. Except by abandoning it. He claims that he took it from the Qur’an, while he is calling for separation from the Qur’an. Was there not bearers of the Qur’an before him and before his companions who acted upon its clear verses and believed in its ambiguous verses? And they were from him on a beacon of clarity of the path, and the Qur’an was the imam of the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم)  and the Apostle of Allah (صلى اللہ علیه و آله وسلم) was the imam of his companions, and his companions were imams for those who came after them, men who were well-known and well-known in the countries, and who agreed in refuting the people of whims despite the differences that existed between them, and the  companions of Their whims, in their opinion, led them on various paths that deviated from the straight path, and departed from it. Their guides led them astray into misleading matters, and they persisted in them, being arbitrary in their delusion. Whenever Satan brought them an innovation in their misguidance, they moved from it to another, because they did not seek the traces of the predecessors, and they did not They follow the example of the Muhajireen. It was reported on the authority of Omar that he said to Ziyad: Do you know what destroys Islam? A scholar’s slip, a hypocrite’s argument with the Qur’an, and misguided imams. Fear Allah and what has happened among your reciters and the people of your mosques of backbiting, gossiping, and walking among people with two faces and two tongues. It has been mentioned that whoever is two -faced in this world will be two -faced in Hellfire. The one who backbites you will meet you and backbite someone in your presence whom he thinks you love. His presence with the one who is present is like the presence of brothers, and his absence from the one from whom he is absent is like the absence of enemies. Whoever is present among them has the advantage, and  whoever is absent among them has no advantage. A sanctity, he tempts those who are present with praise and backbites those who are absent from him. O servants of Allah, is there not among the people a wise person or a reformer who can restrain this man from his plot and prevent him from slandering his Muslim brother? Rather, he knew their desires in what he wa lked with to them, so he was able to control them and they were able to control him in his need, so he ate his religion along with their religions. S o, by Allah, by Allah, defend the sanctity of your absent ones, and hold your tongues from them except for good, and advise Allah regarding your nation, since you are the bearers of the Book and the Sunnah, for the Book does not speak until it speaks.  By it, and the Sunnah is not implemented until it is implemented, so when will the ignorant learn if the scholar remains silent, and does not denounce what is apparent, and does not command what is abandoned? And Allah has taken a covenant from those who w ere given the Scripture: “You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it.” Fear Allah, for you are living in a time in which piety has become weak, humility has become scarce, and knowledge has been carried by its corruptors. They love to be known fo r carrying it and hate to be known for wasting it. So, they speak therein according to their own desires, because they have introduced errors into it and distorted the words from what they intended. They abandoned the truth and adopted falsehood. Their sins are sins for which no forgiveness is sought, and their shortcomings are shortcomings for which no one acknowledges. How can the one seeking evidence and guidance find his way if the evidence is confusing? They loved the world and hated the status of its people, so they shared their lives, and separated themselves from them in speech, 213 and defended themselves with speech from being attributed to their deeds. They did not disavow what they denied, and they did not enter into what they attributed to themselves, because the one who acts according to the truth is speaking, even if he is sile nt. It has been mentioned that Allah Almighty says: I I do not accept all the words of the wise, but I look at his concern and his desires. If his concern and his desire are for Me, I make his silence praise and reverence for Me, even if he does not speak.  Allah the Most High said: “The example of those who were entrusted with the Torah and then did not take it on is like that of a donkey who carries volumes.” Surah Al-Jumu’ah, verse 5: “Books.” And he said: “Take what We have given you with strength.” Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 63: He said: Acting according to what is in it, and do not be satisfied with the Sunnah by attributing it in words without acting upon it, because attributing the Sunnah without acting upon it is lying in words while neglecting the acti on. And do not criticize innovations by adorning themselves with their defects, because the corruption of the people of innovations does not add to your righteousness. And do not criticize them out of transgression against their people, because transgression is from the corruption of your souls. It is not appropriate for a doctor to treat the sick with what cures them and makes him sick, because when he becomes sick, he will be preoccupied with his illness and not with treating them. Rather, he should seek health for himself so that he will be able to treat the sick. So let your matter in what you disapprove of your brothers be a consideration from you for yourselves and sincere advice from you. For your Lord, and out of compassion for your brothers, and that you be more concerned with your own faults than you are with the faults of others, and that some of you should wean one another with sincere advice, and that whoever offers it to you and accepts it from you should be appreciated by you. Umar ibn al - Khattab (رضئ اللہ تعالی عنه) said: “May Allah have mercy on whoever points out my faults to me.” You love to say: So, it is possible for you, and if you were told the same as what you said, you would become angry. You find fault with people in the things you disapprove of, and you do the same. Do you not love for it to be taken against you? Question your own opinion and the opinion of the people of your time, and verify before you speak, and learn before you act. For there will come a time when truth and falsehood will be confused, and good will be ev il, and evil will be good. How many people seek to draw near to Allah through doing things that distance them from Him, and how many seek to be beloved to Him through doing things that anger Him? Allah the Most High said: Is he who has had his evil deeds m ade attractive to him so that he sees them as good? Surah Fatir, verse 8 # So you must stop at doubts until the truth is clearly presented to you with clear evidence, for indeed, he who enters into that which he does not know without knowledge is a sinner. And whoever looks to Allah, Allah will look to him. Stick to the Qur’an, complete it, and lead people in prayer with it, and you must seek the traces of those who came before in it, even if the rabbis The monks did not fear the loss of their ranks and the  corruption of their status by establishing the Book through their actions and clarifying what they distorted or concealed. But when they contradicted the Book through their actions, they sought to deceive their people about what they had done, fearing tha t their ranks would be corrupted and that their corruption would become clear to the people. So, they distorted the Book through interpretation and what they did not. They could distort it, so they concealed it. They kept silent about what they did to preserve their status, and they kept silent about what their people did to please them. And Allah took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture: “You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it.” Rather, they agreed on it and were gentle with them regarding it.

Abu Asim narrated to us, on the authority of Zakariya ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abdullah ibn Saifi, on the authority of Abu Ma’bad, on the authority of Ibn Abbas ( ): When the Prophet ( ) sent Mu’adh ( ) to Yemen, he said: “You are coming to a people of the Book, so call them to bear witness that there is no Allah but Allah and that Muhammad is the Apostle of Allah. If they obey…” You have the right to do so. So tell them that Allah has enjoined upon them five prayers every day and night. If they obey you in that, then tell them that Allah has enjoined upon them charity from their wealth, to be taken from their rich and given to their poor. If they obey you in that, then beware of their best wealth, and beware of the supplication of the oppressed. For there is no veil for her except Allah.

Hashim ibn al-Qasim informed us, Shu`bah narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ziyad, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah ( ) narrating, on the authority of the Prophet ( ) that he said: “The poor person is not the one who is turned away by a morsel or two, or a piece of bread or two, or a date or two, but the poor person is the one who has no wealth that would make him independent and is too shy to ask.” People are persistent, or people are not persistent.

Ya`la ibn `Ubayd informed us, `Abd al-Malik informed us, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir ( ), who said: The Prophet ( ) said: “There is no owner of camels, cows, or sheep who does not pay their dues, except that they will be made to sit on the Day of Resurrection in a turbid plain, trampled by hoofed camels, and gored by horned camels. On that Day there will be no mounts on it.” Nor one with a broken horn.” They said: “O Apostle of Allah, what are its rights?” He said: “Letting its stallion mount, lending its bucket, giving it a gift, milking it at watering places, and carrying a load on it in the cause of Allah.”

Bishr ibn al-Hakam narrated to us, Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn Abdullah ( ) say: I heard the Apostle of Allah ( ) say: “There is no owner of camels who does not treat them according to their rights, except that on the Day of Resurrection they will be more numerous than they ever were, and a clearing will be prepared for them.” And there is no owner of cows who does not do their right with them, except that on the Day of Resurrection they will come more than they ever were, and they will be seated for them in a murmuring valley, butting them with their horns and trampling them with their legs. And there is no owner of sheep who does not do their rights with them, except that on the Day of Resurrection they will come more than they ever were, and they will be seated for them in a murmuring valley. They will butt him with their horns and trample him with their hooves. There is no one among them who is barren or has a broken horn, and no one who has a treasure who does not do what is right with it, except that his treasure will come on the Day of Resurrection, a brave, bald man pursuing him with his mouth wide open. When it comes to him, he will flee from him, and he will call out to him, “Take your treasure that you have hidden.” He said: “I am independent of him. When he sees that he must do it, he puts his hand in his mouth and bites it like a stallion.” Abu al-Zubayr said: “I heard Ubayd ibn Umair say this, then we asked Jabir ibn Abdullah, and he said the same as Ubayd ibn Umair.”

He said: Abu Al-Zubayr said: I heard Ubaid bin Umair say: A man said: O Apostle of Allah, what is the right of camels? He said: “Milking it while it is at water, lending its bucket, lending its stallion, giving it as a gift, and carrying a load on it in the way of Allah.” Al-Hasan ibn al-Rabi’ informed us, Abu al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of al-Ma’rur ibn Suwayd, on the authority of Abu Dharr ( ), on the authority of the Prophet ( ) with some of this hadith.

Al-Hakam ibn al-Mubarak informed us, ‘Abbad ibn al-‘Awwam and Ibrahim ibn Sadaqah told us, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Husayn, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Ibn Umar ( ), that the Prophet ( ) prescribed the zakat. It was for sheep: for every forty-grazing animals, one sheep up to one hundred and twenty. If the number increases, then two sheep up to two hundred are due. If it increases, then three sheep are due up to three hundred. If it increases by one sheep, then only three sheep are due until it reaches four hundred. If it reaches four hundred sheep, then one sheep is due for every hundred. No old animal, no one with a defect, and no one with a flaw are to be taken in charity.

Al-Hakam ibn Musa informed us, Yahya ibn Hamza told us, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Khawlani, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, that the Apostle of Allah ( ) wrote to the people of Yemen with Amr ibn Hazm: “In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, from Muhammad, the Prophet.” To Shurahbil ibn Abd Kulal, Al-Harith ibn Abd Kulal, and Nu`aym ibn Abd Kulal, for forty sheep, one sheep each until it reaches one hundred and twenty. If it exceeds one hundred and twenty, then two sheep are due until it reaches two hundred. If it exceeds one sheep, then three sheep are due until it reaches three hundred. So what? He added, “For every hundred sheep, there is one sheep.” Bishr ibn al-Hakam told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Ma’mar told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, that the Prophet ( ) wrote a letter to them, and he mentioned something similar.

Ya`la ibn `Ubayd narrated to us, Al-A`mash narrated to us, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Masruq and Al-A`mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: Mu`adh ( ) said: “The Apostle of Allah ( ) sent me to Yemen and ordered me to take from every forty an old cow, and from every thirty a young male or female camel.”

Asim ibn Yusuf informed us, Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Mu’adh ( ), who said: “The Apostle of Allah ( ) sent me to Yemen and ordered me to take from among the cows thirty year-old Tab’i’ cows and forty old cows.” Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, something similar.

Al-Hakam ibn al-Mubarak informed us, ‘Abbad ibn al-‘Awwam and Ibrahim ibn Sadaqah told us, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Husayn, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar ( ), that the Prophet ( ) wrote down the zakat, but it was not given to his governors until the Apostle of Allah ( ) died. When he died, Abu Bakr took it and worked on it. And after him, when Abu Bakr died, Umar took it and implemented it after them. Umar was killed while it was still attached to his sword or his will. And in the “zakat on camels” it was: for every five, a sheep up to twenty-five. And when it reaches twenty-five, then a young female camel is due up to thirty-five. And if there is no young female camel, A male camel that has given birth, and if it is more than that, then a bint labun is given to it up to forty-five. If it is more than that, then a hiqah is given to it up to sixty. If it is more than that, then a jadh’ah is given to it up to seventy-five. If it is more than that, then two bint labun is given to it up to ninety. If it is more than that, then two hiqahs are given to it up to one hundred and twenty. If it is more than that, then a Every fifty is a Hiqqah, and every forty is a one-year-old female camel.” Muhammad ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Husayn, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, on the authority of the Prophet ( ) something similar.

Al-Hakam ibn Musa informed us, Yahya ibn Hamza informed us, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Khawlani, al-Zuhri informed me, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, that the Apostle of Allah ( ) wrote with Amr ibn Hazm to Shurahbil ibn Abd Kulal and al-Harith ibn Abd Kulal and Nu'aym ibn Abd Kulal said: “I give away five dirhams for every five awq of silver, and if it is more than that, then for every forty dirhams there is one dirham, and there is nothing for anything less than five awq.”

Al-Mu'alla ibn Asad informed us, Abu 'Awana told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of 'Asim ibn Damrah, on the authority of 'Ali, who traced it back to the Prophet ( ) who said: "I have pardoned the zakat on horses and slaves. Give the zakat on slaves, one dirham for every forty dirhams, and there is nothing on ninety or one hundred, until it reaches two hundred."

Al-Aswad ibn Amir informed us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Uthman al-Thaqafi, on the authority of Abu Laila (he is al-Kindi), on the authority of Suwayd ibn Ghafla, who said: The tax collector of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) came to us, so I took his hand and read in his covenant: “That what is separated should not be brought together, and what is gathered should not be separated, for fear of the charity.”

Abu Asim informed us, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abdullah ibn Saifi, on the authority of Abu Ma’bad, the client of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that when the Prophet ( ) sent Mu’adh to Yemen, he said: “Beware of their most valuable wealth.”

Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, he said: Abdullah ibn Dinar informed me, he said: I heard Sulayman ibn Yasar narrating, on the authority of Irak ibn Malik, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet ( ) who said: "There is no zakat on a Muslim's horse or his slave."

Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Amr ibn Yahya, who said: My father informed me, on the authority of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, on the authority of the Prophet ( ) who said: "There is no zakat on less than five wasqs, no zakat on less than five awqs, and no zakat on less than five camels." Abu Muhammad said: A wasq is sixty sa’s. A sa’ is two and a half manwans according to the people of Hijaz, and four amna’s according to the people of Iraq.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail ibn Umayyah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban, on the authority of Yahya ibn Umarah, on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri ( ), who said: The Apostle of Allah ( ) said: “There is no zakat on less than five wasqs of grain or dates, nor is there zakat on less than five awqs, nor is there zakat on less than five A herd is a charity

Al-Hakam ibn Musa informed us, Yahya ibn Hamza informed us, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Khawlani, al-Zuhri informed me, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, that the Apostle of Allah ( ) wrote with Amr ibn Hazm to Shurahbil ibn Abd Kulal and al-Harith ibn Abd Kulal and Nu'aym ibn Abd Kulal said: “For every five awq of silver, there are five dirhams, and whatever is more, then for every forty dirhams there is one dirham, and there is nothing for anything less than five awq.”

Sa'id ibn Mansur informed us, Ismail ibn Zakariya told us, on the authority of al-Hajjaj ibn Dinar, on the authority of al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah, on the authority of Hujayyah ibn 'Adi, on the authority of Ali: Al-Abbas asked the Apostle of Allah ( ) about paying his zakat in advance before it becomes due, and he granted permission for that. Abu Muhammad said: I accept it, and I see no harm in paying zakat in advance.

Muhammad ibn al-Tufayl informed us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Amir, on the authority of Fatima bint Qais, who said: I heard the Apostle of Allah ( ) say: “I have a right to your wealth other than zakat.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Isra'il informed us, Abu al-Juwayriyyah al-Jarmi informed us, that Ma'n ibn Yazid told him, saying: I, my father, and my grandfather pledged allegiance to the Apostle of Allah ( ). He proposed marriage to me, and I took my case to him. My father Yazid used to bring out dinars to give in charity, and he placed them with a man in the mosque. So I came So I took it and brought it to him. He said, “By Allah, I did not mean you by it.” So I took the matter to the Apostle of Allah ( ) and he said, “You will have what you intended, Yazid, and you will have what you took, Ma’n.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf and Abu Nu'aym informed us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of Rayhan ibn Yazid, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: The Apostle of Allah ( ) said: "Charity is not permissible for a rich person or for one who has a sound heart and is healthy." Abu Muhammad said: He means a strong person.

Yazid ibn Harun informed us, Sharik informed us, on the authority of Hakim ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Apostle of Allah ( ) said: “Whoever asks about something while he is wealthy will come on the Day of Resurrection with scratches, bruises, or abrasions on his face.” It was said: “O Apostle of Allah, what is wealth?” He said: “Fifty dirhams or its value in gold.” Abu Asim and Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hakim ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah, on the authority of the Prophet ( ) in a similar manner.

Hashim ibn al-Qasim informed us, Shu'bah told us, Muhammad ibn Ziyad told me, he said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: Al-Hasan took a date from the charity dates and put it in his mouth, so the Prophet ( ) said: "Kikh, Kikh, throw it away. Don't you realize that we do not eat charity?"

Al-Aswad ibn Amir informed us, Zuhair told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Isa, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Abi Laila, who said: I was with the Prophet ( ) and al-Hasan ibn Ali was with him. He took a date from the charity dates, snatched it from him, and said: “Do you not know that charity is not permissible for us?”

Sa'id ibn Mansur informed us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah told us, on the authority of 'Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, on the authority of his brother, on the authority of Mu'awiyah, who said: The Apostle of Allah ( ) said: "Do not be insistent in asking me, for by Allah, if anyone asks me for something and I give it to him unwillingly, it will be blessed for him."

Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Raqashi informed us, Yazid - he is Ibn Zurai' - told us, Sa'id informed us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, on the authority of Ma'dan ibn Abi Talha, on the authority of Thawban, the freed slave of the Apostle of Allah ( ) that the Apostle of Allah ( ) said: "Whoever asks people something while he is independent of it, it will be a disgrace in his life." His face

Al-Hakam ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Malik told us, from Ibn Shihab, from Ata’ ibn Yazid al- Laythi, from Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, that some of the Ansar asked the Apostle of Allah ( ) and he gave them. Then they asked him again, and he gave them, until he ran out of what he had. Then he said, “Whatever good I have, I will not withhold from you. And whoever…” Whoever seeks chastity, Allah will keep him chaste. Whoever seeks self-sufficiency, Allah will make him self-sufficient. Whoever is patient, Allah will make him patient. No one has been given a gift better and more comprehensive than patience.

Abdullah ibn Salih told us: Al-Layth told me, Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Salim, that he said: Abdullah said: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab say: The Apostle of Allah ( ) would give me something, and I would say: Give it to someone who is more in need of it than I. The Apostle of Allah ( ) said: “Take, and whatever Allah has given you of this wealth, as long as you are neither extravagant nor begging, then take it, but whatever you are not, then do not pursue it for your own benefit.” Al-Hakam ibn Nafi' informed us, on the authority of Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamza, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, who said: As-Sa'ib ibn Yazid informed me that Huwaytib ibn Abd Al-Uzza informed him that Abdullah ibn Al-Sa'di informed him, on the authority of Umar, something similar. Abu al-Walid informed us, al-Layth told us, on the authority of Bukayr, on the authority of Busr ibn Sa`id, on the authority of Ibn al-Sa`di, who said: `Umar appointed me, and he mentioned something similar to it.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, on the authority of al-Awza’i, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyib and ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, that Hakim ibn Hizam said: I asked the Prophet ( ) and he gave me something. Then I asked him again, and he gave me something. Then I asked him again, and he gave me something. Then I asked him again, and he said: “O Hakim, this wealth is green and sweet. Whoever takes it…” “Whoever takes it with generosity of soul, it will be blessed for him, but whoever takes it with gluttony of soul, it will not be blessed for him, and he will be like the one who eats and is not satisfied.”

Abdullah ibn Salih informed us, Al-Layth told me, Hisham told me, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard the Apostle of Allah ( ) say: “The best charity is that which you give from your surplus wealth. Let one of you begin with those whom he supports.”

Sulayman ibn Harb informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Ayyub, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, who said: I heard the Apostle of Allah ( ) say: “The upper hand is better than the lower hand.” He said: “The upper hand is the hand of the giver, and the lower hand is the hand of the beggar.”

Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Amr ibn Uthman narrated to us, he said: I heard Musa ibn Talhah mention, on the authority of Hakim ibn Hizam, he said: The Apostle of Allah ( ) said: “The best charity is that given from one’s surplus wealth, and the upper hand is better than the lower hand and start with those under your care.”

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi informed us, Shu’bah told us, he said: Sulayman informed me, he said: I heard Abu Wa’il narrating, on the authority of Amr ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Zaynab, the wife of Abdullah, that she said: The Apostle of Allah ( ) said: “O women, give in charity, even if it is from your jewelry.”

Abdullah was light-handed, so I came to the Apostle of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) to ask him. I happened to meet Zaynab, a woman from the Ansar, who asked me what I was asking about. So I said to Bilal, "Ask the Apostle of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) where I should put my charity: on Abdullah, or among my relatives?" He asked the Prophet ( ) "Which Zayanib?" He said, "The wife of Abdullah." He said, "She has two rewards: the reward of kinship and the reward of charity."

Al-Hakam ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Malik told us, from Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Talha, from Anas, who said: Abu Talha had the most wealth among the Ansar in Madinah in date palms, and his most beloved property was Bayruha, which faced the mosque. He - meaning the Prophet ( ) - used to enter it and drink from its water. Good. Anas said: When this verse was revealed: “By no means will you attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love. And whatever you spend - indeed, Allah is Knowing of it.” Surah Al Imran, verse 92, he said: “The most beloved of my possessions to me is Bayruha’, and it is a charity for the sake of Allah. I hope for its righteousness and its storage with Allah. So, spend it, O Apostle of Allah, wherever you wish.” The Apostle of Allah ( ) said, "Good! That is profitable or fragrant wealth. I have heard what you said about it, and I think you should allocate it to your closest relatives." Abu Talha said, "I will do so, O Apostle of Allah." So, Abu Talha divided it among his paternal cousins.

Muhammad ibn Bashar informed us, Muadh ibn Hisham informed us, my father informed us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Hayyaj ibn Imran, on the authority of Imran ibn Husayn ( ), who said: “The Apostle of Allah ( ) never addressed us except that he commanded us to give charity and forbade us from mutilation.”

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi informed us, Shu'bah informed us, Amr ibn Murrah informed me, he said: I heard Khaithamah, on the authority of Adi ibn Hatim, on the authority of the Prophet ( ) who said: "Protect yourselves from the Fire, even if it is with half a date in charity. If you cannot find that, then with a kind word."

Abdur-Rahman ibn Ibrahim al-Dimashqi Duhaim informed us, Saeed ibn Maslamah told us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Umayyah, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abdur- Rahman ibn Abi Lubabah, that Abu Lubabah informed him that when the Apostle of Allah ( ) was pleased with him, he said: O Apostle of Allah, part of my repentance is that I leave the home of my people. And I will live with you, and I will give away some of my wealth as charity for the sake of Allah and His Apostle. The Apostle of Allah ( ) said: “A third will suffice for you.”

Ya`la and Ahmad ibn Khalid informed us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of `Asim ibn `Umar ibn Qatadah, on the authority of Mahmud ibn Labid, on the authority of Jabir ibn `Abdullah, who said: While we were with the Apostle of Allah ( ) a man came with an egg-sized piece of gold that he had found in one of the battles. Ahmad said: In one of the Mines, and this is correct. He said: O Apostle of Allah, take it from me as charity, for by Allah I have no wealth other than it. So, he turned away from him. Then he came to him from his left corner and said the same. Then he came to him from in front of him and said the same. Then he said: “Bring it,” angry. So he threw it at him in a way that if it had hit him it would have hurt him or hamstrung him. Then he said: “He deliberately One of you, with his wealth, does not own anything else, so he gives it in charity, then sits begging from people. Charity is only from one's surplus wealth. Take what is yours; we have no need of it." So, the man took his wealth and left. Abu Muhammad said: Malik used to say: When a man devotes his wealth to the poor, he gives a third of his wealth in charity.

Abu Nu'aym informed us, Hisham ibn Sa'd narrated to us, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of his father, who said: I heard Umar say: The Apostle of Allah ( ) commanded us to give charity, and at that time I had some money with me, so I said: Today I will outshine Abu Bakr if I ever outshine him. He said: So, I brought half of my wealth, and the Apostle of Allah ( ) said: “What have you left for your family?” I said: “The same.” He said: So, Abu Bakr brought everything he had, and he said: “O Abu Bakr, what have you left for your family?” So, he said.

Khalid ibn Makhlad informed us, Malik told us, from Nafi', from Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: "The Apostle of Allah ( ) imposed Zakat al-Fitr of Ramadan as a sa' of dates or a sa' of barley on every free and slave, male or female, among the Muslims." Abu Muhammad was asked: "Do you hold this view?" He said: "Malik used to hold this view."

Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ubaydullah, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, who said: “The Apostle of Allah ( ) ordered that the zakat al-fitr be given on behalf of every young and old, free and slave, as a sa’ of barley or a sa’ of dates.” Ibn ‘Umar said: “The people equated it with two mudds of wheat.”

Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us, Dawud ibn Qays narrated to us, on the authority of Iyad ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, who said: “When the Apostle of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was among us, we used to pay Zakat al-Fitr on behalf of every young and old, free and slave, one sa’ of food, or one sa’ of dates, or one sa’ of barley, or one sa’ of dried yogurt, or one sa’ of Raisins, and this continued until Muawiyah came to us in Medina as a pilgrim or a performer of Umrah. He said: “I see two mudds of Samra’ al-Sham equal to a sa’ of dates.” So the people adopted that. Abu Sa’id said: “As for me, I will continue to give it as I used to give it.” Abu Muhammad said: “I see a sa’ of everything.”

Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us, Malik narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Iyad ibn Abdullah ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Sarh, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: "We used to pay Zakat al- Fitr in Ramadan as a sa' of food, or a sa' of dates, or a sa' of barley, or a sa' of raisins, or a sa' of dried yogurt." Ubaydullah bin Musa informed us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Zayd bin Aslam, on the authority of Iyad bin Abdullah, on the authority of Abu Sa`id, who said: We used to give during the time of the Prophet ( ) and he mentioned something similar.

Ahmad ibn Khalid informed us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Shimasa, who said: I heard Uqbah ibn Amir say: I heard the Apostle of Allah ( ) say: “The tax collector will not enter Paradise.” He said: Abu Muhammad said: He means a tax collector.

Asim ibn Yusuf informed us, Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Mu’adh, who said: “The Apostle of Allah ( ) sent me to Yemen and ordered me to take one-tenth of the fruits that were watered by rain, and half of one-tenth of what was watered by a waterwheel.”

Khalid ibn Makhlad informed us, Malik told us, from Ibn Shihab, from Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, and Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah ( ), from the Prophet ( ) who said: “The wound of a mute animal is a compensation, a well is a compensation, a mine is a compensation, and on the treasure there is a fifth.”

Abu al-Yaman al-Hakam ibn Nafi' informed us, Shu'ayb informed us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, who narrated to me from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, on the authority of Abu Humayd al-Ansari, then al-Sa'idi, that he informed him that the Prophet ( ) appointed a worker to collect the charity. When the worker had finished his work, he came to him and said, "O Apostle of Allah, this is what is for you, and this was given to me as a gift." The Prophet ( ) said: “Why didn’t you stay in your father’s and mother’s house and see if you would be given something as a gift or not?” Then the Prophet ( ) stood on the pulpit one evening after the prayer, recited the Shahada (testimony of faith) and praised Allah as He deserved. Then he said: “Why don’t we employ a worker and he comes to us and says: ‘This is from your work and this was given to me?’” Why doesn't he stay in his father's and mother's house and see if he will be guided or not? By the One in Whose Hand is Muhammad’s soul, none of you takes anything from it as a bribe, except that he will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying it on his neck. If it is a camel, he will bring it roaring, if it is a cow, he will bring it mooing, and if it is a sheep, he will bring it bleating. I have conveyed the message.” Abu Humayd said: Then the Apostle of Allah ( ) raised his hands until we Let us look at the whiteness of his armpits. Abu Humayd said: Zayd ibn Thabit heard that with me from the Prophet ( ) so ask him.

Amr ibn Awn informed us, Hisham informed us, on the authority of Dawud and Mujalid, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Jarir, who said: The Apostle of Allah ( ) said: “When the one who confirms comes to you, let him not leave you except while he is pleased with you.” Muhammad ibn Uyaynah narrated to me, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al- Fazari, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Amir, on the authority of Jarir, on the authority of the Prophet ( ) something similar to it.

Al-Hakam ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Malik informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Amr ibn Muadh al-Ashhali, from his grandmother, who was called Hawwa, who said: The Apostle of Allah ( ) said: “O Muslim women, let none of you belittle a gift to her neighbor, even if it is a burnt leg of a sheep.”

Abu Nu`aym informed us, Aban ibn `Abdullah al-Bajali informed us, `Uthman ibn Abi Hazim informed us, on the authority of Sakhr ibn al-`Aylah, who said: The aunt of al-Mughirah ibn Shu`bah was taken prisoner, so she came to the Apostle of Allah ( ). The Prophet ( ) asked his aunt, and he said: “O Sakhr, when people embrace Islam, they are protected.” Their wealth and blood, so give it to them.” There was a water source for Banu Sulaym, and they converted to Islam. They asked him about it, so he called me and said, “O Sakhr, when people convert to Islam, they protect their wealth and blood, so give it to them.” So I gave it. Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Aban ibn Abdullah informed us, Uthman ibn Abi Hazim informed me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather Sakhr, longer than the hadith of Abu Nu`aym.

Sa'id ibn al-Mughirah informed us, on the authority of 'Isa ibn Yunus, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa'id, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Yasar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah ( ), who said: The Apostle of Allah ( ) said: "No man gives charity from lawful earnings - and Allah does not accept anything but that which is lawful - except that He places it in the Hand of the Most Merciful. Indeed, Allah increases for one of you the date is like one of you raising his foal or his young camel until it becomes like Uhud.”

Abu al-Rabi' al-Zahrani narrated to us, Ismail ibn Ja'far narrated to us, on the authority of al-Ala', on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah ( ), that the Apostle of Allah ( ) said: "Charity does not decrease wealth, and Allah does not increase a servant's forgiveness except in honor, and no one humbles himself before Allah except that Allah raises him up."

Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us, Bahz ibn Hakim told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: I heard the Apostle of Allah ( ) say: “For every grazing camel, there is a one-year-old camel for every forty. No camel shall be separated from its account. Whoever gives it to trade with it, he shall have its reward, and whoever withholds it, we shall take it and half of his wealth, as a firm determination from by the will of Allah, nothing of it is permissible for the family of Muhammad.

Musaddad and Abu Nu`aym narrated: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated from Harun ibn Ri`ab, from Kinanah ibn Nu`aym, from Qubaysah ibn Mukhariq al-Hilali, who said: I carried a load and came to the Prophet ( ) to ask him about it. He said: “Stay, Qubaysah, until the zakat comes to us, and we will order it for you.” Then he said: "O Qubaysah, begging is not permissible except for one of three: A man who has taken on a burden and begging is permissible for him, so he asks until he obtains it, then he stops. A man who is struck by a disaster that sweeps away his wealth, so begging is permissible for him, so he asks until he obtains a livelihood, or he said: a full livelihood. A man who is afflicted with poverty until three of his people say: The wise man among his people: So-and-so has been afflicted with poverty, so he has been permitted to beg, so he asks until he obtains a livelihood, or a sufficient livelihood, then he stops. Anything other than these from begging is ill-gotten gain, O Qubaysah, and its owner eats it ill-gotten.

Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of 'Abbad ibn al-'Awwam, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Husayn, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ayyub ibn Bashir, on the authority of Hakim ibn Hizam, that a man asked the Prophet ( ) about charity, which is best. He said, "To a shunned relative."

Abu Hatim al-Basri informed us, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Hafsah bint Sirin, on the authority of Umm al-Raih bint Sulay’, on the authority of Salman ibn ‘Amir al-Dabbi, who mentioned that the Prophet ( ) said: “Charity given to a poor person is charity, and it is two things given to a relative: charity and upholding the ties of kinship.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, who said: I heard it from al- Thawri, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Hafsah bint Sirin, on the authority of al- Rubaab, on the authority of Salman ibn Amir al-Dabbi, who said: “Charity given to a poor person is charity, but it is two things given to a relative: charity and upholding the ties of kinship.”

Khalid ibn Makhlad informed us, Malik told us, on the authority of Wahb ibn Kaysan, on the authority of Umar ibn Abi Salamah, that the Prophet ( ) said to him: “Say Bismillah and eat from what is in front of you.”

Yazid ibn Harun informed us, Hisham informed us, on the authority of Budayl, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umair, on the authority of Ummul Momineen Ummul Momineen Aisha ( ), that the Prophet ( ) was eating food with six of his companions. Then a Bedouin came and ate it in two bites. The Prophet ( ) said: “If he had mentioned the name of Allah, it would have been sufficient for you. So, if one of you eats, let him mention the name of Allah. If he forgets to mention the name of Allah, let him say: “In the name of Allah ( ) at the beginning and at the end.” Bundar informed us, Muadh ibn Hisham told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Budayl, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umair, on the authority of Umm Kulthum, on the authority of Ummul Momineen Ummul Momineen Aisha ( ), with this hadith.

Musa ibn Khalid informed us, Isa ibn Yunus informed us, on the authority of Safwan ibn Amr, who informed us on the authority of Abdullah ibn Busr ( ), who had been a short companion of the Prophet ( ), who said: My father said to my mother: Why don’t you make some food for the Apostle of Allah ( )? So, she made tharidah and said with his hand, "Minimize." My father went and called him. The Apostle of Allah ( ), placed his hand on the top of it and said, "Take it in the name of Allah." So, they took it from its sides. When they had eaten, he supplicated for them, saying, "O Allah, forgive them, have mercy on them, and bless their provision."

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Asadi informed us, Thawr told us, on the authority of Khalid ibn Ma'dan, on the authority of Abu Umamah ( ), who said: Whenever the Apostle of Allah ( ), ate or drank, he would say: "Praise be to Allah, abundant, good, blessed praise, not ungrateful, not bid farewell, and not independent of our Lord."

Nu`aym ibn Hammad informed us, on the authority of `Abd al-`Aziz ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Abdullah ibn Abi Hurrrah, on the authority of his uncle, on the authority of Sinan ibn Sunnah, who said: The Apostle of Allah ( ), said: “The grateful eater is like the patient faster.”

Ishaq ibn Isa narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah informed us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas ( ), on the authority of the Prophet ( ) who said: “When one of you eats, let him lick his three fingers.”

Amr ibn Awn informed us, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas ( ), that the Prophet ( ) said: When one of you eats, he should not wipe his hand until he licks his fingers or has them licked.

Yazid ibn Harun informed us, Abu al-Yaman al-Bara’, who is Mu’alla ibn Rashid, informed us, he said: My grandmother Umm Asim told me, she said: Nubayshah ( ), the freed slave of the Apostle of Allah ( ), entered upon us while we were eating food, so we invited him, and he ate with us, then he said: The Apostle of Allah ( ), told us that whoever eats from a plate Then he licked it, and the bowl asked forgiveness for him.

Ishaq ibn Isa informed us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas ( ), who said: The Apostle of Allah ( ), said: “If one of you drops a morsel of food, let him wipe the dust off it, say Bismillah, and eat it.”

Zakariya ibn Adi informed us, Yazid ibn Zurai’ narrated to us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: Ma’qil ibn Yasar was eating lunch, and his morsel of food fell, so he picked it up, removed the dirt from it, and then ate it. He said: Those peasants began to wink at him, and they said to him: What do you see of what these foreigners are saying? They say: Look at what is in front of him. From food, and what should he do with this morsel? He said: I would not abandon what I heard from the Apostle of Allah ( ), based on the words of these non-Arabs: “If a morsel of food fell, we were commanded to remove whatever was harmful from it and eat it.”

Abu Ali al-Hanafi informed us, Malik told us, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah Ibn Umar ( ), on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Umar ( ), that the Apostle of Allah ( ), said: “When one of you eats, let him eat with his right hand and drink with his right hand, for Satan eats with his left hand and drinks with his left hand.” On his left. Amr ibn Awn informed us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Ibn Umar ( ), on the authority of the Prophet ( ) in a similar manner.

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi informed us, `Ikrimah ibn `Ammar narrated to us, saying: Iyas ibn Salamah narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: The Apostle of Allah ( ), saw Busr ibn Ra’i al-`Ayr eating with his left hand, so he said: “Eat with your right hand.” He said: “I cannot.” He said: “You cannot.” His right hand did not even reach his mouth.

Muhammad ibn ‘Isa informed us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, on the authority of ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa’d al-Madani, on the authority of Ibn Ka’b ibn Malik, on the authority of his father, who said: The Prophet ( ) “used to eat with three fingers, and he would not wipe his hand until he had licked it.”

Musa ibn Khalid narrated to us, ‘Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, on the authority of Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, on the authority of ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa’d al-Madani, that ‘Abdullah ibn Ka’b, or ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka’b - Hisham was uncertain - informed him, on the authority of his father, that the Prophet ( ) “used to eat with his three fingers, and when he finished, he would lick them.” And Hisham pointed to his three fingers

Yazid ibn Harun informed us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Abi Sa`id, on the authority of Abu Shurayh al-Khuza`i, who said: I heard the Apostle of Allah ( ), say: “Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his neighbor. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent. Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honor his guest. His reward is a day and a night, and hospitality is for three days, and anything after that is charity.

Uthman ibn Muhammad informed us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, who said: I heard Nafi’ ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Abu Shurayh al-Khuza’i, that the Apostle of Allah ( ), said: “Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his guest, and whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him be good to his neighbor.” His neighbor, and whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent.

Yazid ibn Harun informed us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu al-Judi, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Muhajir, on the authority of al-Miqdam ibn Ma’di Karib, Abu Karimah, who said: The Apostle of Allah ( ), said: “If a Muslim hosts a people and the guest wakes up deprived, then it is incumbent upon every Muslim to help him until he takes for him a portion of his crops for the night and his money.

Abdullah ibn Maslama informed us, Sulayman ibn Bilal told us, on the authority of Utbah ibn Muslim, that Ubayd ibn Hunayn informed him that he heard Abu Hurayrah ( ) say: The Apostle of Allah ( ), said: “If a fly falls into the drink of one of you, let him dip it completely in it and then remove it, for in one of its wings is a disease and in the other is a cure.”

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Thamamah ibn Abdullah ibn Anas ( ), on the authority of Abu Hurairah ( ) ( ), on the authority of the Prophet ( ) who said: “If a fly falls into the vessel of one of you, let him dip it in it, for in one of its wings is a disease and in the other is a cure.” Abu Muhammad said: Other than Hammad, it was said: Thamamah, on the authority of Anas ( ), instead of Abu Hurairah ( ). And some people say: on the authority of Al-Qaqa’, on the authority of Abu Hurairah ( ), and the hadith of Ubaid bin Hunayn is more authentic.

Abu Asim informed us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir ( ) on the authority of the Prophet ( ) who said: “The believer eats in one intestine, and the disbeliever eats in seven intestines.” Ubaydullah Ibn Umar ( ) al-Qawariri informed us, Yahya ibn Sa`id informed us, on the authority of Ubaydullah, Nafi` informed me, on the authority of Ibn Umar ( ), on the authority of the Prophet ( ). Yahya informed me, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of Abu al-Wadak, on the authority of Abu Sa`id ( ), on the authority of the Prophet ( ).

Yahya told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah ( ) ( ), on the authority of the Prophet ( ) who said: “The believer eats in one intestine, and the disbeliever eats in seven intestines.”

Abu Asim informed us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir ( ), on the authority of the Prophet ( ) who said: “The food of one person is sufficient for two, the food of two is sufficient for four, and the food of four is sufficient for eight.”

Khalid ibn Makhlad informed us, Malik told us, on the authority of Wahb ibn Kaysan, on the authority of Umar ibn Abi Salamah, that the Prophet ( ) said to him: “Say Bismillah and eat from what is in front of you.”

Sa'id ibn 'Amir informed us, on the authority of Shu'bah, on the authority of 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas ( ) that the Apostle of Allah ( ), was brought a bowl, or he said: a bowl of tharid, and he said: "Eat from its edges" or he said: "its sides, and do not eat from its middle, for blessing descends in its middle."

Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, on the authority of Qurrah ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Asma’ bint Abi Bakr ( ), that whenever tharid was brought to her, she would order it to be covered until its smoke had gone away, and she would say: “I heard the Apostle of Allah ( ), say: ‘It is Greater blessing.

Yazid ibn Harun informed us, Al-Muthanna ibn Sa'id informed us, Talhah ibn Nafi' informed us: Abu Sufyan informed us, Jabir ibn Abdullah ( ) informed us: The Prophet ( ) took me by the hand one day to his house and said: "Is there lunch or dinner?" Talhah was unsure. He said: So, he brought out a piece of bread to him and said: “Is there any condiment?” They said: “No, except some vinegar.” He said: “Bring it, for vinegar is an excellent condiment.” Jabir ( ) said: “I have always loved vinegar since I heard it from the Apostle of Allah ( ).” Abu Sufyan said: “I have always loved it since I heard it from Jabir.”

Yahya ibn Hassan told me, Sulayman ibn Bilal told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ummul Momineen Ummul Momineen Aisha ( ) on the authority of the Prophet ( ) who said: “The best condiment or condiment is vinegar.”

Abu Nu`aym informed us, Malik told us, on the authority of Ishaq ibn `Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, on the authority of Anas ( ), who said: “I saw the Prophet ( ) being brought a broth containing a gourd and dried meat, and I saw him following the gourd around, eating it.”

Al-Aswad ibn Amir informed us, Shu'bah told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas ( ), who said: "The Prophet ( ) liked the game of gourd." He said: It was brought to him, and I began to take it and place it in front of him.

Abu Nu'aym informed us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn 'Isa, on the authority of Ata' - not the son of Abi Rabah - on the authority of Abu Asid al-Ansari, who said: The Apostle of Allah ( ), said: "Eat olive oil, for it is blessed. Use it as a condiment and anoint yourselves with it, for it comes from a blessed tree."

Musaddad narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa`id narrated to us, on the authority of `Ubayd Allah, Nafi` informed me, on the authority of Ibn Umar ( ), that the Prophet ( ) said during the Battle of Khaybar: “Whoever eats from this tree, meaning garlic, should not come to the mosques.”

Ali ibn Abdullah informed us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah informed us, Ubaydullah ibn Abi Yazid informed me, on the authority of his father, that Umm Ayyub informed him, she said: The Apostle of Allah ( ), came to us, so we prepared food for him that contained some of these vegetables. When we brought it to him, he disliked it and said to his companions: “Eat it, for I am not like any of you. I fear that I might harm my companion.” Abu Muhammad said: If it does not harm anyone, then there is nothing wrong with eating it.

Abdullah ibn Sa`id informed us, Ibn `Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ayyub, on the authority of al-Qasim al-Tamimi, on the authority of Zahdam al-Jarmi, who said: We were with Abu Musa ( ) when his food was served, and among his food was chicken meat. Among the people was a man from Banu Taym Allah who was red, but he did not come near. So, Abu Musa ( ) said to him: “Come near, for I have seen the Apostle of Allah ( ), He, peace and blessings be upon him, would eat from it.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ayyub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Zahdam al-Jarmi, on the authority of Abu Musa ( ), that he mentioned chickens and said: I saw the Apostle of Allah ( ) eating them.

Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Muqri’ informed us, Haywah told us, Salim ibn Ghailan told us: Al-Walid ibn Qays informed him that he heard Abu Sa’id, or on the authority of Abu al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri ( ), that he heard the Prophet of Allah ( ), say: “Do not befriend anyone but a believer, and do not let anyone eat your food but a pious person.”

Muhammad ibn Isa informed us, Ibrahim ibn Saad informed us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ja`far, who said: “I saw the Apostle of Allah ( ) eating cucumber with fresh dates.”

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi informed us, Shu'bah told us, Jabalah ibn Suhaim told us, he said: We were in Madinah, and a famine struck us, and Ibn al-Zubayr was provided with dates, and Ibn Umar ( ) used to pass by us and say: Do not combine dates, for the Apostle of Allah ( ) forbade combining dates unless a man asks his brother for permission.

Abdullah ibn Maslama informed us, Yaqub ibn Muhammad ibn Tahlā’ narrated to us, on the authority of Abu al-Rijal, on the authority of his mother, Amrah, on the authority of Ummul Momineen Aisha ( ), the wife of the Prophet ( ) that the Apostle of Allah ( ) said: “O Ummul Momineen Aisha ( ), a house in which there are no dates, its people are hungry or its people are hungry,” two or three times.

Yahya ibn Hassan informed us, Sulayman ibn Bilal told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ummul Momineen Aisha ( ), that the Prophet ( ) said: “A household that has dates will not go hungry.”
Abu Nu`aym narrated to us, Mus`ab ibn Sulaym narrated to us, he said: I heard Anas ( ) say: “Dates were given as a gift to the Prophet ( ) and he began to give them away.”
He said: “I saw the Apostle of Allah ( ) eating dates while squatting due to hunger.” Abu Muhammad said: “He was sending it here and there.”

Amr ibn Awn informed us, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Suhayl, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah ( ), who said: The Apostle of Allah ( ), said: “Whoever sleeps while the scent of ghareem is in his hand and something happens to him, let him blame no one but himself.”

Yazid ibn Harun informed us, Humayd informed us, on the authority of Anas ( ), that the Prophet ( ) said to Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf ( ), and he saw a yellowish tinge on him: “What is wrong with you?” He said: “I got married.” He said: “Give a wedding feast, even if it is with a sheep.”

Affan informed us, Hammam told us, Qatada told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Uthman Al-Thaqafi, on the authority of a one-eyed man from Thaqif, who said: He was called Ma’ruf, meaning he was praised for his good deeds, unless his name was Zuhayr bin Uthman, for I do not know what his name was, that the Prophet ( ) said: “The wedding feast on the first day is a right, and the second…” Qatadah said: A man told me, on the authority of Sa`id ibn al-Musayyib, that he was called on the first day and he responded, and he was called on the second day and he responded, and he was called on the third day and he turned away from the Apostle ( ) and did not respond, and he said: “People of reputation and hypocrisy.”

Abu Al-Mughira informed us, Al-Awza’i told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurairah ( ), that he said: “The worst food is the food of a banquet, to which the rich are invited, and the poor are left out. Whoever does not attend the invitation has disobeyed Allah and His Apostle ( ).”

Sa'id ibn Sulayman informed us, on the authority of Sulayman ibn al-Mughira, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas ( ), who said: A man who had prepared food came to the Apostle of Allah ( ), and said: O Apostle of Allah, like this, and he gestured to him with his hand. He said: The Apostle of Allah ( ), says to him: like this, and he pointed to Ummul Momineen Aisha ( ). He said: No, so he turned away from him. The Apostle of Allah ( ), nodded to him a second time. The Apostle of Allah ( ), nodded to him a third time. The Apostle of Allah ( ), said to him: “And this one?” He said: “Yes.” So, the Apostle of Allah ( ), set out with him. And Ummul Momineen Aisha ( ), and they ate from his food.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-A'mash, on the authority of Abu Wa'il, on the authority of Abu Mas'ud, who said: There was a man called Abu Shu'ayb, and he had a slave butcher. He said: Make me some food so that I may invite the Apostle of Allah ( ), to it, as the fifth of five. He said: The Apostle of Allah ( ), called the fifth of five, and a man followed them. The Apostle of Allah ( ), said: “You have called the fifth of five, and this is a man who has followed me. If you wish, you may give him permission, and if you wish, you may leave him alone.” So he gave him permission.

Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, Khalid narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Tuwalah, Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Ma'mar, on the authority of Anas ( ), who said: The Apostle of Allah ( ), said: "The superiority of Ummul Momineen Aisha ( ) over other women is like the superiority of tharid over all other foods."

Ali ibn al-Madini narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, Abd al-Karim narrated to us: Abu Umayyah said: Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal said: My father married me during the caliphate of Uthman, so he called a group of the Companions of the Apostle of Allah ( ). Among those he called was Safwan ibn Umayyah, who was an elderly man, and he said: The Apostle of Allah ( ), Peace be upon him, he said: “Eat the meat thoroughly, for it is more delicious and more satisfying.”
Abu Nu`aym informed us, Sufyan informed us, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Aqmar, Abu Juhayfah informed me, he said: The Apostle of Allah ( ) said: “I do not eat while reclining.”

Nu`aym ibn Hammad informed us, on the authority of `Abd al-`Aziz ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Suhayl, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah ( ), who said: When the first fruits were brought to the Apostle of Allah ( ), he would say: “O Allah, bless us in our city, in our fruits, in our mudd, and in our sa`, blessing upon blessing.” Then he would give it to the smallest of those present. The boys

Ya`la narrated to us, Ismail bin Abi Khalid narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah ( ), who said: The Apostle of Allah ( ), said: “If the servant of one of you brings food, let him sit down, and if he refuses, let him pass it to him.”

Abu al-Walid narrated to us, Shu`bah narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ziyad, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah ( ) narrating, on the authority of the Prophet ( ) who said: “If one of you is served food by his servant, let him sit with him, or give him a morsel or two, or a meal or two, for he is responsible for its heat and smoke.”

Farwah ibn Abi al-Maghra’ narrated to us, Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ummul Momineen Aisha ( ) who said: “The Apostle of Allah ( ) loved sweets and honey.”

Qubaysah narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Abi al-Huwayrith, on the authority of Ibn Abbas ( ), who said: The Prophet ( ) came out from the toilet and food was presented to him. It was said to him: "Why don't you perform ablution?" He said: "I am praying, so should I perform ablution?" Abu Muhammad said: "It was Sa'id ibn al-Huwayrith." Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, on the authority of 'Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Sa'id ibn al- Huwayrith, on the authority of Ibn Abbas ( ). He said: I heard Abu 'Asim narrating, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of 'Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Sa'id ibn al- Huwayrith, on the authority of Ibn Abbas ( ), with his chain of transmission.

Sahl ibn Hammad narrated to us, Shu’bah narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, who said: I heard Ibrahim narrating, on the authority of Al-Aswad, on the authority of Ummul Momineen Aisha ( ), who said: “Whenever the Apostle of Allah ( ), became junub and wanted to eat or sleep, he would perform ablution.”

Abu Nu`aym informed us, Shu`bah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu `Imran al-Jawni, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn al-Samit, on the authority of Abu Dharr ( ), who said: My friend ( ) advised me, saying: “When you cook a broth, add more water, then look for a household among your neighbors and scoop some of it for them.”

Muhammad ibn Sa`id informed us, `Uqbah ibn Khalid informed us, on the authority of Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, who told me, on the authority of my father, on the authority of Anas ( ) who said: The Apostle of Allah ( ), said: “When the food is served, take off your shoes, for that is more soothing for your feet.”

Ibrahim ibn Musa informed us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: The Apostle of Allah ( ), said: “Worship the Most Merciful, spread peace, and feed the poor, and you will enter Paradise.”

Al-Hakam ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Musa ibn Uqbah, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar ( ), that the Apostle of Allah ( ), said: “Answer the caller when you are invited.” He said: “Abdullah would respond to invitations at weddings and other occasions, and he would come while he was fasting.”

Ali ibn Abdullah informed us, Sufyan told us, Al-Zuhri told us, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas ( ), on the authority of Maymunah, that the Apostle of Allah ( ), was asked about a mouse that fell into ghee, so he said: “Throw it and everything around it, and eat.” Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, with his chain of transmission.

Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us, Malik narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah, from Ibn Abbas ( ), who said: The Prophet ( ), was asked about a mouse that fell into some ghee and died. He said: “Take it and everything around it and throw it away.” Zayd ibn Yahya narrated to us, Malik narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah, from Ibn Abbas ( ), from Maymunah, from the Prophet ( ) something similar. Abu Muhammad said: If it is a wolf, it should be poured out.

Abu Asim informed us, Thawr ibn Yazid informed us, Husayn al-Himyari informed us, Abu Sa’d al-Khayr informed me, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah ( ) who said: The Apostle of Allah ( ), said: “Whoever eats, let him use his toothpicks, and whatever he uses his toothpicks, let him spit it out, and whatever he chews with his tongue, let him swallow.”

Sahl ibn Hammad informed us, Shu'bah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas ( ): A woman vowed to perform Hajj, but she died. Her brother came to the Apostle of Allah ( ) and asked him about that. The Apostle of Allah ( ) said to him, "If she had a debt, would you have paid it?" He said, "Yes." He said: "Then pay Allah, for Allah is more deserving of fulfillment."

Abdullah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Hafs narrated to us, Ubaydullah narrated to us, on the authority of Nafi', on the authority of Ibn Umar ( ) ( ), on the authority of Umar ( ), who said: I said: O Apostle of Allah ( ), I made a vow during the pre-Islamic era, then Islam came? He said: "Then fulfill your vow."

Ja'far ibn 'Awn informed us, Yahya ibn Sa'id told us, on the authority of 'Ubayd Allah ibn Zahr, on the authority of Abu Sa'id al-Ru'ayni, on the authority of 'Abdullah ibn Malik, on the authority of 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir al-Juhani, who said: My sister vowed to perform Hajj for the sake of Allah, walking and not wearing a head covering. I mentioned that to the Apostle of Allah ( ) and he said: "Tell your sister So let her ferment, let her ride, and let her fast for three days.”

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi informed us, Hammam informed us, Qatada informed me, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas ( ): The sister of Uqbah vowed to walk to the House, so the Apostle of Allah ( ) said: “Allah is free from the vow of your sister, so let her ride and offer an offering.”

Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muhammad narrated to us, on the authority of 'Amr ibn Abi 'Amr, on the authority of al-A'raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah ( ): The Apostle of Allah ( ) saw an old man walking between his two sons. He said, "What is the matter with this old man?" His sons said, "He vowed to walk." He said, "Ride, for Allah is independent of you and your vow."

Abu Nu`aym informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Ayyub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Abu al-Muhallab, on the authority of Imran ibn Husayn ( ), who said: The Apostle of Allah ( ) said: “A vow to disobey Allah must not be fulfilled, nor must it be made in something over which the son of Adam has no control.”

Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us, Malik narrated to us, from Talha ibn Abd al-Malik al-Ayli, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aisha ( ), who said: The Apostle of Allah ( ) said: “Whoever vows to obey Allah, let him obey Him, and whoever vows to disobey Allah, let him not disobey Him.”

Hajjaj ibn Minhal narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Baqiyah al-Mu'allim, on the authority of Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah: A man said, "O Apostle of Allah, I vowed that if Allah grants you victory, I will pray in Bayt al-Maqdis." He said, "Pray here." He repeated it to him three times, and the Prophet ( ) said: “Then do as you wish.”

Amr ibn Awn informed us, Abu Awana informed us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Murrah, on the authority of Ibn Umar ( ), who said: The Apostle of Allah said: “A vow does not avert anything, but it is only used to extract something from a miser.”

Al-Hakam ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Malik ibn Anas told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar ( ): The Apostle of Allah ( ) caught up with ‘Umar ( ) ibn al-Khattab while he was traveling in a group, and he was swearing by his father. So, the Apostle of Allah ( ) said: “Allah forbids you to swear by your fathers, so whoever is going to swear, let him swear.” For Allah's sake, or let him keep quiet.

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi informed us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Ayyub, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar ( ), on the authority of the Prophet ( ) who said: “Whoever swears an oath, then says: ‘If Allah wills,’ has made an exception.”

Hajjaj informed us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, Ayyub told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar ( ): The Apostle of Allah ( ) said: “Whoever swears an oath, then says, ‘If Allah wills,’ then he has the choice: if he wishes, he may do so, and if he wishes, he may not do so.”

Abdullah ibn Salih informed us, Al-Layth told me, Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas ( ): The Prophet ( ) said to Abu Bakr: “Do not swear.” Abu Muhammad said: The hadith is long.

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi informed us, Shu`bah narrated to us, on the authority of `Amr, who is Ibn Murrah, who said: I heard a man called `Abdullah Ibn `Amr, the time of the skulls, narrating. He said: A man asked `Adiyy Ibn Hatim, and he swore that he would not give him anything. Then he said: Had I not heard the Apostle of Allah ( ) say: Whoever swears an oath, then sees If he does not offer her something better than it, then let him do what is better, and let him atone for his oath.

Muhammad ibn al-Fadl informed us, Jarir ibn Hazim informed us, al-Hasan informed us, Abd al- Rahman ibn Samurah informed us, he said: The Apostle of Allah ( ) said: “O Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah, do not ask for leadership, for if you are given it after asking for it, you will be left to it, and if you are given it without asking for it, you will be helped in it.” “So if you swear an oath and then see something better than it, then expiate your oath and do that which is better.” Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf told us, Sufyan, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah, who said: The Apostle of Allah ( ) said: … and he mentioned something similar to the hadith.

Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi informed us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of al-Sharid, who said: I came to the Prophet ( ) and said: My mother is owed a slave girl, and I have a black Nubian slave girl with me. Will that suffice on her behalf? He said, "Call upon her." He said, "Do you testify that there is no Allah but Allah?" She said, "Yes." He said, "Free her, for she is a believer."

Uthman ibn Muhammad informed us, Hisham informed us, Abdullah ibn Abi Salih informed us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah ( ), who said: The Apostle of Allah ( ) said: “Your oath is based on that which your companion believes in.”

Ubaydullah ibn Musa informed us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Musa ibn Uqbah, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Ibn Umar ( ), who said: The oath by which the Apostle of Allah ( ) swore was, “No, by the One who turns hearts.”

Abu al-Nu'man informed us, Yazid ibn Zurai' told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri ( ): Abu Musa al-Ash’ari ( ) asked permission to enter upon 'Umar ( ) three times, but he was not given permission, so he returned. He said: “I heard the Apostle of Allah ( ) say: "If the one seeking permission asks permission three times, then if he is given permission, then well and good, otherwise..." So let him return,” he said, “You must bring someone to testify with you, or I will do this and that.” Abu Sa'id said: "He came to us while I was with some of the Companions of the Apostle of Allah ( ) in the mosque, and he was terrified by Umar ( )'s warning to him. He stood over us and said, 'I ask Allah to find a man among you who heard this from the Apostle of Allah ( ) to testify to it for me.' I raised my head and said, 'Tell him that I agree with you on this.’ And others said the same, so Abu Musa was relieved.

Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' informed us, Shu'bah narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al- Munkadir, who said: I heard Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah ( ) say: I came to the Apostle of Allah ( ) and knocked on his door. He said: "Who is it?" I said: "It is me." He said: "It is me? It is me?!" He disliked that.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Sufyan told us, he said: I heard Muharib ibn Dithar mentioning, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah ( ), he said: “The Apostle of Allah ( ) forbade a man from knocking on the door of his family at night, or betraying them, or seeking out their faults.” Sufyan said: His statement: “Or he betrays them, or seeks out their mistakes, I do not know” is something. Muharib said: Or something that is in the hadith.

Sa'id ibn 'Amir informed us, on the authority of 'Awf, on the authority of Zurara ibn Awfa, on the authority of 'Abdullah ibn Salam, who said: When the Apostle of Allah ( ) arrived in Medina, the people were anticipating his arrival and said, "The Apostle of Allah ( ) has arrived." He said, "So I went out with those who went out, and when I saw his face, I knew that his face was not the face of a liar." The first thing I heard him say was: “O people, spread peace, feed the poor, maintain family ties, and pray while people are asleep, and you will enter Paradise in peace.”

Ubaydullah informed us, on the authority of Isra'il, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali ( ), who said: The Apostle of Allah ( ) said: “A Muslim has six obligations towards another Muslim: to greet him when he meets him, to say ‘yarhamukhu (Allah bless you)’ when he sneezes, to visit him when he is sick, to answer his call, to be present when he dies, and to love for him what he loves for himself.” And advises him in secret

Abdullah ibn Yazid informed us, Haywah informed us, Abu Hani’ al-Khawlani informed us: Abu Ali ( ) al-Junbi informed him, on the authority of Fadalah ibn Ubayd, on the authority of the Apostle of Allah ( ) who said: “The one riding greets the one walking, the one standing greets the one sitting, and the few greet the many.”
